fields.title: The Psalms
fields.subtitle: Tehillim, “Praises”
fields.description: The prayer book and songbook of Israel and the church: a hundred and fifty psalms, gathered over a thousand years into five books, that begin with “How blessed is the one” and end with “Let every creature that breathes praise the LORD!” The shepherd psalm and the cry “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”; David’s confession after Bathsheba and Moses’ prayer for every generation; the songs of ascents sung by pilgrims on the road to Jerusalem; laments that turn to trust, and the psalms Jesus prayed on the cross. Set out line by line as the poetry it is, in the Open Word Bible, a new translation from the Hebrew given freely to the public domain, with an introduction to the book’s shape and meaning and a conclusion on where to read next.

qa.question: What are the Psalms?
qa.answer: The Psalms are a collection of a hundred and fifty prayers and songs in the Old Testament, the prayer book and hymnbook of ancient Israel, and of the church ever since. Their Hebrew name, Tehillim, means “Praises”, though more of them are laments than anything else. They were written over many centuries, from the time of Moses and David to the return from exile in Babylon, and were gathered into five books, each ending with a blessing of God. No Old Testament book is quoted more often in the New Testament.

qa.question: Who wrote the Psalms?
qa.answer: Many hands. By the titles printed above them, David is linked with seventy-three psalms; Asaph, one of the Levite musicians David appointed, with twelve; the sons of Korah, a family of temple singers, with eleven; Solomon with two; and Moses, Heman and Ethan with one each. About a third have no name at all. The titles are very old, already part of the Hebrew text and translated in the Greek Septuagint before the time of Christ, but most scholars think they were added by the editors who gathered the collections, and the Hebrew “of David” can mean by, for or belonging to David’s collection. Jesus quotes Psalm 110 as David’s words.

qa.question: Why are the Psalms divided into five books?
qa.answer: The final editors arranged the Psalms into five books (Psalms 1–41, 42–72, 73–89, 90–106 and 107–150), each closing with a short doxology, a blessing of God, and the last ending with five psalms of praise. Ancient Jewish teachers saw the five books as Israel’s answer to the five books of Moses. The arrangement also tells a story: Book III ends in grief over the fallen line of David, Book IV answers with Moses’ prayer and the cry “The LORD is King!”, and the whole collection climbs toward praise.

qa.question: What kinds of psalms are there?
qa.answer: The main kinds are psalms of praise, which call people to worship God and give the reason; laments, by one person or the whole people, which pour out a trouble and usually turn to trust; thanksgivings for prayer answered; royal psalms about the king in David’s line, and psalms that celebrate the LORD as King; wisdom psalms on the two paths and God’s law; quiet psalms of trust such as Psalm 23; and the seven penitential psalms of confession (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130 and 143). The imprecatory psalms, which call down judgment on enemies, are the hardest for Christians; the church has read them as honest cries that hand vengeance to God, as a refusal to make light of evil, and as prayers against sin and the devil rather than curses on a neighbour.

qa.question: How do Jesus and the New Testament use the Psalms?
qa.answer: Jesus grew up singing the Psalms and quoted them often. On the cross he prayed the first line of Psalm 22, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”, and, in Luke, Psalm 31:5, committing his spirit into his Father’s hands. He asked how David could call the Messiah “my lord” in Psalm 110, the Old Testament passage the New Testament quotes most. The apostles preached Psalm 2 and Psalm 110 of his kingship, Psalm 16 of his resurrection and Psalm 118 of the rejected stone made the cornerstone, and told the churches to sing psalms together.

qa.question: Which translation of the Bible is this?
qa.answer: The Open Word Bible, a new translation made directly from the Hebrew and dedicated to the public domain, printed here at its Balanced level, which aims to be accurate and to read naturally aloud. Each line of the poetry is set on its own, and “LORD” in capitals stands for God’s personal name. The reasoning behind each of its sentences, with the Hebrew beside it, is published at openwordbible.org. The introduction and conclusion were written for this edition.

fields.title: Introduction
fields.body_html:
Yet you are holy; Israel’s praises are the throne where you sit.

— Psalm 22:3

Most of the Bible is God speaking to his people. The Psalms are his people speaking back: a hundred and fifty prayers and songs, written over something like a thousand years, in which shepherds and kings, temple singers and exiles, the guilty and the falsely accused all turn and say something to God. They shout, they weep, they argue, they confess, they remember, they give thanks. And the church, receiving them from Israel, has found nothing better than to say the same words after them.

No book of the Old Testament is quoted more often in the New, and none has been sung, prayed or memorised more. Monks have recited the whole of it every week for fifteen centuries; the dying have asked for the twenty-third Psalm when they could ask for nothing else. It is the book people turn to when they do not know what to say, and they find that someone has already said it.

“Praises”

The Hebrew name of the book is Tehillim, “Praises”. Our word “psalm” comes from Greek, where it meant a song sung to a stringed instrument, and the collection is often called the Psalter.

The Hebrew name is a surprise to anyone who reads the book through, because the largest single group of psalms is not praise at all. It is lament: complaint, protest, grief, the cry of someone in trouble asking how long God will wait. More than a third of the Psalms are of this kind. A note at the end of Psalm 72 calls the collection so far by a different name, “the prayers of David”.

Yet the name is not a mistake. In the Psalms, even the bitterest complaint is spoken to God, and that is already a kind of praise: it treats him as the one who hears, who is able to act and who will be held to his word. The verse at the head of this introduction comes from the psalm that begins “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”, and in the same breath it calls Israel’s praises the throne where God sits. Lament and praise belong to one conversation. The book’s name tells you where that conversation is going.

Five books and their doxologies

The Psalms were gathered over centuries from smaller collections, and the final editors arranged them into five books, each closing with a short blessing of God, a doxology:

  • Book I (Psalms 1–41), almost all headed “of David”, ending with a blessing of the God of Israel “from ages past to ages to come” (41:13).
  • Book II (Psalms 42–72), opening with the sons of Korah and ending with a psalm for the king, a doxology and a note: “Here end the prayers of David son of Jesse” (72:20).
  • Book III (Psalms 73–89), largely the psalms of Asaph and Korah, ending with Psalm 89’s anguish over the fallen line of David and a two-line blessing (89:52).
  • Book IV (Psalms 90–106), opening with the only psalm headed with the name of Moses and gathering the psalms that cry, “The LORD is King!”, and ending with a blessing to which all the people answer “Amen!” (106:48).
  • Book V (Psalms 107–150), the longest, holding the psalms of ascents and Psalm 119, and ending not with a single doxology but with five psalms of praise in a row, Psalm 150 the last of them.

The first of these doxologies sets the pattern:

May the LORD, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come! Amen and amen.

— Psalm 41:13

Ancient Jewish teachers saw the five books as Israel’s answer to the five books of Moses. Whatever the editors intended, the shape tells a story. Book III ends with the throne of David in ruins and the question of whether God has forgotten his promises. Book IV answers by going back behind David to Moses, and behind the kingdom to God himself: “Lord, you have been our home through every generation.” Human kings fail; the LORD is King. And the whole Psalter climbs, through grief and confession and long waiting, toward its last word, which is praise.

The gateway: Psalms 1 and 2

The first two psalms have no titles. They stand at the door of the book like two pillars, and most readers in the ancient church and synagogue read them as an introduction to the whole. The first is about a person:

How blessed is the one who does not walk by the advice of the wicked, or stand on the path that sinners tread, or sit where mockers gather! Instead, the instruction of the LORD is their delight, and they recite it quietly to themselves day and night.

— Psalm 1:1–2

The word translated “instruction” is torah, the same word as for the Law. Psalm 1 tells you how to read what follows: slowly, often, aloud, as something to be taken in and lived by. And it sets two paths before you, the path of the righteous that the LORD knows and cares for, and the path of the wicked that ends in ruin. Much of the Psalter is the cry of people on the first path who find it harder than Psalm 1 made it sound.

The second psalm is about a king. The nations plot “against the LORD and against his anointed king”, and God speaks a decree to his king: “You are my son. This is the day I have become your father.” Psalm 1 begins with “How blessed”; Psalm 2 ends with it: “How blessed are all who make him their refuge!” Between those two blessings stand the two great themes of the book, the one who delights in God’s word and the king God has chosen. The New Testament will find both fulfilled in one person.

Kinds of psalm

The Psalms are not all alike, and it helps to know what kind you are reading. The main families are easy to recognise:

  • Praise, or hymns, which call people to praise God and give the reason: his greatness in creation (8, 19, 104), his faithfulness to Israel (105, 136), or simply who he is (100, 145–150).
  • Lament, by one person (3, 13, 22, 42) or the whole people (44, 74, 79, 80), which pour out a trouble, plead with God and usually end in trust.
  • Thanksgiving, which tell what God has done in answer to a lament: “I waited and kept on waiting for the LORD” (40, 30, 34, 116, 118).
  • Royal psalms, about the king in David’s line, his coronation, battles and wedding (2, 18, 20, 21, 45, 72, 110), and the psalms that celebrate the LORD himself as King (93, 95–99).
  • Wisdom and the law, which reflect on the two paths and the puzzle of the wicked prospering (1, 37, 49, 73), and delight in God’s word (19, 119).
  • Psalms of trust, quiet and confident (23, 62, 121, 131).
  • The penitential psalms, seven psalms of confession the church has long grouped together (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143).

One more family needs a word of its own. The imprecatory psalms (among them 35, 58, 69, 109 and 137) call down judgment on enemies, sometimes in words that shock a Christian reader. Psalm 137, which begins so tenderly by the rivers of Babylon, ends by blessing whoever smashes Babylon’s children on the rock.

Christians have read these psalms in several ways, often together. They are the honest cry of people who had suffered terrible wrongs, handing vengeance over to God instead of taking it themselves, and refusing to pretend that cruelty does not matter. Many in the church have prayed them against sin, death and the devil rather than against people. A Christian, taught by Jesus to love enemies, may not pray them as a curse on a neighbour. But neither should they be cut out: they teach us that God hears even our rage, and that justice is his.

Hebrew poetry

Hebrew poetry does not rhyme, and its rhythm is hard to carry into English. What does carry is its most distinctive feature, parallelism: a thought is said once, and then said again in a second line that echoes, sharpens, extends or contrasts with the first.

The heavens tell over and over how glorious God is; the vault of the sky makes known what his hands have made.

— Psalm 19:1

The second line does not simply repeat the first; it looks at the same thing from a little further along. Sometimes the second line is the opposite of the first, as at the end of Psalm 1: the LORD knows the path of the righteous, “but the path of the wicked ends in ruin.” Sometimes a third line climbs higher still. Once you hear this pattern, you will hear it everywhere.

Some psalms are acrostics, each line or stanza beginning with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet (25, 34, 111, 145). Psalm 119, the longest chapter in the Bible, gives each of the twenty-two letters a stanza of eight verses: an alphabet of devotion to God’s word.

Because the Psalms are poetry, this edition prints each line on its own, as the Hebrew sets it out, rather than running the lines together as prose. There are no verse numbers, so that you can read a psalm as a song and not as a list. The small word Selah, which appears seventy-one times, is printed where it stands. Its meaning is uncertain; it was probably a musical direction.

The titles

Above most psalms stands a short heading: “For the music director. A psalm of David.” Some name an author, some a tune or instrument (“On the gittith”), some a kind of song (“A maskil”), and about a dozen the moment in David’s life that the psalm belongs to: “A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.” In this edition these titles are printed in italics at the head of the psalm.

By the titles, David is linked with seventy-three psalms; Asaph, one of the Levite musicians David appointed, with twelve; the sons of Korah, a family of temple singers, with eleven; Solomon with two; Moses, Heman and Ethan with one each. About a third have no name at all.

The titles are very old. They are part of the Hebrew text, they were already translated in the Greek Septuagint more than a century before Christ, and they appear in the Psalms scrolls found near the Dead Sea. Most scholars think they were added by the editors who gathered the collections rather than written by the poets themselves, and the little Hebrew word translated “of David” can mean “by David”, “for David”, or “belonging to the Davidic collection”. Even so, the tradition behind them is ancient and weighty, and Jesus himself quotes Psalm 110 as words David spoke by the Holy Spirit. The titles are worth reading: they set a psalm in a real life.

The Hebrew counts a title as verse 1 (or 1 and 2), so its verse numbers often run ahead of English Bibles. This edition prints no verse numbers, and the references in it follow the English numbering.

Lament that turns to trust

Psalm 13 is only six verses long, and it shows in miniature the shape of a great many psalms. It begins in the dark:

How long, LORD? Will you go on forgetting me for good? How long will you turn your face away from me?

— Psalm 13:1

Four times the psalmist asks “How long?” Then he pleads: “Turn and look, LORD my God, and answer me!” And then, with nothing in his circumstances changed, the psalm turns:

But I trust in your loyal love; my heart will be glad because you save. I will sing to the LORD, because he has been so generous to me.

— Psalm 13:5–6

That turn happens again and again in the Psalms, often on a few words: “But you, LORD” or “Yet you”. It is not a pretence that all is well, but a decision to remember who God is while the trouble is still there. The psalms of lament give us permission to bring God our worst, and then they teach us where to look.

Not every lament makes the turn. Psalm 88 ends in darkness, its last line “my one companion is the dark.” It is a gift that the Bible contains such a psalm: no one is too low to pray, and even this prayer is addressed to “God who saves me”.

The songs of ascents

Fifteen psalms in a row (120–134) are headed “A song of ascents”. They were most likely sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem, which stands high in the hills, for the great festivals. They move like a journey: from a cry of trouble far from home (120), to a look toward the mountains and the question where help will come from (121), to joy at the gates of the city (122), to the house of the LORD and the blessing of those who serve in it at night (134). Along the way come some of the best-loved psalms of all: tears sown and sheaves brought home (126), a cry “from the deep waters” (130), a soul as calm as a weaned child (131), and the goodness of brothers and sisters living in harmony (133).

The Psalms in the life of Jesus

Jesus grew up with the Psalms, singing them in the synagogue and on the road to the festivals; after the last supper, the Gospels say, he and his disciples sang a hymn before going out to the Mount of Olives, most likely the psalms of praise sung at Passover (113–118). After his resurrection he told his disciples that everything written about him in the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms had to be fulfilled.

On the cross he prayed the Psalms. Mark records that he cried out in his own Aramaic, and Matthew records it too, the first line of Psalm 22:

My God, my God, why have you abandoned me? I roar out my words, and still rescue is far away.

— Psalm 22:1

Psalm 22 goes on to describe a man mocked by onlookers who shake their heads, his hands and feet attacked, his clothes shared out by lot, and the Gospels echo it all through the crucifixion. But the psalm does not end in abandonment: its second half breaks out into praise in the great assembly and the promise that the farthest ends of the earth will turn to the LORD.

Luke records Jesus’s last words as another line from the Psalms, a prayer of trust that has long been part of Jewish prayer at nightfall:

I put my spirit into your hand for safekeeping; you have redeemed me, LORD, God who is faithful.

— Psalm 31:5

The rest of the New Testament reads the Psalms in the same light. The voice from heaven at Jesus’s baptism echoes Psalm 2: “You are my son.” Jesus asks how David can call the Messiah his lord in Psalm 110 (“The LORD declares to my lord: ‘Take your seat at my right hand’”), the Old Testament verse the New quotes most often. Psalm 118’s stone that the builders cast aside, now “the stone at the head of the corner”, becomes the apostles’ picture of the rejected and risen Christ. Peter at Pentecost preaches Psalm 16, “nor allow your loyal one to see the pit”, as a promise of resurrection. The early church heard Christ in the Psalms in two ways at once: as the one they speak about, and as the one who prays them with his people.

How to pray the Psalms

The Psalms are best understood by praying them. Athanasius, in the fourth century, said that most of Scripture speaks to us, while the Psalms are like a mirror in which we see ourselves. Martin Luther called the book a little Bible. John Calvin called it “an anatomy of all the parts of the soul”, because there is no feeling a person can have that is not pictured somewhere in it.

A few ways in:

  • Read them aloud. They were made for the voice.
  • Read them through. An old custom reads five psalms a day, taking the day of the month and adding thirty each time (on the 3rd, Psalms 3, 33, 63, 93 and 123), to finish the book in a month.
  • Pray the psalm that does not fit your mood. On a happy day, a lament teaches you to pray for those who suffer; on a hard day, a psalm of praise reminds you of what is still true.
  • Let a psalm say what you cannot. When there are no words of your own, Psalm 51 can confess for you, Psalm 23 can trust for you, and Psalm 88 can sit with you in the dark.

I am quiet before God alone; my rescue comes from him.

— Psalm 62:1

About this translation

The text in this edition is the Open Word Bible, a new translation made directly from the Hebrew and given freely to the public domain. It is printed here at its Balanced level, which aims to be accurate and to read naturally aloud. A few of its choices in the Psalms are worth knowing before you begin.

“The LORD.” When you see LORD in capital letters, it stands for God’s personal name, the four Hebrew letters YHWH, probably pronounced Yahweh, which Jewish readers out of reverence did not say aloud. Following a very old custom, this translation, like most English Bibles, prints it as “the LORD”. Where the Hebrew has the ordinary word for “master”, it reads “Lord” in small letters, and where the two come together, “Lord GOD”. So Psalm 8 begins, “LORD, our Lord, how glorious is your name across the whole earth!”

“Loyal love.” The Hebrew word hesed, which older Bibles render “mercy”, “loving-kindness” or “steadfast love”, means the faithful love that keeps a promise and will not let go. This translation calls it “loyal love”, and you will meet it on almost every page: “his loyal love lasts forever.”

“How blessed.” The first word of the Psalter, and a favourite of the psalmists, is an exclamation, not a statement: “How blessed is the one…” It is printed that way throughout.

For the reasoning behind every sentence of the translation, with the Hebrew beside it, see the Open Word Bible itself at openwordbible.org.

May what my mouth speaks and what my heart ponders be welcome before you, LORD, my rock and my redeemer.

— Psalm 19:14

fields.title: Psalm 1
fields.body_html:
The two ways

1How blessed is the one who does not walk by the advice of the wicked,
or stand on the path that sinners tread,
or sit where mockers gather!
2Instead, the instruction of the LORD is their delight,
and they recite it quietly to themselves day and night.
3That person is like a tree set out beside channels of water,
which bears its fruit when its season comes,
and whose leaves never dry up.
Whatever they do turns out well.
4The wicked are nothing like that.
They are like chaff, scattered by the wind.
5That is why the wicked will not stand firm when judgment comes,
and sinners will have no place in the gathering of the righteous.
6For the LORD knows the path of the righteous and cares for it,
but the path of the wicked ends in ruin.
fields.summary: The one who delights in God’s instruction is like a tree planted by streams of water, while the wicked are like chaff that the wind blows away.

fields.title: Psalm 2
fields.body_html:
The king the LORD has anointed

1Why are the nations in an uproar,
and the peoples muttering empty schemes?
2The kings of the earth take up their positions,
and the rulers plot together
against the LORD and against his anointed king.
3“Let us snap their chains,” they say,
“and fling their ropes off us.”
4The one seated on the throne in the heavens laughs;
the Lord ridicules them.
5Then he speaks to them in anger
and fills them with terror in his blazing rage.
6“I am the one who has set my king in place
on Zion, my holy mountain.”
7I will announce the decree.
The LORD said to me, “You are my son.
This is the day I have become your father.
8Ask me, and I will give you the nations to inherit,
and the farthest places of the earth to hold as your own.
9You will crush them with an iron scepter
and smash them to pieces like a clay pot.”
10So then, you kings, show good sense!
Accept correction, you who rule the earth.
11Serve the LORD with awe,
and let your joy be mixed with trembling.
12Kiss the son, or he will be angry and you will come to ruin on your path,
for his anger can blaze up in an instant.
How blessed are all who make him their refuge!
fields.summary: The nations plot against God and the anointed king, but God laughs at them and declares the king to be God’s son, set on Zion; the rulers are warned to serve God.

fields.title: Psalm 3
fields.body_html:
A shield all around me

A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.

1LORD, how my enemies have multiplied!
Many are rising up against me.
2Many are saying about me,
“God is not going to rescue him.” Selah
3But you, LORD, are a shield on every side of me.
You are my glory, and you lift my head up again.
4I lift my voice and call to the LORD,
and from his holy mountain he answers me. Selah
5I lay down and fell asleep,
and I woke up again,
because the LORD holds me up.
6I have no fear of the tens of thousands
who have taken up positions against me on every side.
7Rise up, LORD! Rescue me, my God!
For you have struck all my enemies across the jaw
and smashed the teeth of the wicked.
8It is the LORD who saves.
Let your blessing rest on your people. Selah
fields.summary: David, fleeing from Absalom, cries out that his enemies are many, yet he lies down and sleeps, for God is his shield and rescue.

fields.title: Psalm 4
fields.body_html:
Lying down in peace

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David.

1When I call, answer me, God who stands up for my right! When I was hemmed in, you gave me room. Show me grace now and listen to my prayer.
2You people, how long will my honor be dragged into disgrace? How long will you love empty things and go looking for lies? Selah
3Be sure of this: the LORD has set apart the one who is faithful to him as his own. The LORD will hear me when I call to him.
4Tremble, and do not sin. Lying on your bed, reason it out in your own heart, and be still. Selah
5Bring sacrifices as they should be brought, and rely on the LORD.
6Many are saying, “Who will let us see good times?” LORD, turn your shining face toward us.
7The joy you have put in my heart is greater than theirs at harvest, when grain and new wine overflow.
8I will lie down in peace and fall asleep at once, because it is you, LORD, and you alone, who let me live in safety.
fields.summary: David calls on God to answer him and tells others to trust God; God has given him more joy than a rich harvest, and he sleeps in peace.

fields.title: Psalm 5
fields.body_html:
A prayer at daybreak

For the music director. For flutes. A psalm of David.

1LORD, hear what I say; take note of my sighs.
2Listen to me crying for help, my King and my God, because it is to you that I pray.
3LORD, at daybreak you hear my voice. At daybreak I set everything out before you and keep watch.
4For you are not a God who takes pleasure in wickedness; evil cannot be your guest.
5Those who boast cannot stand in your sight; you hate all who practice evil.
6You bring liars to ruin. The LORD loathes those who shed blood and deceive.
7But I, because your loyal love is so great, will come into your house; in awe of you I will bow down toward your holy temple.
8LORD, guide me in your righteousness, because my enemies are watching; level your road in front of me.
9Not one thing they say is reliable; deep inside them is only ruin. Their throats are graves left open, and their tongues are smooth with flattery.
10Hold them to account, God! Let them be tripped up by their own schemes. Thrust them away for all their many crimes, since it is against you that they have rebelled.
11But let everyone who makes you their refuge be glad and sing for joy forever. Keep them under your cover, and those who love your name will find their joy in you.
12For you bless the righteous, LORD; your favor surrounds them like a great shield.
fields.summary: David prays in the morning for God to hear him and lead him in righteousness, for God hates evil, and he asks God to protect those who take refuge in God.

fields.title: Psalm 6
fields.body_html:
A prayer from a bed of tears

For the music director. With stringed instruments, on the sheminith. A psalm of David.

1LORD, when you correct me, do not do it in anger; when you discipline me, do not do it in your fury.
2Show me grace, LORD, for I am wasting away; heal me, LORD, for my very bones are shaking.
3My soul is shaken to its depths. But you, LORD, how long?
4Turn back to me, LORD, and set my life free; save me because your love is loyal.
5For in death no one calls you to mind. Who gives you thanks down in Sheol?
6I am exhausted from groaning. Night after night my bed swims with my tears, and my couch dissolves in them.
7Grief has dimmed my eyes; they have aged because of all who oppose me.
8Get away from me, all who practice evil, for the LORD has heard me weeping.
9The LORD has heard me beg for his grace; the LORD welcomes my prayer.
10All my enemies will be put to shame and filled with terror; they will turn back, suddenly disgraced.
fields.summary: In distress and illness David begs God not to correct him in anger; worn out with weeping, he is sure that God has heard his cry.

fields.title: Psalm 7
fields.body_html:
A plea to the righteous judge

A shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD about Cush, a man of the tribe of Benjamin.

1LORD my God, I have made you my refuge. Save me from all who are hunting me down, and rescue me,
2or he will tear me apart like a lion, dragging me off with no one to rescue me.
3LORD my God, if I have done what they say, if my hands are guilty of wrong,
4if I have paid back a friend with harm, or robbed my enemy for no reason,
5then let my enemy chase me down and catch me; let him trample my life into the ground and leave my honor lying in the dust. Selah
6Rise up, LORD, in your anger! Stand up against the rage of my enemies. Wake up and act for me; you have ordered justice to be done.
7Let the peoples gather around you, and take your seat again above them on high.
8The LORD judges the peoples. Give me justice, LORD, because I am in the right and have done no wrong.
9Bring the evil of the wicked to an end, and make the righteous secure, for you are the righteous God who tests minds and hearts.
10My shield is God, who rescues those whose hearts are right.
11God is a righteous judge, a God who is angry at evil every day.
12If anyone will not turn back, God will sharpen his sword; he has strung his bow and taken aim.
13He has made ready deadly weapons for that person, and he turns his arrows into fire.
14See how the wicked person is pregnant with evil: having conceived trouble, he gives birth to lies.
15He dug a pit and scooped it out deep, and fell into the very hole he made.
16The trouble he caused comes back on his own head; his violence falls on his own skull.
17I will thank the LORD because he does what is right, and I will sing praises to the name of the LORD Most High.
fields.summary: David takes refuge in God against those who pursue him and asks God, the righteous judge, to vindicate him.

fields.title: Psalm 8
fields.body_html:
Your name across the whole earth

For the music director. On the gittith. A psalm of David.

1LORD, our Lord, how glorious is your name across the whole earth! Your splendor reaches higher than the heavens.
2Out of the mouths of children and babies at the breast you have built a stronghold against your foes, to silence the enemy and the one bent on revenge.
3When I look up at your heavens, which your fingers made, at the moon and stars you have fixed in their places,
4what are human beings, that you keep them in mind, mere mortals, that you look after them?
5You made them only a little less than God and set a crown of glory and honor on them.
6You made them rulers over all that your hands have made; you put everything under their feet:
7sheep and cattle, all of them, and the wild animals too,
8the birds of the air and the fish of the sea, and everything that travels the paths of the seas.
9LORD, our Lord, how glorious is your name across the whole earth!
fields.summary: God’s name is glorious in all the earth; when David looks at the heavens he wonders that God cares for human beings and has crowned them with glory over all creation.

fields.title: Psalm 9
fields.body_html:
Thanks to the judge of the world

For the music director. On Muth-labben. A psalm of David.

1I will thank the LORD with my whole heart; I will tell of all the wonderful things you have done.
2I will be glad and celebrate because of you; I will sing praises to your name, Most High.
3When my enemies turn and retreat, they stumble and are destroyed in your presence.
4For you have taken up my case and given me justice; you sat on your throne as a judge who does what is right.
5You have rebuked the nations and brought the wicked to ruin; you have wiped their name away for all time.
6The enemy is finished, left in ruins forever; you have torn up their cities by the roots, and no one remembers them now.
7But the LORD remains on his throne forever; it is a throne he has set up to judge from.
8He will judge the world rightly and govern the peoples with fairness.
9The LORD is a fortress on the heights for those who are crushed, a safe height in times of trouble.
10Those who know your name will rely on you, because you do not desert anyone who comes looking for you, LORD.
11Make music to the LORD, whose throne is in Zion! Announce his deeds among the peoples.
12For the God who calls murderers to account remembers the victims; he has not overlooked the cry of those who suffer.
13Show me grace, LORD! See how my enemies make me suffer, you who lift me up from the gates of death,
14so that in the gates of the city of Zion I may tell all the reasons you are praised, and be glad that you saved me.
15The nations have sunk down into the very pit they dug; the net they hid has snared their own feet.
16The LORD has made himself known by doing justice: he snares the wicked in the work of their own hands. Higgaion. Selah
17The wicked will go back down to Sheol, every nation that forgets God.
18For the needy will not always be forgotten, nor will the hope of the poor be lost forever.
19Rise up, LORD! Do not let mere humans win. Bring the nations to judgment before you.
20Fill them with fear, LORD, and let the nations find out they are nothing but human. Selah
fields.summary: David thanks God for judging the nations with justice and for being a stronghold for the oppressed, who are not forgotten.

fields.title: Psalm 10
fields.body_html:
Why do you keep so far away?

1LORD, why do you keep so far away? Why do you hide yourself when trouble comes?
2In their arrogance the wicked hunt down the poor. Let them be trapped in the very schemes they have dreamed up!
3The wicked brag about what they crave; the greedy bless themselves while they treat the LORD with contempt.
4With their noses in the air, the wicked never seek God. All their scheming says, “There is no God.”
5Their ways always seem to succeed; your judgments are high above them, out of their sight; they sneer at all their enemies.
6“Nothing can shake me,” they tell themselves; “I will never come to harm, now or ever.”
7Their mouths are full of curses, lies and threats; they keep mischief and wrongdoing ready under the tongue.
8They lie in wait near the villages and murder the innocent from hiding; their eyes are on the lookout for the helpless.
9They crouch in hiding like a lion in its thicket, waiting to grab the poor; they grab them and haul them away in their nets.
10The weak are crushed and bowed down; the helpless fall into their strong grip.
11They tell themselves, “God has forgotten; he has turned his face away and will never see.”
12Rise up, LORD! God, raise your hand! Do not forget those who suffer.
13Why do the wicked treat God with contempt and tell themselves, “You will not call us to account”?
14But you do see! You take note of trouble and grief and take the matter into your own hands. The helpless entrust themselves to you; you have always helped the orphan.
15Break the power of the wicked and the evildoer; hunt down their wickedness until there is none left to find.
16The LORD reigns as King for all time; the nations are gone from his land.
17LORD, you have heard what the humble long for; you steady their hearts and bend down to listen,
18to give justice to the orphan and the oppressed, so that mere mortals made of earth will strike terror no more.
fields.summary: The psalmist asks why God seems far away while the wicked hunt down the poor, and calls on God to rise up, for God hears the afflicted and defends the fatherless.

fields.title: Psalm 11
fields.body_html:
Refuge when the foundations give way

For the music director. Of David.

1I have taken refuge in the LORD. How can you say to me, “Escape to the hills like a bird!
2Look, the wicked have their bows bent and their arrows set on the string, ready to shoot under cover of darkness at those whose hearts are right.
3If the very pillars that hold things up are pulled down, what can the righteous accomplish?”
4The LORD is in his holy temple; the throne of the LORD is in heaven. His eyes watch; his gaze examines every human being.
5The LORD tests the righteous, but he hates with all his being the wicked and those who love violence.
6On the wicked he will rain down snares; fire, burning sulfur and a scorching wind will be the cup they are given.
7For the LORD is righteous and loves what is right; those who are upright will look on his face.
fields.summary: When advised to flee like a bird, David declares that he takes refuge in God, who sees from heaven and loves justice.

fields.title: Psalm 12
fields.body_html:
Pure words in a time of lies

For the music director. On the sheminith. A psalm of David.

1Save us, LORD! The faithful are no more; no one you can trust is left among humankind.
2People tell each other lies; their lips are smooth with flattery, their hearts are divided.
3May the LORD cut off every flattering lip and every tongue that boasts so loudly,
4those who say, “Our tongues will win the day; our lips are our own. Who can be master over us?”
5“The poor are being robbed and the needy are groaning, so now I will get up,” says the LORD. “I will bring them to the safety they long for.”
6The words of the LORD are pure words, like silver refined in a clay furnace, purified seven times over.
7You, LORD, will watch over them; you will protect each of them from this generation forever.
8On every side the wicked prowl, while what is vile is prized among people.
fields.summary: When the faithful have vanished and everyone speaks lies, God promises to rise up for the poor, and God’s words are pure as refined silver.

fields.title: Psalm 13
fields.body_html:
How long, LORD?

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1How long, LORD? Will you go on forgetting me for good? How long will you turn your face away from me?
2How long must I keep turning plans over in my mind, with grief in my heart all day long? How long will my enemy stand over me in triumph?
3Turn and look, LORD my God, and answer me! Bring the light back to my eyes, or I will fall asleep in death,
4and my enemy will say, “I have beaten him,” and those against me will celebrate when I stumble.
5–6But I trust in your loyal love; my heart will be glad because you save. I will sing to the LORD, because he has been so generous to me.
fields.summary: David asks how long God will forget him, then trusts in God’s loyal love and sings of God’s goodness.

fields.title: Psalm 14
fields.body_html:
No one who does good

For the music director. Of David.

1Fools tell themselves, “There is no God.” They are rotten through and through; what they do is detestable. Not one of them does good.
2From heaven the LORD looks down on the human race to see whether anyone is wise, anyone who is looking for God.
3Everyone has left the road; all alike have gone bad. No one does good, not a single one.
4Have they learned nothing, all these evildoers? They devour my people as if they were eating bread, and they never call on the LORD.
5There they will be gripped by terror, because God is with the people who are righteous.
6You evildoers would make the hopes of the poor come to nothing, but the LORD is their shelter.
7If only Zion would send Israel its rescue! When the LORD turns back the fortunes of his people, let Jacob shout for joy and Israel be glad.
fields.summary: Fools say there is no God, and no one does good, yet God is with the righteous and will restore the fortunes of God’s people.

fields.title: Psalm 15
fields.body_html:
Who may stay in God’s tent?

A psalm of David.

1LORD, who may stay as a guest in your tent? Who may make a home on your holy mountain?
2Whoever walks without blame, practices what is right, and speaks truth that comes from the heart,
3who does not go around spreading slander, does no harm to a neighbor, and does not heap insults on those close by,
4who looks with contempt on one who is rejected but shows honor to all who fear the LORD, and who stands by a sworn promise at personal cost, never going back on it.
5who does not lend money to make a profit from interest, and will not take a bribe to harm the innocent. Anyone who lives like this will stand firm forever.
fields.summary: David asks who may dwell on God’s holy mountain: the one who walks without blame, speaks truth and keeps his word.

fields.title: Psalm 16
fields.body_html:
My share is the LORD

A miktam of David.

1Guard me, God, for I have made you my refuge.
2My soul, you have told the LORD, “You are my Lord; my good is found in you alone.”
3The holy people who live in the land are the truly great; they are my whole delight.
4Those who court another god will have sorrow upon sorrow. I will not pour out their offerings of blood, or even speak the names of their gods.
5The LORD is the share I have been given and the cup I drink; it is you who hold my lot secure.
6The measuring lines have marked out a lovely place for me; truly, the land I inherit delights me.
7I bless the LORD, my adviser; even at night my deepest self keeps teaching me.
8I have placed the LORD in front of me at all times; since he is there at my right hand, I will never stumble.
9That is why my heart is glad and my spirit celebrates; my body too will live in safety.
10For you will not give me up to Sheol, nor allow your loyal one to see the pit.
11You teach me the road that leads to life; in your presence there is joy in full, and at your right hand delights that never end.
fields.summary: David has made God his refuge and his portion; he will not be abandoned to the grave but shown the path of life and fullness of joy.

fields.title: Psalm 17
fields.body_html:
Hide me in the shadow of your wings

A prayer of David.

1Hear a just cause, LORD; listen closely to my cry. Turn your ear to my prayer, which comes from lips that do not lie.
2Let my verdict come from you; let your eyes see what is fair.
3You have tested my heart and come to me in the night; you have put me through the fire and found nothing wrong. I have made up my mind not to sin with my mouth.
4Whatever others may do, I have kept to the word that comes from your lips and stayed off the roads of the violent.
5My steps have held to your tracks; my feet have never slid.
6I call to you, for you answer me, God; bend your ear toward me and listen to what I say.
7Show your loyal love in a wonderful way, you who by your right hand save those who come to you for shelter from their attackers.
8Guard me as one guards the pupil of the eye; shelter me under the shade of your wings,
9from the wicked who attack me, from deadly enemies who close in around me.
10They have shut up their hearts, hardened with fat; their mouths speak proud words.
11Now they track our steps and surround us; their eyes are fixed on throwing us to the ground,
12like a lion eager to tear its prey, like a young lion crouching in its lair.
13Rise up, LORD! Meet them face to face and bring them to their knees. Rescue me from the wicked with your sword,
14from such people, LORD, by your hand, from people of this world whose share is in this life alone. You fill their stomachs with what you have stored up; their children have plenty, and they leave what is left to their little ones.
15But I, in the right, will look on your face; when I wake up, the sight of you will be all I want.
fields.summary: David appeals to God to hear his just cause and to hide him in the shadow of God’s wings from the wicked.

fields.title: Psalm 18
fields.body_html:
David’s song of rescue and victory

For the music director. By David, the servant of the LORD. He sang the words of this song to the LORD on the day the LORD rescued him from the power of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

1He said: “I love you, LORD, my strength.
2The LORD is my cliff, my stronghold, the one who sets me free; my God is my rock, and I shelter in him. He is my shield, my strong salvation, my tower on the heights.
3I call on the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and from my enemies I am rescued.
4Death’s ropes were wrapped around me; floods of ruin overwhelmed me with terror.
5The ropes of Sheol coiled around me; death’s traps lay right in front of me.
6When I was hard pressed I called on the LORD and cried out to my God. Out of his temple he listened to my voice; my cry came before him and reached his ears.
7Then the earth shuddered and rocked; the roots of the mountains trembled and were shaken, because he was furious.
8Smoke rose from his nostrils, and fire that consumes came from his mouth; burning coals flamed out of it.
9He bowed the heavens low and came down; storm clouds were dark beneath his feet.
10Riding on a cherub, he flew; he swooped down on the wings of the wind.
11He wrapped himself in darkness and hid in it; all around him was a tent of dark rain clouds, thick clouds of the sky.
12Out of the brightness in front of him his clouds broke through, with hail and burning coals.
13The LORD thundered in the heavens; the Most High raised his voice, with hail and burning coals.
14He let his arrows fly and scattered the enemy; he hurled lightning bolts and threw them into confusion.
15The beds of the sea came into view, and the world’s foundations lay bare at your rebuke, LORD, at the blast of breath from your nostrils.
16From on high he stretched out his hand and seized me; he pulled me out of deep waters.
17He snatched me away from my powerful enemy, from those who hated me, because they were stronger than I was.
18They came at me on my day of disaster, but the LORD held me up.
19He led me out into open country; he set me free, because he was pleased with me.
20The LORD treated me as my right conduct deserved; he rewarded me because my hands were clean.
21For I have walked in the LORD’s ways and have not turned from my God to do evil.
22All his rulings have been in front of me; I have not pushed his laws aside.
23I was whole-hearted with him; I guarded myself from sin.
24So the LORD rewarded me for doing right, for the clean hands he could see.
25To the faithful you are faithful; to those of integrity you show integrity.
26To the pure you prove yourself pure, but with the crooked you are subtle.
27You rescue people who are humbled, but proud eyes you bring down.
28You make my lamp shine; the LORD my God brightens my darkness.
29With you I can rush an armed band; by the strength of my God I can vault a wall.
30This is God: his way is without flaw; the word of the LORD is tested and true; he is a shield for all who make him their refuge.
31Is there any God but the LORD? Is there any rock but our God?
32the God who straps strength around me like a belt and makes my way secure,
33who makes my feet as sure as a deer’s and sets me firm on the heights,
34who trains my hands for war, so that my arms can draw a bronze bow.
35You have handed me your saving shield; your right hand holds me up, and your stooping down to me has made me great.
36You make room for my steps, so my ankles do not turn.
37I chased my enemies and caught them; I did not give up the chase until I had made an end of them.
38I shattered them, and they could not stand again; they lay fallen at my feet.
39You strapped strength on me for the fight; you brought my attackers to their knees beneath me.
40You put my enemies to flight before me, and I destroyed those who hated me.
41They called for help, but no one came to save them; they cried to the LORD, but he gave them no answer.
42I ground them as fine as dust blown by the wind; I threw them out like mud in the streets.
43You set me free from the people’s quarrels; you put me at the head of the nations. A nation I never knew now serves me.
44The moment they hear, they obey me; foreigners come to me cringing.
45Foreigners lose heart; they come out of their fortresses shaking.
46The LORD is alive! Blessed be my rock! May the God who saves me be lifted high,
47the God who avenges me and brings nations under my rule,
48who saves me from my enemies. You raise me high above my attackers; you save me from the violent man.
49That is why I will give you thanks among the nations, LORD, and sing praise to your name.
50Great are the victories he grants his king; he keeps faith in loyal love with his anointed one, with David and his line for all time.”
fields.summary: David sings of the day God rescued him from all his enemies: God, his rock and fortress, came down in storm and thunder and drew him out of deep waters.

fields.title: Psalm 19
fields.body_html:
Heavens and instruction tell God’s glory

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1The heavens tell over and over how glorious God is; the vault of the sky makes known what his hands have made.
2Each day passes the message on to the next; each night hands its knowledge to the night that follows.
3There is no speech, there are no words; nothing of their voice reaches the ear.
4Even so, their line runs out over the whole earth, their words to the far edge of the world. There he has set up a tent for the sun,
5and the sun comes out like a bridegroom from the wedding room and runs its course with the joy of a strong warrior.
6It sets out from one edge of the heavens and circles round to the other; nothing escapes its heat.
7The instruction of the LORD is whole and without fault; it brings back life. What the LORD has declared can be trusted; it makes the naive wise.
8The charges the LORD lays down are right and fill the heart with joy; the command of the LORD is clear and makes the eyes shine.
9The fear of the LORD is clean and lasts for all time; the rulings of the LORD are true, and every one of them is just.
10They are worth wanting more than gold, more than a great hoard of fine gold; sweeter than honey, sweeter than honey fresh from the comb.
11They also warn your servant, and those who keep them gain a great reward.
12Who can catch all their own mistakes? Hold me clear of faults hidden even from me.
13Hold your servant back from arrogant sins too; let them never be my master. Then I will be whole and clear of any great rebellion.
14May what my mouth speaks and what my heart ponders be welcome before you, LORD, my rock and my redeemer.
fields.summary: The heavens declare God’s glory, and God’s instruction is perfect, more precious than gold; David prays that his words and thoughts may please God.

fields.title: Psalm 20
fields.body_html:
A prayer for the king before battle

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1May the LORD answer you when trouble comes; may the God of Jacob, by his name, keep you safe on the heights.
2May he send you help from the holy place and hold you up from Zion.
3May he remember every gift you have offered and look with favor on your burnt offerings. Selah
4May he grant you what your heart desires and bring every plan of yours to pass.
5We will shout for joy when you win the day, and we will raise our banners in our God’s name. May the LORD give you all you ask for.
6Now I know that the LORD brings his anointed king through safely; from his holy heaven he will answer him with the mighty saving acts of his right hand.
7Some count on chariots, some on horses; we call on the LORD our God by name.
8They will buckle and fall, but we will get up and stand our ground.
9LORD, save! May the King answer us when we cry out.
fields.summary: The people pray that God will answer the king in the day of trouble and give him victory, for they trust not in chariots but in God’s name.

fields.title: Psalm 21
fields.body_html:
The king rejoices in the LORD’s strength

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1LORD, the king takes delight in your strength; your saving help fills him with overflowing joy!
2What his heart longed for, you have given him; what his lips asked, you have not held back. Selah
3Indeed, you go out to greet him with good gifts and blessings; on his head you set a crown of refined gold.
4He asked for life, and you granted it, days stretching on forever and ever.
5Because you rescued him, his honor stands high; you lay royal splendor and majesty on him.
6For you make him a blessing that never ends; you fill him with gladness in your presence.
7The king relies on the LORD, and because of the loyal love of the Most High, nothing will shake him.
8Your hand will reach all your enemies; your right hand will track down all who hate you.
9When you come against them, you will make them like a blazing oven; in his anger the LORD will swallow them, and fire will eat them up.
10You will wipe out their offspring from the earth, their line from among all people.
11Though they aim evil at you and hatch their schemes, they will not get their way.
12For you will put them to flight; you will set arrows to your bowstring and aim at their faces.
13Rise high in your strength, LORD! We will sing and make music in praise of your power.
fields.summary: The king rejoices in God’s strength and saving help, and trusts that God will defeat his enemies.

fields.title: Psalm 22
fields.body_html:
From forsaken to praise among the nations

For the music director. On Ayyeleth-hashshahar. A psalm of David.

1My God, my God, why have you abandoned me? I roar out my words, and still rescue is far away.
2My God, all day I call, and you do not answer; all night too, and I cannot be still.
3Yet you are holy; Israel’s praises are the throne where you sit.
4Our ancestors relied on you; they relied on you, and you brought them out safe.
5They cried out to you and escaped; they relied on you and were never disgraced.
6But I am a worm and no longer a man, a byword of scorn among people, despised by the crowd.
7Everyone who sees me laughs at me; they curl their lips and shake their heads,
8“Leave it to the LORD! Let him get him out of it; let him save him, since he is so delighted with him!”
9Yet it was you who drew me out at birth and kept me safe as I nursed at my mother’s breast.
10From birth I was thrown into your arms; since my mother carried me, you have been my God.
11Do not keep your distance from me; distress is at hand, and I have no helper.
12A herd of bulls has closed in around me; the powerful bulls of Bashan hem me in.
13They gape at me with open jaws, like a lion that roars and rips its prey.
14My life drains away like spilled water; every bone in me is wrenched apart. My heart is like wax, melting deep inside me.
15My strength is as dry as a shard of broken pottery; my tongue is stuck fast to my jaw, and you bring me down to the dust of death.
16Dogs are all around me; a gang of evildoers has closed in on me; like a lion they go for my hands and my feet.
17I can count every one of my bones, while they look on and stare at me.
18They share out my clothes among themselves and throw lots for what I wear.
19But you, LORD, do not stand far off! My strength, hurry to help me!
20Save my life from the sword; save the only life I have from the dog’s paw.
21Save me from the lion’s mouth! Even as the wild oxen lower their horns at me, you have answered me!
22I will make your name known to my brothers and sisters; with the whole assembly gathered, I will praise you.
23Praise him, all who fear the LORD! Let all of Jacob’s family give him honor; let all of Israel’s people stand in awe of him!
24For he has not looked down on the suffering of the one in misery or turned from it in disgust; he did not turn his face away, but heard him when he called for help.
25It is you who give me my praise in the great assembly; I will pay what I vowed where those who fear him can see.
26The poor will eat and have their fill; those who seek him will praise the LORD. May new life fill your hearts forever!
27People at the farthest ends of the earth will remember and come back to the LORD; every clan of every nation will bow low before you.
28For the kingdom is the LORD’s, and he governs the nations.
29The prosperous of the earth will eat and bow in worship; those on their way down to the dust, who have no power to keep their own lives, will bend the knee before him.
30A new generation of descendants will serve him, and they will be told about the Lord in the age that follows.
31They will come and tell of his justice to a people not yet born: he has done this!
fields.summary: David cries, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?” surrounded by mocking enemies, then praises God who has heard him, and all the earth will turn to God.

fields.title: Psalm 23
fields.body_html:
The LORD, my shepherd and host

A psalm of David.

1The LORD is my shepherd;
I will never be in need.
2He settles me down in meadows of fresh green grass;
he leads me gently to water where I can rest.
3He brings back my life
and leads me in the tracks of what is right,
true to his name.
4Even if my path goes down through a valley of deepest darkness, I will not be afraid of any harm,
because you are there with me;
your rod and your staff give me courage.
5You spread a meal before me while my enemies look on;
you refresh my head with oil,
and my cup is full to the brim.
6Goodness and loyal love will surely chase after me every day I live,
and I will come home to the house of the LORD for all my days to come.
fields.summary: God is David’s shepherd, who leads him to rest, guides him through the darkest valley and spreads a table before him; goodness and love will follow him all his life.

fields.title: Psalm 24
fields.body_html:
The King of glory comes in

Of David. A psalm.

1The earth is the LORD’s, and all that fills it, the world and everyone who lives there.
2For it was he who laid its foundations on the seas and set it firmly on the rivers.
3Who has the right to climb the mountain of the LORD? Who may stand in the place of his holiness?
4Those whose hands are innocent and whose hearts are pure, who have not called on God’s own life to back what is false, and have not sworn an oath to deceive.
5Such people carry away a blessing from the LORD, and justice from the God who saves them.
6Such are the people who look for him, who seek your face: this is Jacob. Selah
7Gates, raise your heads high! Lift yourselves up, age-old doors, so that the King of glory may enter.
8Who is this King of glory? It is the LORD, mighty and strong, the LORD, a warrior strong in battle.
9Gates, raise your heads high! Raise them, age-old doors, so that the King of glory may enter.
10Who then is he, this King of glory? It is the LORD of Armies; he is the glorious King. Selah
fields.summary: The earth belongs to God, who made it; those with clean hands may stand in God’s holy place, and the gates are told to open for the King of glory.

fields.title: Psalm 25
fields.body_html:
Teach me your paths and forgive me

Of David.

1To you, LORD, I lift up my whole self.
2My God, I trust in you; do not let me be disgraced, and do not let my enemies gloat over me.
3Indeed, everyone who waits for you will be spared disgrace; it is those who betray others for nothing who will be disgraced.
4LORD, let me come to know your ways; teach me to follow your paths.
5Lead me by your faithfulness and teach me, since you are the God who saves me; it is you I wait for the whole day through.
6LORD, keep in mind your tender mercies and your acts of loyal love; they have been yours since ancient times.
7Do not hold against me the sins of my youth or my acts of rebellion; in your loyal love remember me, for the sake of your goodness, LORD.
8The LORD is good and upright; that is why he shows sinners the way to go.
9He directs the lowly in what is just, and to the lowly he teaches his way.
10Every path the LORD takes is loyal love and faithfulness toward all who hold to his covenant and his decrees.
11LORD, for the honor of your name, forgive the wrong I have done, because it is so great.
12Is there anyone who fears the LORD? He will show that person which way to choose.
13They will live their lives in well-being, and their descendants will possess the land.
14The LORD takes those who fear him into his confidence; he lets them know his covenant.
15I never stop looking to the LORD, because he will pull my feet free of the net.
16Turn toward me and show me grace, for I am lonely and in misery.
17The troubles in my heart have grown larger and larger; rescue me from the tight places I am in.
18See my misery and my toil, and lift the weight of all my sins from me.
19Look how my enemies have multiplied, and how violent is the hatred they hold against me.
20Keep my life safe and set me free; do not let me be disgraced, for I have made you my refuge.
21May integrity and uprightness stand guard over me, for I wait for you.
22God, set Israel free from all its troubles.
fields.summary: David lifts up his whole self to God, asks to be taught God’s ways and forgiven, and trusts God to rescue him.

fields.title: Psalm 26
fields.body_html:
Judge me, for I walk with integrity

Of David.

1LORD, decide my case, for I have walked with integrity; my trust has been in the LORD, and I will not stumble.
2LORD, examine me and put me through trials; refine my innermost feelings and my mind.
3I have kept your loyal love in view, and I have lived my life by your faithfulness.
4I have not sat among the false, and I will not keep company with those who hide what they are.
5I hate the crowd that gathers to do evil; I will not take a seat among the wicked.
6I wash my hands to show that I am innocent, and I walk around your altar, LORD,
7making a song of thanks be heard and telling of every wonder you have done.
8LORD, I love the house that is your home, the place in which your glory has its dwelling.
9Do not carry me off with the sinners, or my life with those who shed blood,
10people whose hands carry out shameful plots and whose right hand is loaded with bribes.
11But as for me, I will live with integrity; set me free and show me grace.
12I stand firm on level ground; in the assemblies I will bless the LORD.
fields.summary: David asks God to examine him, for he has walked with integrity and loves the house where God’s glory dwells.

fields.title: Psalm 27
fields.body_html:
The LORD is my light

Of David.

1The LORD is my light and the one who saves me; who is there for me to fear? The LORD is the fortress that guards my life; who could make me tremble?
2When evil people closed in on me to devour my flesh, my foes and my enemies, they themselves tripped and went down.
3If an army sets up camp against me, my heart will not be afraid; if war rises up against me, I will still hold on to my trust.
4I have asked the LORD for one thing, and it is what I am looking for: to live in the house of the LORD as long as I live, to look on the loveliness of the LORD and to seek him in his temple.
5When the day of trouble comes, he will tuck me away in his shelter, keep me hidden deep inside his tent, and put me up on a rock out of reach.
6So now I will hold my head high over the enemies who surround me; in his tent I will offer sacrifices with joyful shouting, and I will sing and play music for the LORD.
7LORD, listen as I cry out to you; show me grace and answer me.
8My heart says to you what you have said: “Seek my face.” So I will seek your face, LORD.
9Do not turn your face away from me or send your servant off in anger. You have always been my help; do not let go of me or leave me, God who saves me.
10If my father and my mother were to leave me, the LORD would still gather me in.
11LORD, teach me your way; guide me along a smooth path, for there are enemies watching me.
12Do not hand me over to what my enemies want, for lying witnesses have stood up against me, people who breathe out violence.
13Had I not believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD while still among the living, where would I be?
14Keep waiting for the LORD. Stand firm and be brave in heart. Yes, wait for the LORD.
fields.summary: God is David’s light and salvation, so he has no one to fear; he asks to live in God’s house and urges waiting for God.

fields.title: Psalm 28
fields.body_html:
My rock, do not be silent

Of David.

1I call to you, LORD; my rock, do not refuse to hear me. For if you say nothing to me, I will be like those who sink into the pit.
2Listen to my voice as I beg for mercy and cry to you for help, as I raise my hands toward the innermost room of your holy house.
3Do not haul me away along with the wicked and the evildoers, who wish their neighbors peace while they plan harm in their hearts.
4Pay them back for what they do, for the evil of their actions; give them what their hands have earned; let what they deserve come back on them.
5Because they pay no attention to what the LORD does or to what his hands have made, he will pull them down and not raise them up again.
6Blessed is the LORD, because he has listened to my voice as I pleaded.
7The LORD is my strength, the shield that protects me; my heart trusted in him, and help came to me. Now my heart is full of joy, and I will thank him in song.
8The LORD is their strength; he is the fortress where his anointed one finds rescue.
9Rescue your people, bless those who belong to you; be a shepherd to them and carry them in your arms for all time.
fields.summary: David cries out to God, his rock, to hear him and not count him with the wicked, and praises God who has heard.

fields.title: Psalm 29
fields.body_html:
The voice of the LORD in the storm

A psalm of David.

1Acknowledge the LORD, you heavenly beings; acknowledge that glory and strength belong to the LORD.
2Acknowledge the glory that belongs to the name of the LORD; bow before the LORD in holy splendor.
3The voice of the LORD sounds over the waters; the glorious God thunders; the LORD is above the vast waters.
4The voice of the LORD is mighty; the voice of the LORD is splendid as a king.
5The voice of the LORD snaps cedar trees; the LORD smashes the cedars of Lebanon to pieces.
6He sets Lebanon jumping like a calf and Sirion bucking like a young wild ox.
7The voice of the LORD carves out flames of fire.
8The voice of the LORD sets the desert trembling; the LORD makes the Kadesh desert quake.
9The voice of the LORD brings the does to labor and leaves the woods stripped; and in his temple everyone shouts, “Glory!”
10The LORD sat on his throne above the flood; the LORD is seated as King for all time.
11The LORD will make his people strong; the LORD will give his people the blessing of peace.
fields.summary: The heavenly beings are called to give God glory, whose voice thunders over the waters and shakes the wilderness, and who blesses the people with peace.

fields.title: Psalm 30
fields.body_html:
Mourning turned into dancing

A psalm. A song for the dedication of the house. Of David.

1I will praise you as high above all, LORD, because you drew me up as from a well and did not give my enemies the joy of seeing me fall.
2LORD, my God, I shouted to you for help, and you made me well.
3LORD, you brought me back up from Sheol; you kept me alive and did not let me sink into the pit.
4Make music to the LORD, all you who are loyal to him; give thanks as you call to mind his holy name.
5For his anger is over in a moment, but in his favor there is life; weeping may come to spend the night, but at dawn there are shouts of joy.
6When things were going well for me, I said, “Nothing will ever shake me.”
7LORD, in your kindness you had made me firm as a mountain; then you hid your face, and I was overcome with fear.
8I called out to you, LORD; I begged the Lord for mercy.
9“What would anyone gain from my death, from my going down into the pit? Can dust give thanks to you? Can it speak of how faithful you are?
10Listen, LORD, and show me grace; LORD, come and help me.”
11You have changed my lament into dancing; you took off my sackcloth and dressed me in joy,
12so that with all that is in me I may make music to you and not keep quiet. LORD my God, I will give you thanks for all time.
fields.summary: David praises God for lifting him up from the grave; weeping may last for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

fields.title: Psalm 31
fields.body_html:
Into your hand I commit my spirit

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1LORD, I have made you my refuge; never let me be disgraced; because you are righteous, set me free.
2Bend down and listen to me; hurry to rescue me. Be a rock where I can shelter, a fortified house that keeps me safe.
3You yourself are my rock and my stronghold; for the honor of your name you will lead me and show me the way.
4You will free me from the net they have secretly laid for me, because you are my stronghold.
5I put my spirit into your hand for safekeeping; you have redeemed me, LORD, God who is faithful.
6I hate those who devote themselves to useless idols; but my trust is in the LORD.
7I will be full of joy and delight because of your loyal love, for you saw how I suffered and took notice of the troubles I was in.
8You did not give me up into the power of my enemy; you have set my feet down in a wide-open place.
9Have pity on me, LORD, for I am in trouble; grief has worn out my eyes, my whole self, my body.
10Sorrow is using up my life, and groaning my years; my guilt has made my strength give way, and my bones are wasting.
11All my enemies have made me a disgrace, above all to my neighbors; the people I know are afraid of me, and when they see me outside they run from me.
12People have put me out of their minds as if I had died; I am like a smashed pot.
13I hear many people whispering lies — terror everywhere! — as they plan together against me, scheming to take my life.
14But I put my trust in you, LORD; I tell you, “You alone are my God.”
15My whole life, every season of it, is in your hand; rescue me from the power of my enemies and from those chasing me.
16Turn the light of your face toward your servant; in your loyal love, save me.
17LORD, do not let me be disgraced, for I have called to you; let the disgrace fall on the wicked; let them lie silent in Sheol.
18May the lips that lie be struck dumb, lips that speak insolently against the righteous with pride and scorn.
19How great is the good you keep in store for those who fear you, the good you do, for all to see, to those who make you their refuge!
20You hide them under the cover of your presence, away from human plotting; you keep them in a shelter, safe from quarrelsome tongues.
21Blessed is the LORD, who has done a wonder of loyal love for me when I was in a city under siege.
22In my panic I said, “I have been cut off, out of your sight.” Yet you heard my voice as I pleaded for mercy and cried out to you.
23Love the LORD, all you who are loyal to him! The LORD watches over those who keep faith, but the one who acts proudly he repays in full measure.
24Stand firm and be brave in heart, all of you who put your hope in the LORD.
fields.summary: David commits his spirit into God’s hand, tells of his distress and the plots against him, and praises God’s goodness to those who take refuge in God.

fields.title: Psalm 32
fields.body_html:
The joy of sin forgiven

Of David. A maskil.

1How blessed is the one whose rebellion is forgiven, whose sin is covered over!
2How blessed is anyone whose guilt the LORD does not hold against them, who has no deceit in their spirit!
3While I kept quiet, my bones wore away with my groaning the whole day long.
4Day and night your hand pressed hard on me; the life in me dried up as in the drought of summer. Selah
5I made my sin known to you; I did not hide my wrongdoing. I said, “I will own my rebellion before the LORD,” and you took away my sin and its guilt. Selah
6So let everyone who is faithful pray to you in the time when you can be found. Even when great waters come flooding in, the flood will not reach them.
7You are my shelter where I can hide; you keep me safe from distress and put glad cries of rescue all around me. Selah
8I will give you insight and show you the road you are to take; I will advise you and keep my eye on you.
9Do not be like a horse or mule with no sense, which needs a harness of bit and halter to rein it in, or else it will not come near you.
10The wicked have many sorrows, but whoever trusts in the LORD is surrounded by loyal love.
11Celebrate in the LORD and be joyful, you righteous; sing out with joy, all whose hearts are upright!
fields.summary: Those whose rebellion is forgiven are blessed; when David kept silent he wasted away, but when he confessed, God forgave him.

fields.title: Psalm 33
fields.body_html:
Praise the Creator who rules the nations

1Sing for joy in the LORD, you righteous; praise suits those who are upright.
2Thank the LORD on the lyre; play music for him on the ten-stringed harp.
3Sing him a new song; play your best, with shouts of joy.
4For the LORD’s word is right, and all his deeds show his faithfulness.
5He loves what is right and just; the LORD’s loyal love fills the whole earth.
6The heavens were made at the LORD’s word, and the breath of his mouth made all their array of stars.
7He heaps up the waters of the sea like a mound and keeps the ocean depths in storerooms.
8Let the whole earth fear the LORD; let everyone who lives in the world tremble with awe before him.
9For he only had to speak, and it was; he gave the command, and there it stood.
10The LORD brings the schemes of nations to nothing; he blocks what the peoples plan.
11The LORD’s purpose stands firm forever, and what he has planned in his heart lasts through every generation.
12How blessed is the nation that has the LORD as its God, the people he chose to be his own possession!
13The LORD looks out from heaven and sees every human being.
14From the place where he lives he keeps his eye on everyone who lives on the earth,
15the one who shaped every one of their hearts and who notices everything they do.
16No king wins the day because his army is large; no warrior escapes because his strength is great.
17The horse is a deceptive hope for victory; with all its great strength it saves no one.
18Look, the LORD keeps watch over those who fear him, who wait with hope for his loyal love,
19to save their lives from death and to keep them living through famine.
20With all our being we wait for the LORD; he is the one who helps us and shields us.
21Our hearts are glad in him, because we have put our trust in his holy name.
22LORD, let your loyal love be over us, in keeping with our hope in you.
fields.summary: The righteous are called to sing a new song to God, whose word made the heavens and whose eye is on those who fear God and hope in God’s loyal love.

fields.title: Psalm 34
fields.body_html:
Taste and see the LORD’s goodness

Of David, when he pretended to be insane in front of Abimelech, who drove him away, and he left.

1I will bless the LORD in every season; praise of him will never leave my mouth.
2I will make my boast in the LORD; let the humble hear it and rejoice.
3Join me in telling how great the LORD is; let us lift high his name together.
4I went looking for the LORD; he gave me an answer and rescued me from everything I dreaded.
5Those who look to him glow with joy, and no shame will darken their faces.
6Here was a poor man who cried out; the LORD heard and rescued him from every one of his troubles.
7The angel of the LORD pitches camp all around the people who fear him, and sets them free.
8Taste and see how good the LORD is! How blessed is the person who makes him their refuge!
9Fear the LORD, all you his people set apart; nothing is missing for those who fear him.
10Even young lions can go short and feel hunger, but those who seek the LORD will never be without anything good.
11Come here, children, and hear what I say; I will teach you what it means to fear the LORD.
12Which of you wants life and longs for many days to enjoy good things?
13Hold your tongue back from evil, and keep your lips from saying anything false.
14Turn away from evil and do what is good; look for peace and go after it.
15The LORD keeps his eyes on the righteous and his ears open to their call for help.
16The LORD turns his face against people who do evil, to erase every trace of them from the earth.
17When the righteous cry out, the LORD listens and frees them from every trouble they face.
18The LORD stays close to those whose hearts are broken, and rescues those whose spirits are crushed.
19A righteous person faces many troubles, but the LORD brings them safely through every one.
20He watches over their whole body; not a single bone will be broken.
21The wicked will be killed by their own evil; whoever hates the righteous will bear the guilt.
22The LORD ransoms the lives of his servants; none who make him their refuge will bear guilt.
fields.summary: David praises God, who answered him and delivered him from all his fears, and invites others to taste and see that God is good.

fields.title: Psalm 35
fields.body_html:
Fight for me, LORD

Of David.

1LORD, oppose those who oppose me; do battle with those who battle against me.
2Seize the small shield and the large one, and stand up to help me.
3Draw the spear and battle-axe to face those who chase me; let me hear you say, “I am your salvation.”
4Let those who are hunting for my life be shamed and disgraced; let those who are plotting to hurt me be driven back in confusion.
5May they be like chaff the wind blows off, with the LORD’s angel driving them along.
6May their path turn dark and slick, with the LORD’s angel hunting them down.
7For no reason they set a hidden net in a pit for me; for no reason they dug a hole to trap me.
8Let disaster fall on them before they know it; let the net they hid catch them, and let them drop into it to their ruin.
9Then my whole being will be glad in the LORD and celebrate the salvation he brings.
10Every bone in my body will say, “LORD, is there anyone like you? You save the helpless from people stronger than they are, the helpless and the poor from those who rob them.”
11Violent witnesses stand up against me and question me about things I know nothing of.
12They pay me back harm for good; I am left desolate, like someone who has lost a child.
13But as for me, when they lay sick, I dressed in sackcloth; I humbled myself by fasting, and I prayed with my head bent low.
14I went about as if for a friend or a brother; I bent low, dressed in dark mourning clothes, like one grieving for a mother.
15But when I stumbled, they were glad and gathered together; attackers gathered against me without my knowing it; they ripped into me and would not be quiet.
16Like ungodly jesters who mock for a bite of food, they ground their teeth at me.
17Lord, how long will you stand and watch? Bring me back from the ruin they cause; save my one and only life from the lions.
18I will thank you when the great congregation gathers; I will praise you among crowds of people.
19Do not let my lying enemies gloat over me; do not let those who hate me for nothing wink at each other.
20For they do not talk of peace; they dream up lies against people living quietly in the land.
21They open their mouths wide at me and say, “Aha! Aha! We saw it with our own eyes!”
22You have seen it, LORD; do not keep silent. Lord, do not stay far away from me.
23Wake up! Rouse yourself to do me justice; my God and my Lord, take up my case!
24LORD my God, give judgment for me as your righteousness requires; let them not rejoice over me.
25Do not let them say to themselves, “Aha! We got our wish!” Do not let them say, “We have gulped him down.”
