26Let all who are glad at my trouble be shamed and confused together; let those who lift themselves up over me be dressed in shame and disgrace.
27Let those who want to see me proved right shout with joy and be glad; let them say again and again, “The LORD is great! He is pleased when his servant has peace.”
28Then all day long I will talk about how righteous you are and sing your praise.
fields.summary: David asks God to fight those who fight against him and repay those who return evil for good.

fields.title: Psalm 36
fields.body_html:
Rebellion’s whisper and God’s wide love

For the music director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David.

1Deep in my heart I hear what rebellion says to the wicked: they have no dread of God before their eyes.
2For they flatter themselves in their own sight too much to see their own guilt and hate it.
3What they say is evil and lies; they have given up being wise and doing good.
4Even lying in bed they plot evil; they set themselves on a path that leads nowhere good and never turn away from wrong.
5LORD, your loyal love reaches up into the heavens, your faithfulness as high as the clouds.
6Your righteousness stands like the mighty mountains; your judgments are deep as the ocean depths. LORD, you rescue people and animals alike.
7God, how precious your loyal love is! All kinds of people make you their refuge, sheltering in the shade of your wings.
8They are filled with the rich food of your house; you let them drink from your stream of joys.
9For the spring of life is with you; it is your light that lets us see light.
10Keep showing your loyal love to all who know you, and show your righteousness to people whose hearts are upright.
11Do not let the foot of the proud trample me, or the hand of the wicked push me away.
12There the evildoers have fallen; they have been knocked down and cannot stand up again.
fields.summary: The wicked have no fear of God, but God’s loyal love reaches to the heavens, and with God is the fountain of life.

fields.title: Psalm 37
fields.body_html:
Do not fret; wait for the LORD

Of David.

1Do not let evildoers get you heated; do not envy people who practice injustice.
2They will dry up quickly, like grass, and droop like tender green shoots.
3Trust in the LORD and do what is good; make your home in the land and feed on faithfulness.
4Make the LORD your joy, and he will grant what your heart asks.
5Lay the course of your life on the LORD; rely on him, and he will step in.
6He will bring your innocence into the open like daylight, the justice of your cause like the blaze of noon.
7Be silent before the LORD; wait for him with longing. Do not be upset by those whose way goes well, by people who put their plots into action.
8Let go of anger and leave rage behind. Do not get heated; it can end only in wrongdoing.
9Evildoers will be cut down, but those who look to the LORD in hope will take possession of the land.
10Wait a short while, and the wicked will have vanished; look closely at the place where they stood, and you will find nothing.
11But the lowly will possess the land and take their delight in great well-being.
12The wicked plot harm for the righteous and grind their teeth at them.
13The Lord laughs at them, for he sees their day drawing near.
14The wicked have unsheathed the sword and strung their bows, ready to cut down the poor and the needy and to butcher those who walk straight.
15But the sword they drew will be thrust into their own hearts; their bows will snap in two.
16The little that the righteous own is worth more than the plenty of many wicked people.
17The wicked will have their arms snapped, while the LORD keeps the righteous on their feet.
18The LORD watches over every day the blameless live, and their share will last for all time.
19When disaster comes they will not be disgraced; when famine strikes they will have enough to eat.
20The wicked are doomed to perish, and the LORD’s enemies will be like the bloom of the fields: they come to an end, and end in smoke.
21The wicked borrow and never pay back, but the righteous are kind and give freely.
22Those he blesses will possess the land, but those he curses will be cut off.
23The LORD makes a person’s steps secure when he takes pleasure in their way.
24They may stumble, but they will not be thrown down, for the LORD holds them by the hand.
25Young I was, and now I am old, and in all those years I have not known the righteous to be deserted, or their children to go hunting for bread.
26All day long they show kindness and lend, and their offspring become a blessing.
27Turn away from evil and do what is good, and you will have a home for all time.
28For the LORD loves what is just and will not abandon his faithful people. They are guarded for all time, while the line of the wicked comes to an end.
29The righteous will take possession of the land and live there for all time.
30The righteous murmur wisdom with their mouths, and their tongues talk of what is right.
31They hold the instruction of their God in their hearts; their steps never falter.
32The wicked spy on the righteous, looking for a chance to kill them.
33The LORD will not abandon them to the grip of their enemy; when they stand trial, he will not declare them guilty.
34Put your hope in the LORD and keep to his way; he will raise you up to take possession of the land, and you will see the wicked cut off.
35I have seen someone wicked and ruthless, spreading out like a leafy tree in its home soil.
36Yet that person passed on, and suddenly was gone; I searched, but could find no trace.
37Pay attention to people of integrity, look closely at the upright: those who live in peace have a future ahead of them.
38Rebels will be destroyed, every one of them, and what lies ahead for the wicked will be cut off.
39It is the LORD who saves the righteous; he is their fortress in days of distress.
40The LORD helps them and sets them free; he pulls them from the grip of the wicked and keeps them safe, since they make him their refuge.
fields.summary: The righteous are told not to fret over evildoers, who will soon wither, but to trust God and wait patiently, for the meek will inherit the land.

fields.title: Psalm 38
fields.body_html:
Prayer of a sick and guilty sufferer

A psalm of David. For remembrance.

1LORD, if you must rebuke me, let it not be in anger; if you discipline me, let it not be in fury.
2Your arrows have driven deep into me; your hand weighs down on me.
3Nothing in my body is healthy, because of your fury; nothing in my bones is whole, because of my sin.
4My sins have closed over my head; like a heavy load, they weigh more than I can bear.
5My sores are foul and rotting, all because of my own foolishness.
6I am bent over, bowed down completely; I spend the whole day going about in grief.
7A burning fever fills my sides, and nothing in my body is well.
8I have gone numb and am crushed to the core; my heart groans, and I cry out aloud.
9Lord, you see everything I long for; not one of my sighs escapes you.
10My heart races; my strength has deserted me; the light of my eyes, that too is gone.
11My friends and companions keep away from my sickness; even my own family stands at a distance.
12Those who want my life set traps; those who want to hurt me speak of destroying me and mutter lies all day long.
13But I act as if I were deaf and hear nothing, as if I were mute and could not open my mouth.
14I have turned into someone who hears nothing and has no answer to give.
15LORD, my hope is fixed on you; you are the one who will answer, Lord my God.
16For I said, “Do not let them enjoy my fall; when my foot slips, they lord it over me.”
17I am on the edge of collapse, and my pain never leaves my sight.
18I openly admit my guilt; my sin weighs on me with dread.
19Meanwhile my enemies are full of life and strength; many hate me for no good reason.
20Those who return evil for kindness act as my accusers, because I go after what is good.
21Do not abandon me, LORD; my God, do not stay far from me.
22Be quick to help me, Lord, my salvation.
fields.summary: Sick and burdened by guilt, abandoned by friends, David confesses his sin and pleads with God not to forsake him.

fields.title: Psalm 39
fields.body_html:
My life is only a breath

For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

1I made up my mind: “I will be careful how I live, so that my tongue does not lead me into sin. I will keep my mouth muzzled for as long as the wicked stand before me.”
2I said nothing at all; I held my peace, even from saying good, and my pain grew sharper.
3Inside me my heart was burning; as I brooded, it flared into fire, and at last I spoke:
4LORD, let me know my end and how many days are measured out for me; let me understand how short-lived I am.
5See, you have made my days only a few hand widths long; my whole lifetime is as nothing in your sight. Every human being, however firmly they stand, is only a breath. Selah
6Truly, people go about like shadows; their busy noise is all for nothing; they pile things up, not knowing who will collect them.
7So then, Lord, what is left for me to wait for? My hope rests on you.
8Rescue me from all my rebellious acts; do not make me something fools laugh at.
9I stay silent and say nothing, because this is your doing.
10Take your blow away from me; I am worn out by the force of your hand.
11You punish people for their wrongs with rebukes, and like a moth you eat away what they love most. Every human being is only a breath. Selah
12LORD, hear what I pray; turn your ear to my plea for help, and do not keep silent when I weep. I am only a guest with you, a foreigner passing through, just like my ancestors before me.
13Turn your gaze from me, and let me find joy again before I leave and am no longer here.
fields.summary: David reflects that human life is a breath and asks God to show him how short his days are; his hope is in God.

fields.title: Psalm 40
fields.body_html:
A new song, then a cry for help

For the music director. Of David. A psalm.

1I waited and kept on waiting for the LORD, and he bent down toward me and listened to my cry for help.
2He drew me up from the roaring pit, out of the clinging mud; he planted my feet on a rock and steadied my steps.
3He gave me a new song to sing, a hymn for our God. Many people will look on and be filled with awe, and they will put their trust in the LORD.
4How blessed are those who make the LORD their trust, who do not turn to the arrogant or to those who wander off after lies!
5LORD my God, you have done so many things, your wonders and your plans for us; no one can compare with you! If I tried to tell them all and speak of them, there would be more than I could count.
6You took no pleasure in sacrifice and offering, but you opened my ears; you did not ask for burnt offerings or sin offerings.
7Then I said, “Here I come! What I must do is written down for me in the scroll of the book.
8My God, I love to do what you want; your instruction is deep inside me.”
9In the great assembly I have announced the good news of righteousness. I have not held my lips back; you know it, LORD.
10Your justice I did not keep shut up in my heart; I talked of how faithful you are and how you rescue. Your loyal love and your truth I did not hide from the great assembly.
11And you, LORD, will not hold back your tender mercy from me; your loyal love and your truth will guard me always.
12Troubles too many to count have closed in around me; my sins have caught up with me, and I cannot see. They outnumber the hairs on my head, and my courage has left me.
13LORD, be willing to rescue me! LORD, hurry and help me!
14Let those who hunt for my life to snatch it away be shamed and confounded, all of them; let those who wish me harm be driven back and humiliated.
15Let those who jeer at me, “Aha! Aha!”, be stunned by their own shame.
16But may everyone who looks for you shout for joy and find gladness in you; may those who love to see you save never stop saying, “How great the LORD is!”
17As for me, I am poor and in need; may the Lord keep me in mind. You are the one who helps me and sets me free; my God, do not be slow!
fields.summary: David waited patiently for God, who drew him up from the pit and put a new song in his mouth; he delights to do God’s will.

fields.title: Psalm 41
fields.body_html:
Betrayed by a friend, upheld by God

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1How blessed are those who care about the weak! When trouble comes, the LORD will rescue them.
2The LORD will protect them and keep them alive; they will be counted blessed in the land. Do not hand them over to the will of their enemies!
3The LORD will hold them up on their sickbed; when they are ill, you turn their whole bed of sickness to health.
4I said, “LORD, show me grace! Heal me, because it is you I have sinned against.”
5My enemies say cruel things about me: “When will he die and be wiped from memory?”
6When any of them come to visit me, they say what they do not mean, while inside they gather up bad news; then they go out and spread it.
7All who hate me whisper together about me; they plot harm against me, saying,
8“Some deadly thing has been poured into him; now that he is down, he will never get up again.”
9Even the friend I was at peace with, the one I trusted, who shared my bread, has turned his heel against me.
10But you, LORD, show me grace and lift me up, so that I can pay them back.
11This is how I know you are pleased with me: my enemy does not get to cheer in triumph over me.
12As for me, you keep hold of me in my integrity and let me stand before your face for all time.
13May the LORD, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come! Amen and amen.
fields.summary: Those who care for the weak are blessed; in sickness, betrayed even by a close friend, David asks God to raise him up.

fields.title: Psalm 42
fields.body_html:
Thirsty for the living God

For the music director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.

1Like a doe that longs for running streams, I long for you, God, with all my being.
2I am thirsty for God, the living God. When may I come and stand before God’s face?
3Day and night I have fed on my tears, while all day long people ask me, “Where is your God?”
4I pour out my heart as I call these things to mind: how I walked with the crowd and led them up to God’s house, among shouts of joy and songs of thanks, a great crowd celebrating the feast.
5Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give him thanks again, for the rescue that comes from his presence.
6My God, I am bent low inside; so I will remember you here in the Jordan country and on the peaks of Hermon, on Mount Mizar.
7One deep calls out to another at the roar of your cascades; all your breaking waves and rollers have gone over my head.
8By day the LORD sends out his loyal love, and at night his song stays with me, a prayer to the God who gives me life.
9I cry out to God, my rock: “Why have you put me out of your mind? Why do I walk about dressed in grief while the enemy presses me hard?”
10My foes mock me with a taunt that crushes my bones, while all day long they ask me, “Where is your God?”
11Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give him thanks again, the one who saves me, my God.
fields.summary: Like a deer longing for streams, the psalmist thirsts for God, and asks his soul why it is downcast: hope in God.

fields.title: Psalm 43
fields.body_html:
Send out your light and truth

1Give judgment for me, God, and take up my case against a nation without loyalty; save me from people who lie and do wrong.
2For you are God, my fortress. Why have you pushed me away? Why do I walk about dressed in grief while the enemy presses me hard?
3Let your light and your truth go out to guide me; may they lead me up to your holy mountain, to the place where you live.
4Then I will come up to God’s altar, to God, who is my gladness and my joy, and with the lyre I will give you thanks, God, my God.
5Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give him thanks again, the one who saves me, my God.
fields.summary: The psalmist asks God to send out light and truth to lead him to God’s altar, and again urges his soul to hope in God.

fields.title: Psalm 44
fields.body_html:
Faithful, yet crushed: wake up, Lord

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil.

1God, our own ears have heard it; our ancestors told us of the deeds you did when they lived, in times long past.
2With your own hand you drove out nations and planted our ancestors in their place; you struck down peoples and let our ancestors spread out.
3Their own swords did not win them the land; their own strength did not bring them rescue. Your right hand did it, your arm, and the shining of your face, because you took delight in them.
4You alone are my King, God; give the order for Jacob’s victories.
5Through you we gore our enemies like a bull; through your name we stamp down those who attack us.
6I do not rely on my own bow, and my sword cannot save me.
7No, it is you who rescued us from our enemies and put to shame those who hate us.
8God has been our boast the whole day long, and to your name we will give praise for all time. Selah
9Yet you have thrown us aside and disgraced us; you do not go into battle with our troops.
10You made us retreat before the enemy, and those who hate us have helped themselves to our goods.
11You hand us over like sheep to be eaten, and you have spread us out among the nations.
12You sell off your own people for next to nothing; their price has not made you any richer.
13You have made us a disgrace in the eyes of our neighbors, a joke and a laughingstock to all around us.
14You have turned our name into a proverb among the nations; the peoples shake their heads at us.
15All day long I see my disgrace, and shame is written over my face,
16because of the voice of those who taunt and mock, because of the sight of the enemy bent on revenge.
17All this has fallen on us, yet we have not put you out of mind or broken faith with your covenant.
18Our hearts have not turned away, and our feet have not wandered from your road,
19yet you have crushed us in a place where only jackals live, and wrapped us in deathly darkness.
20Had we forgotten our God’s name, or lifted our hands in prayer to a foreign god,
21would not God have searched it out? For he knows what is hidden in the heart.
22Because we belong to you, we are being killed all day long; we are looked on as sheep marked for the butcher.
23Wake up, Lord! Why are you sleeping? Rise from your sleep! Do not cast us off forever!
24Why do you turn your face away and forget how we suffer and are oppressed?
25We are bowed down into the dust; our bodies are pressed flat against the ground.
26Rise up and come to our help! Set us free because of your loyal love.
fields.summary: Israel recalls God’s deeds for their ancestors, yet now they are defeated and scorned though they have not forgotten God; they cry out for God to wake and help.

fields.title: Psalm 45
fields.body_html:
A wedding song for the king

For the music director. On shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A love song.

1A lovely theme has set my heart astir; I offer my verses to the king, and my tongue runs like the pen of an expert scribe.
2You are more handsome than anyone else; grace pours from your lips; that is why God has blessed you forever.
3Strap your sword to your side, mighty warrior, in your splendor and your majesty!
4In your majesty ride out to victory for the sake of truth, humility and justice; let your right hand show you deeds that inspire awe.
5Your arrows are sharp; peoples fall beneath you; they pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies.
6Your throne, God, lasts for ever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter that rules rightly.
7You love justice and hate evil; that is why God, your God, has anointed you, rather than your companions, with the oil of gladness.
8Your robes all breathe out myrrh and aloes and cassia; the sound of strings from ivory-inlaid palaces brings you joy.
9Princesses are among the ladies of your court; at your right hand stands the queen, adorned with gold from Ophir.
10Hear me, daughter, take note and listen closely: leave behind your own people and your family home,
11then the king will long for your beauty. He is your lord; bow down to him.
12Tyre’s daughter will come with a gift; the wealthiest of the people will try to win your favor.
13The princess waits within, all splendid; her gown is woven with gold.
14In bright embroidered robes she is led to the king, with her maiden companions following, brought to you.
15Amid joy and celebration they are escorted in, and they go into the king’s palace.
16Where your fathers once stood, your sons will stand; you will set them up as princes over all the land.
17I will make your name remembered from one generation to the next; so the nations will give you thanks for all time.
fields.summary: A love song for the king’s wedding praises the king’s majesty and righteous rule and calls the bride to honor him.

fields.title: Psalm 46
fields.body_html:
God is with us in the shaking world

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. On alamoth. A song.

1God is a shelter and a strength for us, a help always close at hand in times of distress.
2So we will not be afraid, even if the earth is overturned and the mountains slide down into the depths of the sea,
3when its waters roar and churn and the mountains shudder as the sea heaves. Selah
4There is a river; its channels bring joy to God’s city, the sacred home of the Most High.
5God is in the middle of the city; nothing will topple it. God will come to its aid as the morning breaks.
6Nations were in turmoil and kingdoms shook; he thundered, and the earth melted away.
7The LORD of Armies is on our side; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah
8Come, look at the deeds of the LORD, the havoc he has worked across the earth.
9He puts an end to wars as far as the earth reaches; he snaps the bow, splits the spear, and sets the war wagons on fire.
10“Stop, and acknowledge that I am God. Among the nations I will be lifted high; over all the earth I will be lifted high.”
11The LORD of Armies is on our side; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah
fields.summary: God is our refuge and strength, so we will not fear though the earth gives way; God is in the city, and the nations are told to be still and know God.

fields.title: Psalm 47
fields.body_html:
God goes up as King of all the earth

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1All you peoples, clap your hands! Raise a shout to God with ringing cries of joy!
2For the LORD Most High inspires awe; he is the great King who rules the whole earth.
3He brings peoples under our rule and lays nations at our feet.
4He picked out our heritage for us, the glory of Jacob, the one he loved. Selah
5God has gone up amid shouting; the LORD has gone up as the ram’s horn sounds.
6Make music to God, make music! Make music to our King, make music!
7For God reigns as King of all the earth; make music with a skillful psalm.
8God now rules as King over the nations; upon his holy throne God sits.
9The princes of the peoples come together to be the people of Abraham’s God. For the shields of the earth are God’s; he is raised high above all.
fields.summary: All peoples are called to clap and shout to God, the great King over all the earth.

fields.title: Psalm 48
fields.body_html:
Zion, the city of the great King

A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.

1The LORD is great and deserves all praise in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.
2Mount Zion rises in beauty, the delight of the whole earth; it is the true heights of Zaphon, the great King’s city.
3Within the city’s strongholds God has proved himself a high refuge.
4Look: the kings gathered their armies and marched on together.
5They looked, and were stunned; they panicked and ran.
6There they were seized with shaking, with pangs like a woman giving birth.
7With a wind from the east you wreck the ships of Tarshish.
8What we had heard, we have now seen with our own eyes in the city of the LORD of Armies, the city of our God: God will make it stand firm forever. Selah
9God, we have reflected on your loyal love here inside your temple.
10Your praise, God, matches your name and spreads to the far ends of the earth; your right hand overflows with justice.
11Let Mount Zion be glad, and the towns of Judah celebrate, because you judge rightly.
12Make a circuit of Zion and walk all the way around; count up its towers,
13take careful note of its walls, walk through its strongholds, so that you can tell the generation to come
14that this is God, our God forever and always; he will be our guide until we die.
fields.summary: Zion, the city of God, is beautiful and secure; kings who saw it fled in terror, and God will guide God’s people forever.

fields.title: Psalm 49
fields.body_html:
No one can buy a way out of death

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1Listen to this, all you nations; pay attention, everyone who lives in the world,
2the humble and the great, the rich and the poor together.
3What I say will be wise; what my heart has pondered will give insight.
4I will listen closely to a proverb; to the music of the lyre I will lay open my riddle.
5Why should I be afraid in evil times, when the wrongdoing of those who dog my steps closes in on me,
6people who rely on their money and brag about how rich they are?
7No one can ever buy back the life of another, or pay God the price for that person’s life,
8for the price of a life is far too high, and no payment could ever be enough,
9so that anyone could live on forever and never see the grave.
10Anyone can see it: wise people die, and fools and dullards perish with them, handing over their wealth to others.
11They imagine their houses will last forever, their homes for all generations; they have named whole estates after themselves.
12Yet no one, however honored, stays for long; humans are no different from animals that die.
13Such is the road of the foolishly self-assured, and of those who come after them and like what they say. Selah
14Like sheep they are herded into Sheol, and Death is their shepherd. The upright will rule over them when morning comes; their bodies will waste away in Sheol, far from their grand houses.
15But God will pay the ransom for my life and free it from Sheol’s grip, for he will take me. Selah
16Do not be alarmed when someone gets rich and their household gains in wealth and honor,
17for when they die they can take none of it with them; their splendor will not follow them down.
18Though in life they count themselves blessed — and people praise you when you prosper —
19they will go to join the generation of their ancestors, who will never again see the light.
20A person held in honor who does not understand is no different from animals that die.
fields.summary: Wealth cannot ransom anyone from death; the rich and the foolish perish alike, but God will redeem the psalmist’s life from the grave.

fields.title: Psalm 50
fields.body_html:
God brings his people to court

A psalm of Asaph.

1The Mighty One, God, the LORD, has spoken; he has called to the whole earth, from the sunrise to the sunset.
2God has blazed out from Zion, the city of flawless beauty.
3Our God is coming, and he will not stay silent; a fire consumes all in his path, and a fierce storm rages on every side.
4He calls heaven above and earth below as witnesses, as he judges his people:
5“Bring together before me my loyal people, who sealed my covenant with a sacrifice.”
6The heavens make known his justice, because it is God who sits as judge. Selah
7“Pay attention, my people, for I am about to speak; I am bringing testimony against you, Israel. I am God, your God.
8I do not find fault with you over your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are always in front of me.
9I will not accept a young bull from your household, or male goats out of your sheepfolds.
10For all the creatures of the woods belong to me, and so do the herds grazing over a thousand hills.
11I know every bird of the high hills; whatever stirs in the open country is in my keeping.
12Were I ever hungry, you are not the one I would tell, since the world and all it holds are mine.
13Am I one who eats the meat of bulls, or drinks the blood of goats?
14Offer thanksgiving to God as your sacrifice, and keep the vows you made to the Most High,
15and call to me when trouble comes; I will set you free, and you will give me glory.”
16But to the wicked God says: “What business do you have reciting my decrees, or mouthing the words of my covenant?
17You hate to be corrected, and you toss my words over your shoulder.
18You see a thief and are happy to go along with him; you share in what adulterers do.
19You let your mouth run free to do harm, and your tongue weaves lies.
20You sit around speaking against your brother; you smear the name of your own mother’s son.
21You did these things and I said nothing, so you imagined I was no different from you. Now I will rebuke you and lay out the case before your eyes.
22Now take this to heart, all of you who forget God, or I will tear you apart like a lion, and no one will be able to save you.
23Whoever offers thanks as a sacrifice gives me honor, and whoever walks the right road, I will let them see how God saves.”
fields.summary: God summons heaven and earth to judge the people: God needs no sacrifices but wants thanksgiving and faithfulness, and rebukes the wicked.

fields.title: Psalm 51
fields.body_html:
Create a pure heart in me

For the music director. A psalm of David, when the prophet Nathan came to him after he had slept with Bathsheba.

1God, be gracious to me in keeping with your loyal love;
in the fullness of your compassion,
wipe away my rebellious acts.
2Scrub me completely clean of my guilt,
and purify me from my sin.
3I myself know my rebellious acts,
and my sin is never out of my sight.
4I have sinned against you, against you alone,
and done what you see as evil.
So you are shown to be right in your sentence
and pure in your judgment.
5Indeed, guilt was with me when I was born;
sin was there when my mother conceived me.
6Yet you long for truth deep within,
and in my secret self you make wisdom known to me.
7Take away my sin with hyssop, and I will be pure;
when you wash me, I will be whiter than snow.
8Fill my ears with gladness and joy;
let the bones you crushed dance.
9Turn your face away from my sins,
and erase all my guilt.
10God, create a pure heart for me,
and make my spirit new and steady inside me.
11Do not drive me away from your presence,
and do not withdraw your Holy Spirit from me.
12Give back to me the gladness of your salvation,
and keep me steady with a willing spirit.
13I will teach rebels your paths,
and sinners will come home to you.
14Rescue me, God, from the guilt of the blood I have shed,
God who saves me;
then my tongue will ring out with your righteousness.
15Lord, open my lips to speak,
and I will make your praise known.
16Sacrifice is not what you desire, or I would offer it;
a burnt offering does not please you.
17The sacrifices that God accepts are a broken spirit.
A heart that is broken and crushed,
God, you will never reject.
18In your goodwill be kind to Zion,
and raise up Jerusalem’s walls.
19Then you will welcome sacrifices offered in righteousness, burnt offerings and whole offerings;
then young bulls will be brought up onto your altar.
fields.summary: After Nathan confronts him about Bathsheba, David pleads for mercy and cleansing, asking God to create in him a clean heart; God does not despise a broken spirit.

fields.title: Psalm 52
fields.body_html:
The boaster and the olive tree

For the music director. A maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite went and informed Saul, telling him, “David has gone to Ahimelech’s house.”

1Why brag about evil, you mighty warrior?
God’s loyal love goes on all day long.
2Your tongue devises ruin;
it cuts like a honed razor, you schemer of lies.
3You prefer evil to good,
and a lie to an honest word. Selah
4You love every word that devours,
you lying tongue.
5But God will bring you down for good;
he will seize you and drag you out of your tent,
and pull you up by the roots from the land of the living. Selah
6The righteous will see it and be filled with awe;
they will laugh at him and say,
7“Look at the man who would not take God as his fortress!
He relied on his great wealth
and looked for safety in the ruin he caused.”
8I, though, am like an olive tree in full leaf in God’s house;
I rely on God’s loyal love forever and ever.
9I will thank you forever for what you have done;
before your loyal people I will wait in hope on your name,
because it is good.
fields.summary: David denounces the boastful man who trusts in wealth and lies, while he is like an olive tree flourishing in God’s house.

fields.title: Psalm 53
fields.body_html:
Not one does good

For the music director. On mahalath. A maskil of David.

1Fools tell themselves, “There is no God.”
They are rotten through and through;
their wrongdoing is detestable.
Not one of them does good.
2From heaven God looks down on the human race
to see whether anyone is wise,
anyone who is looking for God.
3Everyone has turned away; all alike have gone bad.
No one does good,
not a single one.
4Have they learned nothing, these evildoers?
They devour my people as if they were eating bread,
and they never call on God.
5Terror gripped them there, where there had been nothing to fear,
for God scattered the bones of the army camped against you.
You brought them to shame, because God had thrown them aside.
6If only Zion would send Israel its rescue!
When God turns back the fortunes of his people,
let Jacob shout for joy and Israel be glad.
fields.summary: Fools say there is no God, and no one does good, yet God will scatter the enemies and restore God’s people.

fields.title: Psalm 54
fields.body_html:
God, save me by your name

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David, when the people of Ziph came and said to Saul, “David is hiding among us, is he not?”

1God, save me by your name;
by your strength take up my cause.
2God, listen to my prayer;
pay attention to what I am saying.
3For outsiders have risen up against me,
and violent people are hunting for my life;
they give God no thought. Selah
4But see, God comes to my aid;
the Lord is the one who holds my life up.
5He will turn back the harm on my enemies;
because you are faithful, wipe them out.
6I will offer you a sacrifice of my own free will;
LORD, I will thank you and honor your name, for it is good.
7For he has pulled me out of every trouble,
and my eyes have seen my enemies defeated.
fields.summary: When the Ziphites betray him, David asks God to save him and vindicate him, and promises to offer thanks.

fields.title: Psalm 55
fields.body_html:
Betrayed by a close friend

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David.

1God, listen to my prayer;
do not close your eyes to my plea.
2Listen to me and answer me.
My worries leave me no rest, and I groan aloud,
3at the shouting of the enemy
and the crushing weight of the wicked;
for they bring trouble crashing down on me,
and in their anger they nurse a grudge against me.
4My heart twists in pain inside me;
the dread of death has come down on me.
5Fear and trembling take hold of me;
I am wrapped in horror.
6I said, “If only I had a dove’s wings!
I would fly off and settle somewhere far away.
7See, I would run far off
and spend my nights in the wilderness. Selah
8I would hurry to a refuge of my own,
away from the raging wind and the storm.”
9Lord, bring them to nothing and split their speech,
because I have seen violence and quarreling all through the city.
10Day and night violence and strife make their rounds on its walls,
and evil and misery fill the city.
11Ruin is at its center;
cruelty and lies never leave its public square.
12The one who mocks me is not an enemy, or I could bear it;
the one who lords it over me is not someone who hates me,
or I could keep out of his way.
13But it is you, a man of my own standing,
my friend and my trusted companion,
14we used to share our hearts as friends,
and we walked with the crowd at the house of God.
15Let death catch them off guard;
let them drop alive into Sheol,
for evil lives in their homes and deep within them.
16But I will cry out to God,
and the LORD will come to save me.
17At evening, at morning and at noon I pour out my troubles and groan aloud,
and he hears me.
18He has ransomed my life and brought me safely out of the battle waged on me,
for many were lined up against me.
19God, enthroned since ancient times, will hear and bring them low,
for they never change their ways and they do not fear God. Selah
20My friend has raised his hand against those who were at peace with him;
he has broken his covenant.
21His talk was as smooth as cream, but his heart was set on war;
his words flowed more gently than oil, yet each was a drawn sword.
22Hand over to the LORD whatever weighs on you, and he will hold you up;
never will he allow the righteous to stumble and fall.
23But you, God, will send them down to the deepest pit;
killers and liars will not see even half their years.
As for me, I will trust in you.
fields.summary: David grieves that a close friend has betrayed him; he longs for wings to fly away, but casts his burden on God.

fields.title: Psalm 56
fields.body_html:
When I am afraid, I trust

For the music director. On yonath elem rechokim. Of David. A miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.

1God, show me grace, for people trample on me;
all day long they fight me and press me hard.
2My enemies hound me all day long;
many are fighting against me in their arrogance.
3On the day fear strikes,
I will rely on you.
4With God I celebrate his promise;
in God I have put my trust and will not be afraid.
What can mere flesh do to me?
5All day long they twist what I say;
every plan they make is for my harm.
6They band together and hide;
they watch my every step,
eager to take my life.
7Will they get away with such wickedness?
God, in anger throw down the nations.
8You yourself have kept count of my wanderings;
store my tears in your flask.
Are they not already in your record?
9When I call for help, my enemies will retreat;
this much I know, God is on my side.
10In God, whose promise I celebrate,
in the LORD, whose promise I celebrate,
11in God I have put my trust; I will not fear.
What can a mere human do to me?
12God, I am bound by the vows I made to you;
I will pay them with offerings of thanks to you.
13For you have rescued me from death
and kept my feet from slipping,
so that I can walk with God
in the light of the living.
fields.summary: When the Philistines seize him in Gath, David trusts God and is not afraid, for God keeps count of his tears.

fields.title: Psalm 57
fields.body_html:
Shelter in the shadow of your wings

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, when he fled from Saul into the cave.

1Show me grace, God, show me grace,
for I have made you my refuge;
I will shelter under the shadow of your wings
until the time of ruin is over.
2I call on God Most High,
the God who carries out his plan for me.
3He will reach down from heaven and rescue me,
and disgrace the one who hounds me;
God will send forth his loyal love and his faithfulness. Selah
4I am surrounded by lions; I must lie down among people who devour like beasts.
Their teeth are spear points and arrows,
their tongues a sharpened sword.
5God, be lifted high above the heavens;
let your glory spread over all the earth.
6They laid a net for my steps, and I sank down in despair;
they hollowed out a pit ahead of me,
and into it they fell. Selah
7My heart is firm, God, my heart is firm;
I will sing and play songs of praise.
8Rouse yourself, my soul!
Come awake, harp and lyre!
I will wake up the dawn.
9Lord, I will thank you before all peoples;
I will sing your praise in every nation.
10For your loyal love towers up to the heavens,
and your faithfulness rises to the clouds.
11God, be lifted high above the heavens;
let your glory spread over all the earth.
fields.summary: Hiding in the cave from Saul, David takes refuge in the shadow of God’s wings and resolves to sing God’s praise among the nations.

fields.title: Psalm 58
fields.body_html:
A God who judges the earth

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam.

1You gods, do you really speak what is right?
Do you judge human beings fairly?
2No, in your hearts you plan wrong,
and on earth your hands deal out violence by weight.
3From the womb the wicked have turned aside;
from birth those who tell lies have wandered off.
4Their poison is like a snake’s poison,
like a cobra that is deaf and stops up its ear,
5so that it does not hear the voice of the charmers,
however skilled the one who weaves the spell.
6God, smash the teeth in their mouths;
LORD, rip out the young lions’ fangs!
7Let them drain away like water running off;
when they take aim with their arrows, let the shafts be snapped.
8May they be like a snail that turns to slime as it moves,
like a baby born dead, who has not looked on the sun.
9Sooner than your pots can sense the thorn fire,
green or blazing, he will sweep it all away in a storm.
10The righteous will be glad when they see justice repaid;
they will bathe their feet in the wicked’s blood.
11Then people will say, “Yes, the righteous do receive a reward;
yes, a God does judge on the earth.”
fields.summary: David denounces unjust rulers and asks God to break their power, so that people will know that God judges the earth.

fields.title: Psalm 59
fields.body_html:
Rescue from enemies who prowl at night

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, from the time when Saul sent men to watch David’s house in order to kill him.

1Rescue me from my enemies, my God;
lift me high out of reach of those who rise against me.
2Rescue me from those who do evil;
save me from men who shed blood.
3Look, they lie in ambush for my life;
powerful men band together against me,
though I have not rebelled or sinned, LORD.
4Through no fault of mine they rush to take up their places.
Wake up, come to meet me, and look!
5LORD God of Armies, God of Israel,
rise up and call all the nations to account;
have no pity on any who plot evil in their treachery. Selah
6At nightfall they return,
snarling like dogs as they roam the city.
7Look how their mouths gush with insults;
their lips are swords,
for they say, “Who will hear?”
8But you, LORD, laugh at them;
you hold all the nations in derision.
9Against his strength I will keep watch for you,
for God is my high fortress.
10My God of loyal love will go before me;
God will let me look down on my foes.
11Do not kill them outright, in case my people forget;
by your power send them staggering and bring them low,
Lord, our shield.
12Every word from their lips is sin in their mouths;
let them be snared by their own pride,
for the cursing and lying they speak.
13Destroy them in your anger, destroy them until they are gone,
so that people will know that God rules over Jacob
to the ends of the earth. Selah
14At nightfall they return,
snarling like dogs as they roam the city.
15They roam about for food,
and if they are not filled, they stay out all night.
16But I will sing of your might,
and at daybreak I will shout for joy over your loyal love,
for you have been my high fortress,
a place to flee to when I was in trouble.
17My Strength, I will make music to you,
for God is my high fortress, my God of loyal love.
fields.summary: When Saul’s men watch his house, David asks God to rescue him from his enemies and praises God as his fortress.

fields.title: Psalm 60
fields.body_html:
Help against the foe after defeat

For the music director. On shushan eduth. A miktam of David, for teaching, when he fought against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab came back and struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.

1God, you have thrown us off and burst through our walls.
You have been angry; turn to us again!
2You made the land shudder and tore it apart;
mend its cracks, for it is giving way.
3You let your people see hard things;
you made us drink a wine that sent us reeling.
4For those who fear you, you have raised a banner to rally to,
out of reach of the bow. Selah
5So that those you love may be set free,
bring rescue with your right hand and answer me!
6God has spoken from his holy place: “I will rejoice
as I share out Shechem
and mark off the Valley of Succoth.
7Gilead belongs to me, Manasseh is mine;
Ephraim is the helmet on my head,
Judah the staff of my rule.
8Moab is my washing bowl;
on Edom I toss my sandal;
Philistia, raise your shout to me!”
9Who will take me into the walled city?
Who will guide me all the way to Edom?
10Is it not you, God, who rejected us
and no longer march out with our armies?
11Help us against the enemy,
for any rescue that people can bring is useless.
12With God on our side we will fight with courage;
he is the one who will crush our foes underfoot.
fields.summary: After defeat, the people ask God to restore them, and God promises to divide the land and humble their enemies.

fields.title: Psalm 61
fields.body_html:
Lead me to the rock higher than I

For the music director. On a stringed instrument. Of David.

1God, hear my loud cry;
pay attention to my prayer.
2From the far edge of the earth I call to you while my heart fails;
lead me up onto a rock too high for me to climb.
3For you have been my shelter,
a strong tower to hold off the enemy.
4Let me live as a guest in your tent for all time;
let me find refuge under the cover of your wings. Selah
5God, you have heard the promises I made;
you have granted me the share that belongs to those who honor your name.
6Add days upon days to the king’s life;
may his years go on through generation after generation.
7May he sit on his throne in God’s presence forever;
let loyal love and faithfulness be appointed as his guards.
8Then I will make music to your name for all time
as I keep my vows day after day.
fields.summary: From the ends of the earth David cries out to God, his rock and refuge, and prays for the king’s long life.

fields.title: Psalm 62
fields.body_html:
Wait quietly for God alone

For the music director. According to Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

1I am quiet before God alone;
my rescue comes from him.
2Only he is my rock who saves me, my high fortress;
I will not be badly shaken.
3How long will you all rush at one man to batter him down,
as if he were a leaning wall,
a fence about to fall?
4Their only plan is to bring him down from his high place; they love what is false.
Their lips speak blessing
while inside they curse. Selah
5Be still before God alone, my soul,
for he is the source of my hope.
6Only he is my rock who saves me, my high fortress;
I will not be shaken.
7On God rest my rescue and my honor;
the rock of my strength and my shelter are in God.
8People, rely on him in every season;
empty your hearts out before him.
God is our shelter. Selah
9Ordinary people are only a breath, and the great are a lie;
put on the scales, they rise;
all together they weigh less than a breath.
10Do not lean on what you gain by force, or let robbery fill you with empty hopes;
if wealth multiplies,
do not give your heart to it.
11God has spoken one thing,
and I have heard it twice over:
that strength is God’s,
12and to you, Lord, belongs loyal love;
for you pay all people back for what they have done.
fields.summary: David waits in quiet for God alone, his rock and salvation, and urges people to trust in God at all times rather than in wealth.

fields.title: Psalm 63
fields.body_html:
Thirsting for God in a dry land

A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.

1God, you are my God, and I search hard for you.
My whole self thirsts for you; my body aches for you
in a dry and worn-out land with no water.
2So I have gazed on you in the holy place
and seen your might and your glory.
3Your loyal love is worth more than life,
so my lips will sing your praise.
4So I will bless you all my life;
I will raise my hands as I call on your name.
5I will be filled as with a feast of rich food,
and with shouts of joy on my lips my mouth will sing your praise.
6When I call you to mind as I lie in bed,
I muse on you through the hours of the night.
7You have come to my help,
and under the shadow of your wings I sing out for joy.
8I hold fast to you;
your right hand keeps me safe.
9But those who hunt my life to ruin it
will sink into the lowest places of the earth.
10The sword will have them in its grip,
and jackals will take them as their share.
11But the king will find his joy in God;
all who take their oaths in his name will celebrate,
while liars will have their mouths shut.
fields.summary: In the wilderness David thirsts for God, whose loyal love is better than life, and clings to God.

fields.title: Psalm 64
fields.body_html:
God’s arrows against secret plotters

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1God, listen to me as I pour out my complaint;
keep me safe from the enemy I dread.
2Shelter me from the wicked when they plot together in secret,
from the restless crowd of those who do evil,
3who grind their tongues sharp as a sword
and fit bitter words to the bow like arrows,
4to fire from hiding at the blameless;
all at once they let fly, without any fear.
5They make each other bold in their evil scheme
and talk of setting traps where none can see;
they say, “Who will notice them?”
6They search out crimes and say,
“We have a flawless scheme, thoroughly thought out!”
How deep are the thoughts and the heart of a human being!
7But God lets fly an arrow at them;
in an instant they are wounded.
8Their own words trip them and bring them down;
everyone who sees them shakes their head.
9Then everyone is struck with awe;
they announce what God has done
and think deeply about his deeds.
10May the righteous be glad in the LORD and make him their refuge;
may all whose hearts are true give praise.
fields.summary: David asks God to protect him from the secret plots of evildoers, whom God will strike down.

fields.title: Psalm 65
fields.body_html:
Praise for the God who sends rain

For the music director. A psalm of David. A song.

1For you, God, in Zion, silence is praise,
and to you vows will be kept.
2You hear prayer;
all people will come before you.
3Wrongdoings overwhelm me,
but you cover over our rebellions.
4How blessed are those whom you choose and draw close, to dwell in your courts!
May we feast on the goodness of your house,
your holy temple.
5With deeds that inspire awe you answer us in righteousness, God of our rescue,
trusted by all the ends of the earth
and by those on the far-off seas,
6who fixed the mountains in place by his power,
wearing might like a belt,
7who quiets the thunder of the seas and the crash of their waves,
and the uproar of the nations.
8Those who live at the far edges of the world stand in awe of your wonders;
you make the lands of sunrise and sunset sing for joy.
9You pay a visit to the earth and soak it with rain; you make it richly fertile.
God’s channel is brimming with water;
you supply people with grain,
for this is how you have prepared the land.
10Pouring water into its furrows and pressing down its ridges,
you make the soil soft with rain showers
and bless all that springs up from it.
11You set a crown on the year of your goodness,
and the tracks of your chariot drip with richness.
12Even the pastures of the open country drip with plenty,
and the hills put on joy like a belt.
13Flocks cover the pastures like clothing,
and grain wraps the valleys;
they cry out in triumph, yes, they sing!
fields.summary: God answers prayer, forgives, and crowns the year with abundance, making the meadows and valleys shout for joy.

fields.title: Psalm 66
fields.body_html:
Come and see what God has done

For the music director. A song. A psalm.

1Raise a shout to God, all the earth!
2Make music to the honor of his name;
give him praise that is full of glory!
3Say to God, “How fearsome are your deeds!
Because your strength is so great,
your enemies cower and fawn before you.
4The whole earth bows low to you and sings to you;
they make music to your name.” Selah
5Come and look at the works of God,
how fearsome his dealings are with humankind!
6He changed the sea into dry ground;
they crossed the river on foot.
There let us rejoice in him!
7He reigns in his power forever,
and his eyes watch closely over the nations.
Let no rebels raise themselves up. Selah
8Peoples of the world, bless our God,
and make the sound of his praise ring out,
9the one who keeps us alive
and has not let our feet stumble.
10For you have put us to the test, God;
you have refined us the way silver is refined.
11You led us into the trap;
you laid a heavy weight on our backs.
12You let mere mortals ride roughshod over our heads;
we came through fire and water,
but you led us out into overflowing plenty.
13I will enter your house with whole burnt offerings
and keep my vows to you,
14the promises that burst from my lips,
that my mouth made in my time of distress.
15I will offer you burnt offerings of fattened animals, along with the smoke of rams rising to you;
I will sacrifice bulls together with goats. Selah
16Come, listen, all who revere God;
let me recount the things he has done for me.
17With my own mouth I called to him,
and praise to lift him high was ready under my tongue.
18The Lord would not have heard me
if I had kept wrongdoing in my heart.
19Yet God has indeed heard me;
he has paid close attention as I prayed.
20Blessed be God,
who has not pushed my prayer aside
or taken his loyal love away from me!
fields.summary: All the earth is called to praise God for awesome deeds, such as bringing Israel through the sea and through trials, and the psalmist tells what God has done for him.

fields.title: Psalm 67
fields.body_html:
May all the peoples praise you, God

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.

1May God show us grace and bless us;
may he let the light of his face shine on us. Selah
2Then the earth will know your ways,
and every nation your power to save.
3May the peoples give you thanks, God;
may every people give you thanks!
4Let the nations celebrate and shout with joy,
because you judge the peoples fairly
and lead the nations across the earth. Selah
5May the peoples give you thanks, God;
may every people give you thanks!
6The earth has brought forth its crops;
God, our own God, will bless us.
7God is going to bless us,
and all the far corners of the earth will hold him in awe.
fields.summary: The people pray that God will bless them so that all nations will know God’s ways and praise God.

fields.title: Psalm 68
fields.body_html:
God marches from Sinai to Zion

For the music director. Of David. A psalm. A song.

1Let God rise up and his enemies scatter;
let all who hate him run from his presence.
2Blow them away as smoke is blown away;
as wax melts in front of the flames,
may the wicked come to nothing in God’s presence.
3But let the righteous be glad and celebrate before God;
let them be overjoyed.
4Sing to God, make music to his name;
prepare a highway for the one who rides through the deserts.
The LORD is his name; celebrate before him!
5From his holy dwelling
God acts as father to orphans and defender of widows.
6God gives the lonely a home to live in;
he leads prisoners out into well-being,
but rebels stay in a sunbaked land.
7God, you went out at the head of your people;
you strode through the desert. Selah
8The earth trembled and the sky streamed with rain before God,
the God of Sinai;
before God, Israel’s God.
9God, you sent showers of generous rain;
when your land was worn out, you restored it.
10Your flock found a home there;
out of your goodness, God, you made ready what the afflicted needed.
11The Lord speaks the word,
and a great army of women spreads the good news:
12“Kings with their armies run, they run away,
and the woman who stayed at home shares out the spoil.”
13Even if you men lie among the sheep pens,
there are a dove’s wings sheathed in silver,
its feathers shining with pale gold.
14When the Almighty scattered kings across the land,
snow came down on Zalmon.
15Mount Bashan is a mighty mountain;
Mount Bashan is a mountain of many peaks.
16Why do you glare in envy, you many-peaked mountains,
at the mountain God longed for as his home?
There the LORD will live for all time.
17God’s chariots number twenty thousand, thousands more again;
the Lord is among them, and Sinai has come into the holy place.
18You climbed to the heights and led away a band of captives;
you accepted tribute from human beings,
even from those who rebelled, so that the LORD God could make a home there.
19Blessed be the Lord, who carries our load day after day,
the God who saves us. Selah
20This God of ours is a God of rescues;
the Lord GOD holds the ways of escape from death.
21Yes, God will smash the skulls of his enemies,
the hairy scalps of those who keep walking in their guilt.
22The Lord has spoken: “I will fetch them back from Bashan,
fetch them back from the deepest sea,
23so that you may plunge your feet in blood,
and your dogs’ tongues may have their share of the enemy.”
24Your solemn marches have been seen, God,
the marches of my God, my King, as he enters the holy place.
25The singers lead the way, the players of strings follow,
and all around them young women beat their tambourines.
26Bless God in the great assemblies;
bless the LORD, you who spring from Israel’s fountain.
27There goes little Benjamin in the lead,
the princes of Judah in their crowded ranks,
then Zebulun’s princes and Naphtali’s princes.
28Your God has decreed your strength, Israel.
Show your might, God,
as you have acted for us before.
29On account of your temple high over Jerusalem,
kings will carry tribute to you.
30Rebuke the beast that lurks among the reeds, that herd of bulls with the calves of the nations,
until they come bowing low with bars of silver.
God has scattered the peoples who love war.
31High officials will come out of Egypt;
Cush will quickly lift its hands in prayer to God.
32Sing to God, all you kingdoms on earth;
make music for the Lord. Selah
33Sing to the one who rides across the ancient heavens, the heaven of heavens;
listen, he lets his voice ring out, his voice of power.
34Declare that power belongs to God!
His majesty rests over Israel;
his might is in the clouds.
35God, you inspire awe from your holy places;
Israel’s God is the one who gives his people strength and might.
Blessed be God!
fields.summary: God rises up and enemies scatter; God, father of the fatherless, leads the people from Sinai to the sanctuary, and the kingdoms of the earth are called to sing to God.

fields.title: Psalm 69
fields.body_html:
Rescue me from the deep waters

For the music director. On shoshannim. Of David.

1Rescue me, God,
for the water has risen to my throat.
2I am sinking in deep mud with nothing to stand on;
I have gone down into deep water, and the current is carrying me away.
3I am exhausted from calling out; my throat is burning dry.
My eyes have grown dim
from watching for my God.
4There are more people hating me for no reason than hairs on my head;
strong are the ones who seek my ruin, my enemies with their lies.
Am I to repay what I never took?
5God, you know my foolishness;
none of my guilt is hidden from you.
6May no one who waits for you be shamed through me, Lord GOD of Armies;
may no one who seeks you be humiliated through me,
God of Israel.
7Because of you I have carried scorn;
humiliation covers my face.
8My own brothers treat me as a stranger;
to my mother’s sons I am an outsider.
9Passion for your house burns me up,
and the taunts aimed at you have landed on me.
10I wept and went without food,
and for that they mocked me.
11When I put on sackcloth for clothing,
they made me the butt of their sayings.
12The people who sit at the city gate gossip about me,
and drunkards sing songs mocking me.
13But as for me, I pray to you, LORD, at a time you will accept;
God, in your great loyal love,
answer me with your faithful rescue.
14Pull me out of the mud, and do not let me go under;
let me be snatched away from those who hate me, out of the deep water.
15Do not let the flood waters wash over me or the deep gulp me down,
or the pit shut its mouth on me.
16Answer me, LORD, because your loyal love is good;
in your great compassion, turn toward me.
17Do not turn away from me, your servant;
I am hard pressed, so be quick to answer me.
18Come close to me and buy me back;
set me free because of my enemies.
19You know the scorn I bear, my shame and my disgrace;
every one of my enemies is in your sight.
20Scorn has broken my heart, leaving me sick;
I hoped someone would pity me, but no one did,
that someone would comfort me, but there was no one to be found.
21They put bitter poison into my food,
and for my thirst they handed me sour wine.
22May the meal set before them become a trap for them,
a snare when they feel secure.
23May their eyes grow dim until they cannot see;
make their bodies tremble without end.
24Pour your fury out on them;
let your blazing anger catch up with them.
25Let their camp become a wasteland,
with nobody living in their tents.
26For they chase down the one you have struck,
and gossip about the pain of the people you have wounded.
27Add guilt to their guilt;
let them have no share in your saving justice.
28May their names be erased from the book of life,
never to be entered with the righteous.
29But I am poor and hurting;
let your saving help, God, lift me up to safety.
30With a song I will praise God’s name
and proclaim his greatness with thanksgiving.
31That will delight the LORD more than an ox
or a young bull with full-grown horns and hooves.
32The humble will see it and be glad;
you who seek God, take heart and live!
33For the LORD hears the poor
and does not look down on his people in chains.
34Let the heavens and the earth praise him,
the seas and all that swarms in them.
35For God will rescue Zion and build up Judah’s towns again;
his people will live there and hold it as their own,
36the descendants of his servants will receive it as their inheritance,
and all who love his name will make their home in it.
fields.summary: Sinking in deep water and hated without cause, the psalmist pleads for rescue and asks God to repay his enemies.

fields.title: Psalm 70
fields.body_html:
Hurry, God, and help me

For the music director. Of David. For remembrance.

1God, come and rescue me!
LORD, be quick to help me!
2Let those who are out to take my life be shamed and confounded;
let those who want me hurt be driven back in disgrace.
3Let those who crow “Aha! Aha!”
retreat because of their own disgrace.
4But may all who look for you be glad and take delight in you,
and let all who love your saving help keep saying, “God is great!”
5As for me, I am poor and in need; God, come to me quickly!
You are my helper and the one who sets me free;
LORD, do not hold back!
fields.summary: David asks God to hurry to save him, and to let all who seek God rejoice.

fields.title: Psalm 71
fields.body_html:
Do not leave me now I am old

1LORD, I have made you my refuge;
never let me be disgraced.
2Because you are just, rescue me and set me free;
bend down to listen to me, and save me.
3Be a rock I can live in, a place I can always come to.
You have given the order to save me,
since you yourself are my crag and my stronghold.
4My God, pull me out of the clutches of the wicked,
out of the grip of the unjust and the cruel.
5For you are my hope,
Lord GOD; I have trusted in you since I was young.
6I have leaned on you from birth;
it was you who drew me from my mother’s body.
I will praise you without ceasing.
7To many I have become a sign that makes them wonder,
but you are my strong shelter.
8My mouth is full of praise for you;
all day long I speak of your glory.
9Do not throw me aside now that I am old;
do not abandon me as my strength gives out.
10For my enemies are talking about me;
those who are waiting to take my life are plotting together,
11and they say, “God has abandoned him.
Go after him and grab him,
for no one will save him.”
12God, do not stay far away from me;
my God, come quickly and help me!
13Let my accusers be put to shame and brought to nothing;
let those who want to hurt me be wrapped in scorn and dishonor.
14As for me, I will never stop hoping;
I will add to your praise again and again.
15My mouth will tell of your righteousness
and of your saving help all day long,
though they are more than I can count.
16I will come and tell of the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD;
I will call to mind your righteousness, yours and no one else’s.
17God, you have been teaching me since I was young,
and I am telling of your wonders still.
18Now that I am old and gray, God, do not abandon me,
not until I have told the generation after me what your arm has done,
and made your power known to all who are yet to be born.
19God, your righteousness rises as high as the heavens;
you have done mighty things.
God, who is there like you?
20You have made me see many troubles and hard times,
but you will bring me back to life,
and raise me once more out of the deep places of the earth.
21Make me greater than before,
and turn to comfort me once more.
22I in turn will thank you to the music of the harp; my God, I will praise your faithfulness.
With the lyre I will play for you,
Holy One of Israel.
23My lips will ring out with joy as I sing your praise,
and so will my whole self, which you have set free.
24All day long my tongue will speak of your righteousness,
for the people who sought my hurt are ashamed and humbled.
fields.summary: From his youth to old age the psalmist has relied on God, and he asks God not to forsake him now that he is gray.

fields.title: Psalm 72
fields.body_html:
A prayer for the king’s reign

Of Solomon.

1God, grant the king your justice,
and the king’s son your righteousness.
2May he govern your people rightly,
and your poor with fairness.
3May the mountains yield well-being for the people,
and the hills bring it through righteousness.
4May he defend the poor among the people
and bring rescue to needy families;
may he break the oppressor in pieces.
5May people stand in awe of you as long as there is a sun and a moon,
from one generation to the next.
6May he be like rain falling on a cut field,
like showers soaking the land.
7In his days may the righteous thrive,
and peace overflow until the moon is gone.
8May his rule stretch from sea to sea,
from the River to the far ends of the earth.
9Let the nomads of the desert kneel before him,
and let his foes lick the dust.
10Let Tarshish and the coastlands send their kings with tribute;
let the kings of Sheba and Seba bring him presents.
11Let every king bow low before him
and every nation be his servant.
12For he rescues the needy when they cry out,
and the poor who have no one else to stand by them.
13He feels for the weak and the needy,
and he saves the lives of those in need.
14He sets them free from cruelty and violence;
their lives are of great worth in his sight.
15May the king live! Let him receive Sheba’s gold;
let prayer be made for him always,
and blessing asked for him all day.
16Let grain grow thick across the land, right up to the hilltops;
let its harvest rustle like the trees of Lebanon,
and let city people spring up like grass in the fields.
17May his name live on forever,
his fame spread as long as the sun shines.
May all nations ask to be blessed as he is blessed, and call him happy.
18Blessed be the LORD God, Israel’s God;
only he works wonders.
19Blessed be his glorious name for all time;
may his glory fill all the earth.
Amen and Amen.
20Here end the prayers of David son of Jesse.
fields.summary: A prayer for the king asks that he judge the poor with justice, rule from sea to sea, and that all nations be blessed through him.

fields.title: Psalm 73
fields.body_html:
Envy of the wicked, and nearness to God

A psalm of Asaph.

1God really is good to Israel,
to people with a clean heart.
2But I came close to losing my footing;
my steps very nearly slid out from under me.
3I had grown jealous of the proud,
watching wicked people do well.
4They die without pain,
and their bodies are plump and healthy.
5They are free from the hardships others carry;
they are not plagued like the rest of humankind.
6So they wear pride like a chain around the neck,
and violence wraps them like a robe.
7Their eyes bulge from their fat faces;
the fancies of their minds run past all limits.
8They jeer and talk of evil;
from on high they speak of crushing others.
9Their mouths speak as if they owned heaven;
their tongues go swaggering through the land.
10So his people turn their way
and gulp down their words like water from a full cup.
11And they ask, “What can God know?
Is the Most High aware of anything?”
12So these are the wicked:
never troubled, always growing richer.
13So it was for nothing that I kept my heart clean
and washed my hands to show I was innocent.
14I have been beaten down the whole day long,
and corrected afresh each morning.
15Had I resolved to speak like this,
I would have broken faith with the family of your children.
16So I tried to make sense of it,
but it seemed a weary task to me,
17until I entered God’s holy place;
then I saw where they will end.
18In fact, you have set them where the footing is slick,
and you let them crash into ruin.
19In an instant they are ruined!
Sudden terrors make an end of them.
20They are like a dream once the sleeper wakes;
Lord, when you stir, you will scorn them as mere shadows.
21When my heart had turned sour
and I felt stabbed deep inside,
22I was a fool and knew nothing;
in your presence I was no better than an animal.
23Even so, I am with you at all times;
you have taken me by the right hand.
24You lead me by your wise advice,
and at the end you will take me up in glory.
25Who else is there for me in heaven?
And having you, I want nothing on earth.
26Though body and heart wear out,
God is the rock my heart rests on and the share that is mine forever.
27Those who move far from you are lost;
everyone who deserts you to love another, you cut off.
28As for me, being close to God is my good;
in the Lord GOD I have found my shelter,
and I will tell of all you have done.
fields.summary: Asaph nearly stumbled when he saw the wicked prosper, until he entered God’s sanctuary and understood their end; God is his portion forever.

fields.title: Psalm 74
fields.body_html:
Remember your people and your ruined sanctuary

A maskil of Asaph.

1God, why have you cast us off for good?
Why does your anger burn and smoke against the flock you tend?
2Remember your people, whom you made your own long ago,
the tribe you bought back to be your inheritance;
remember Mount Zion, where you made your home.
3Come, make your way over these ruins that never end;
the enemy has smashed everything in the holy place.
4Your enemies roared in the middle of the place where you met with us;
they set up their own banners as signs.
5They seemed like woodcutters lifting their axes
against a dense stand of trees.
6And now they hack away at all its carved panels
with hatchets and hammers.
7They set your sanctuary on fire;
they dragged the home of your name down to the ground and defiled it.
8In their hearts they said, “Let us beat them down, all of them!”
They set fire to all God’s meeting places throughout the land.
9We see no signs for us anymore;
no prophet is left,
and no one among us can say how long it will be.
10How long, God, will the enemy jeer?
Will the foe go on insulting your name forever?
11Why do you hold your hand still, your strong right hand?
Pull it out of your cloak and make an end of them!
12But God has been my King since ancient times,
bringing rescue in the middle of the earth.
13By your power you tore the sea in two;
you crushed the heads of the dragons in the water.
14You shattered the heads of Leviathan
and gave it as food to the creatures of the desert.
15You broke open springs and brooks;
you made rivers that always flowed run dry.
16The day is yours, and the night is yours as well;
you set the moon and the sun in their places.
17You fixed every boundary of the earth;
summer and winter are your handiwork.
18Remember this, LORD: the enemy has jeered at you,
and a foolish people has insulted your name.
19Do not let your dove fall prey to the greedy beasts;
do not leave your suffering people forgotten for good.
20Pay heed to the covenant,
because every dark corner of the land is filled with places of violence.
21Do not let the downtrodden go back ashamed;
may the poor and the needy give praise to your name.
22Rise up, God! Take up your own case;
keep in mind the insults the fool throws at you all day long.
23Do not ignore the shouting of your enemies,
the din of those who rise against you, which never stops rising.
fields.summary: The psalmist mourns the enemies’ destruction of the sanctuary and asks God to remember the covenant and rise up.

fields.title: Psalm 75
fields.body_html:
God is judge: he lowers and lifts

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph. A song.

1We thank you, God, we thank you; your name is close to us,
and people speak of the marvels you have done.
2“When the time I have fixed has come,
I will judge with fairness.
3The earth and everyone on it may sway and melt,
but I have set its pillars firm. Selah
4I tell the proud, ‘Stop your boasting,’
and the wicked, ‘Do not toss your horn high.’
5Do not raise your horn against the heights,
or talk with a stiff and insolent neck.”
6For it is not from the east or the west,
nor from the desert, that a person is raised up,
7but God is the judge:
he lays one person low and lifts another up.
8For the LORD holds a cup in his hand, and the wine in it foams, richly spiced; he pours from it,
and every wicked person on earth will have to drain it, dregs and all.
9But I will never stop telling of it;
I will make music to the God of Jacob.
10I will hack off every horn the wicked raise,
but those who do right will have their horns lifted high.
fields.summary: The people give thanks to God, who judges in due time, humbling some and lifting up others.

fields.title: Psalm 76
fields.body_html:
God breaks the weapons at Zion

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.

1God has made himself known in Judah;
his name stands high in Israel.
2His lair is set in Salem,
his den in Zion.
3There he shattered the fiery shafts of the bow,
shield and sword and all the gear of battle. Selah
4You shine with light,
in greater splendor than the mountains of prey.
5The brave were stripped bare; they dropped into their final sleep,
and not one of the warriors could find a hand to raise.
6When you rebuked them, God of Jacob,
chariot and horse sank into a stupor.
7You, yes, you are to be feared!
When your anger blazes,
who can hold out in your presence?
8From heaven you announced your verdict;
the earth was afraid and fell silent,
9when God stood up to give judgment
and to rescue all the lowly on earth. Selah
10Even human fury will end in praise for you;
what is left of it you will tie on like a belt.
11Vow to the LORD your God, and keep what you vow;
let all who surround him
bring tribute to the One who inspires fear.
12He cuts short the breath of princes;
the kings of the earth stand in fear of him.
fields.summary: God is renowned in Judah and breaks the weapons of war; God judges to save the humble of the earth.

fields.title: Psalm 77
fields.body_html:
Remembering God’s way through the sea

For the music director. On Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.

1I raise my voice to God and cry out;
I raise my voice to God, so that he will listen to me.
2When trouble came I looked for the Lord;
all night I kept my hands raised and did not tire,
and I would take no comfort.
3I think of God and groan;
I ponder, and my spirit sinks. Selah
4You would not let my eyelids close;
I was too shaken to say a word.
5I turned my mind to days gone by,
to years long past.
6I call to mind the songs I sang at night;
I talk with my own heart,
and my spirit searches for answers:
7Will the Lord turn away for all time,
and never again show kindness?
8Is his loyal love gone for good?
Is his promise finished for every generation to come?
9Has God forgotten how to show mercy?
Has he let anger lock away his compassion? Selah
10Then I said: This is what pierces me,
that the Most High’s right hand is not what it was.
11I will call to mind what the LORD has done;
yes, I will remember the marvels you worked long ago.
12I will reflect on all your work
and turn over in my mind what you have done.
13God, your way is holy.
Is there a god anywhere as great as God?
14You are the God whose deeds are marvels;
you have shown the nations how strong you are.
15With your strong arm you set your people free,
the families of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
16God, when the waters caught sight of you,
when the waters saw you, they twisted in fear;
even the deep sea quaked.
17The clouds poured down rain,
the skies rumbled with thunder,
and your arrows flashed this way and that.
18Your thunder rumbled in the whirlwind;
flashes of lightning lit the world;
the earth shook and quaked.
19Your road went through the sea
and your track through the deep waters,
but no trace of your steps could be seen.
20Like a shepherd with his sheep you guided your people,
through Moses and Aaron.
fields.summary: In distress the psalmist wonders whether God has forgotten to be gracious, then remembers God’s wonders of old, when God led the people through the sea.

fields.title: Psalm 78
fields.body_html:
Tell the next generation: grace despite rebellion

A maskil of Asaph.

1My people, listen closely to my instruction;
bend your ears to what I say.
2I will open my mouth to speak a parable;
I will bring out the hidden lessons of long ago,
3what we have heard and learned,
what our forebears passed on to us.
4We will not conceal them from their children;
we will pass on to those who come after us the deeds for which the LORD is praised,
his strength, and the marvels he has worked.
5He laid down a solemn charge in Jacob and set up instruction in Israel;
he ordered our forebears
to teach these to their children,
6so that those born later, children not yet born, would know them,
and would grow up and tell them to their own children,
7so that they would rest their hope on God,
remember the works of God,
and keep his commands,
8and would not be like their ancestors, a defiant and rebellious generation,
whose hearts were never steady
and whose spirits did not stay true to God.
9The Ephraimites, armed and skilled with the bow,
fled when the day of battle came.
10They failed to keep the covenant God had made
and would not follow his instruction.
11They let his deeds slip from memory,
the marvels they had seen him work.
12In full view of their ancestors he worked marvels
in Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
13He split the sea in two and took them across,
piling up the waters in a heap.
14By day he guided them with the cloud,
and all through the night with the glow of fire.
15He broke open rocks in the desert
and let them drink water as plentiful as the ocean depths.
16He drew streams out of the cliff
and sent water rushing down like rivers.
17Yet they kept on sinning against him,
defying the Most High in the parched desert.
18In their hearts they challenged God,
insisting on food to feed their cravings.
19They spoke against God
