and said, “Can God lay out a meal in the desert?
20Yes, he hit the rock and water burst out and torrents swept along;
but is he able to give bread too,
or to put meat before his people?”
21So when the LORD heard it, he was enraged;
fire blazed up against Jacob,
and his anger rose against Israel,
22because they had no faith in God
and did not rely on his power to save.
23Even so, he gave orders to the clouds above
and threw open the doors of the sky,
24and showered manna on them for food;
he handed them grain from heaven.
25Everyone ate the bread of the mighty ones;
he sent them supplies until they had their fill.
26He set the east wind moving across the sky
and steered the south wind by his power.
27He showered meat on them as thick as dust,
birds on the wing as many as the grains of sand by the sea.
28He brought them down in the middle of their camp,
all around their tents.
29They ate and were more than satisfied;
he gave them what they longed for.
30They had not yet turned away from their craving;
they were still chewing their food,
31when the anger of God blazed against them;
he slew the best-fed among them
and brought down the young men of Israel.
32Even so they went on sinning;
in spite of his marvels they would not believe.
33So he let their days drift away like vapor
and ended their years in sudden dread.
34Whenever he struck them down, they would look for him;
they would turn back and search hard for God.
35They recalled that their Rock was God,
that God Most High was the one who had set them free.
36But their words to him were only flattery;
with their tongues they lied to him,
37and their hearts were not set on him;
they did not stay true to his covenant.
38Yet he was full of compassion; he covered their guilt and did not wipe them out.
Many a time he held back his anger
and did not let all his fury loose.
39He remembered that they were only flesh,
a breeze that blows past and does not come back.
40How many times they defied him in the wilderness
and caused him grief in the barren land!
41Once more they challenged God
and wounded the Holy One of Israel.
42They forgot his power
and the day he bought them free from the enemy,
43when he displayed his signs in Egypt
and his marvels in the fields around Zoan.
44He changed their rivers into blood,
and their running water could not be drunk.
45He sent swarms of insects among them to eat them up,
and frogs to bring them to ruin.
46He handed their harvest over to the grasshopper
and all they had worked for to the swarming locust.
47He struck their vines dead with hail
and froze their sycamore-figs with ice.
48He left their cattle at the mercy of the hail,
and their herds to the flashing fire.
49He let loose on them the heat of his anger,
rage and fury and distress,
a troop of angels bringing disaster.
50He cleared a road for his anger;
he did not hold them back from death,
but handed their lives over to the plague.
51He cut down every firstborn in Egypt,
the eldest sons, the first of their strength, throughout the tents of Ham.
52Then he moved his people out like sheep
and herded them like a flock across the wilderness.
53He kept them safe as he led them, and they were not afraid;
but the sea closed over their enemies.
54He led them to his sacred land,
to these mountains that his own power had gained.
55He pushed out nations ahead of them
and shared out their land by measuring line as a possession;
he gave the tribes of Israel their tents to live in.
56Still they challenged God Most High and defied him;
they did not keep his decrees.
57They turned away and broke faith as their ancestors did;
they went crooked like a warped bow.
58They angered him with their hilltop shrines,
and by their idols roused his jealous anger.
59When God heard, his anger blazed,
and he cast Israel off entirely.
60He deserted the sanctuary at Shiloh,
the tent where he had made his home among people.
61He let his might be carried off as a captive,
his glory into enemy hands.
62He handed his people over to the sword;
he raged against his own inheritance.
63Their young men were eaten up by fire;
no one sang the wedding song for their young women.
64Their priests were cut down by the sword,
and the widows they left could not raise a lament.
65Then the Lord roused himself like a sleeper waking,
like a warrior shouting as the wine stirs him.
66He beat his enemies back
and put them to lasting shame.
67He turned down the tent of Joseph;
Ephraim’s tribe was not the one he chose,
68instead he picked out the tribe of Judah
and Mount Zion, which he holds dear.
69He made his sanctuary as lofty as the heavens
and as firm as the earth, which he founded to last forever.
70He singled out David, his servant,
and called him away from the sheepfolds,
71from walking behind the nursing ewes he brought him
to care for Jacob, his people,
and for Israel, his own possession, as their shepherd.
72He cared for them as a shepherd with an honest heart
and led them with skillful hands.
fields.summary: Asaph tells the next generation of God’s wonders in Egypt and the wilderness and of Israel’s repeated rebellion, and how God chose Judah, Zion and David to shepherd the people.

fields.title: Psalm 79
fields.body_html:
A plea for ruined Jerusalem

A psalm of Asaph.

1God, the nations have broken into the land that is your own;
they have made your holy temple unclean
and turned Jerusalem into piles of rubble.
2They have thrown out the bodies of your servants for the birds of the air to eat,
and the flesh of your faithful people for the wild animals.
3They have spilled their blood like water on every side of Jerusalem,
and no one was left to bury them.
4We have become a disgrace in our neighbors’ eyes,
laughed at and scorned by everyone near us.
5How long, LORD? Will you be angry without end?
Must your jealousy keep burning like fire?
6Pour out your fury on the nations that have not known you,
on the kingdoms
that never call on your name,
7for they have swallowed up Jacob
and left his homeland desolate.
8Do not count against us the wrongs of those who came before us;
let your compassion hurry to meet us,
for we are at the end of our strength.
9God who saves us, come to our help for the glory of your name.
Rescue us and cover our sins, to honor your name.
10Why should the nations get to say, “Where is their God?”
Let the nations see you pay back the blood of your servants that was shed,
and let us see it with our own eyes.
11May the groaning of the captives reach you;
with the might of your arm,
spare those who are marked for death.
12Pay back our neighbors seven times over, right into their laps,
for the scorn they have heaped on you, Lord.
13Then we, your people, the flock you tend, will thank you for all time;
to every generation
we will tell of your praise.
fields.summary: The nations have defiled the temple and laid Jerusalem in ruins, and the people ask God to forgive and to avenge them.

fields.title: Psalm 80
fields.body_html:
Restore your vine, God of Armies

For the music director. On shoshannim eduth. Of Asaph. A psalm.

1Turn your ear to us, Shepherd of Israel,
guiding Joseph like a flock!
Throned above the cherubim, blaze out in splendor!
2Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh,
rouse your strength
and come to rescue us!
3God, bring us back!
Turn the light of your face on us, and we will be saved.
4LORD God of Armies,
how long will you seethe with anger even while your people pray?
5You have made tears their food,
and given them full measures of tears to drink.
6You make us something our neighbors fight over,
and our enemies sneer at us among themselves.
7God of Armies, bring us back!
Turn the light of your face on us, and we will be saved.
8You lifted a vine out of Egypt;
you expelled nations to plant it.
9You prepared the soil to receive it;
it put down its roots and covered the land.
10Its shadow spread over the mountains,
and its branches over the giant cedars.
11It stretched its branches as far as the sea,
and its shoots to the River.
12Why did you break down the walls around it?
Now everyone who walks along the road picks its grapes.
13Wild boars from the forest tear it up,
and the creatures of the open country feed on it.
14God of Armies, please come back!
Gaze down from heaven and see;
care for this vine,
15the root your right hand planted,
the son you raised to strength for yourself.
16It has been burned with fire and cut down;
your people are dying under your angry rebuke.
17Let your hand protect the man at your right hand,
the son of man you raised to strength for yourself.
18Then we will not drift away from you.
Bring us back to life, and we will call on you by name.
19LORD God of Armies, bring us back!
Turn the light of your face on us, and we will be saved.
fields.summary: The people pray to the Shepherd of Israel to restore them, picturing Israel as a vine brought out of Egypt and now cut down, and ask God to turn the light of God’s face on them so they will be saved.

fields.title: Psalm 81
fields.body_html:
If only my people would listen

For the music director. On the gittith. Of Asaph.

1Sing out with joy to God, our strength;
raise a shout to the God of Jacob!
2Strike up the music and beat the tambourine;
play the sweet lyre along with the harp.
3At the new moon, blow the ram’s horn,
and at the full moon, for our feast day,
4for this is a law laid down for Israel,
a rule given by the God of Jacob.
5He made it a solemn charge for Joseph
when he went out against the land of Egypt.
Then I heard a voice I had never known:
6“I lifted the heavy load from their shoulders;
their hands let go of the brick basket.
7When you were in trouble you cried out, and I set you free;
I answered you from the hidden place of the thunder;
I put you to the test at the waters of Meribah. Selah
8Listen, my people, and I will give you a solemn warning;
Israel, oh, that you would listen to me!
9You must have no strange god among you;
you must not bow down to any foreign god.
10I am the LORD your God,
the one who led you up out of Egypt’s land.
Open your mouth as wide as you can, and I will fill it.
11But my people refused to listen to my voice;
Israel would have nothing to do with me.
12So I left them to their stubborn hearts,
and they followed their own schemes.
13If only my people were listening to me,
if only Israel would walk in my paths,
14I would soon bring their enemies low
and turn my hand against their attackers.
15Those who hate the LORD would come cringing to him,
and their doom would never end.
16He would give them the finest wheat to eat,
and I would fill you up with honey from the rock.”
fields.summary: The people are called to celebrate a festival, and God speaks, longing for Israel to listen and walk in God’s ways.

fields.title: Psalm 82
fields.body_html:
God judges the gods

A psalm of Asaph.

1God takes his stand in the divine assembly;
he gives judgment among the gods.
2“How long will you judge unfairly
and take the side of the wicked? Selah
3Judge fairly for the weak and for orphans;
declare the afflicted and the destitute in the right.
4Bring the weak and the poor to safety;
snatch them from the grip of the wicked.
5They have no knowledge and no understanding;
they wander around in the dark,
and the earth’s foundations all totter.
6I myself said, ‘You are gods;
every one of you is a son of the Most High.’
7Yet you will die as human beings die,
and fall like any one of the princes.”
8Rise up, God, judge the earth,
since every nation belongs to you.
fields.summary: God judges among the gods, rebuking them for failing to defend the weak and the fatherless, and the psalmist calls on God to judge the earth.

fields.title: Psalm 83
fields.body_html:
Do not keep silent, God

A song. A psalm of Asaph.

1God, do not rest!
Do not keep silent, and do not sit idle, God!
2Look, your enemies are in an uproar;
those who hate you hold their heads high.
3They are plotting slyly against your people
and conspiring against those you treasure.
4They say, “Come, let us wipe them out so they are no longer a nation;
let no one ever again remember the name of Israel.”
5They have agreed together with one mind;
they are making a treaty against you,
6Edom’s tent-dwellers, the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagrites,
7Gebal, Ammon and Amalek,
Philistia and the people who live in Tyre.
8Assyria too has joined them;
they lend their strength to the descendants of Lot. Selah
9Treat them the way you treated Midian,
the way you treated Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon valley,
10who were wiped out at Endor
and became manure on the ground.
11Deal with their nobles as with Oreb and Zeeb,
and with all their chiefs as with Zebah and Zalmunna,
12who said,
“Let us take God’s pasturelands as our own.”
13My God, make them like a tumbleweed spinning away,
like husks driven by the wind.
14As a fire eats through a forest,
as flames set the mountainsides alight,
15so hunt them down with your storm
and fill them with terror by your gale.
16Load their faces with disgrace,
so that they come seeking your name, LORD.
17May they be shamed and terrified for all time;
may they be disgraced and come to ruin,
18and let them come to know that your name is the LORD,
that only you are Most High over the whole earth.
fields.summary: Enemy nations conspire against Israel, and the psalmist asks God to deal with them as with enemies of old, so that they may know God alone is Most High.

fields.title: Psalm 84
fields.body_html:
Longing for the LORD’s house

For the music director. On the gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1How deeply loved is your dwelling place,
LORD of Armies!
2My whole being longs, even aches, for the courts of the LORD;
heart and body,
I shout with joy to the living God.
3The sparrow, too, has found itself a home, and the swallow has a nest where it keeps its young,
beside your altars, LORD of Armies,
my King and my God.
4How blessed are the ones who live in your house;
they never stop praising you. Selah
5How blessed are people who find their strength in you
and fix their hearts on the pilgrim highways.
6When they travel through the Baca Valley, they make it a land of springs;
the early rain wraps it in blessings.
7They walk on from strength to strength,
till every one of them comes before God in Zion.
8LORD God of Armies, hear my prayer;
turn your ear to me, God of Jacob! Selah
9God, see our shield;
look with care on the face of your anointed one.
10Truly, one day spent in your courts is worth more than a thousand anywhere else;
I would choose to stand at the threshold of my God’s house
over living in the tents of wicked people.
11For the LORD God is both sun and shield;
the LORD gives favor and honor;
from those who walk blamelessly he keeps back nothing good.
12LORD of Armies,
how blessed is anyone who trusts in you!
fields.summary: The psalmist longs for God’s dwelling place; one day in God’s courts is better than a thousand elsewhere.

fields.title: Psalm 85
fields.body_html:
Loyal love and faithfulness meet

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1You were pleased with your land, LORD;
you brought Jacob’s fortunes back.
2You took away the guilt of your people
and covered over all their sins. Selah
3You drew back all your fury;
you turned away from your blazing anger.
4Bring us back, God who saves us,
and put an end to your displeasure with us.
5Will you be angry with us for all time?
Will you stretch out your anger to every generation?
6Will you not bring us back to life once more,
and let your people be glad in you?
7Let us see your loyal love, LORD,
and give us your salvation.
8I am listening for what God, the LORD, will say:
he will speak of peace to his people, to those who are loyal to him;
only let them not slide back into foolishness.
9Truly his salvation is close at hand for those who fear him,
so that glory will settle in our land.
10Loyal love and faithfulness meet as friends;
righteousness and peace greet each other with a kiss.
11Faithfulness grows up out of the earth,
and righteousness gazes down from heaven.
12The LORD will surely give good things,
and our soil will bring forth its crops.
13Righteousness will walk ahead of him
and make a road for his steps.
fields.summary: The people recall how God forgave and restored them and ask God to do so again; loyal love and faithfulness meet as friends, and righteousness and peace greet each other with a kiss.

fields.title: Psalm 86
fields.body_html:
Unite my heart to fear your name

A prayer of David.

1LORD, turn your ear toward me and answer,
because I am afflicted and in need.
2Protect my life, for I am loyal to you. You are my God; rescue me, your servant,
for I trust in you.
3Lord, show me your favor;
I keep calling to you the whole day through.
4Make your servant glad,
for my heart reaches out to you, Lord.
5For you, Lord, are good and quick to forgive,
rich in loyal love to everyone who calls to you.
6LORD, turn your ear to my prayer;
pay attention to my voice as I plead for mercy.
7On my day of trouble I cry out to you,
sure that you will answer.
8Lord, no god is like you,
and no one has done works like yours.
9Every nation you formed will come and bow low before you, Lord,
and give glory to your name.
10For you are great, a worker of wonders;
only you are God.
11LORD, teach me your way,
and I will live by your truth;
give me a heart set on one thing, to revere your name.
12Lord my God, I will thank you with my whole heart
and honor your name for all time.
13For your loyal love for me is great;
you have pulled me out of deepest Sheol.
14God, the proud have come at me,
and a pack of brutal people is hunting for my life;
they do not keep you in view.
15But you, Lord, are a God full of compassion and grace,
slow to grow angry,
overflowing with loyal love and faithfulness.
16Turn to me and show me your favor;
lend your servant your strength,
and rescue the son of your servant woman.
17Give me a sign that you mean me good,
so that those who hate me see it and are left ashamed,
because you, LORD, have come to my aid and brought me comfort.
fields.summary: David, afflicted and in need, asks God to answer him and to teach him God’s way, for God is merciful and gracious.

fields.title: Psalm 87
fields.body_html:
The nations born in Zion

Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.

1The city he founded stands on the holy mountains.
2The gates of Zion are dearer to the LORD
than all the places where Jacob’s people live.
3City of God,
splendid things are said of you. Selah
4“Among those who know me I will name Rahab and Babylon;
see Philistia and Tyre, and Cush as well:
‘This one was born there.’”
5And of Zion people will say, “Every one of them was born in her,”
and it is the Most High who will make her secure.
6As the LORD lists the peoples in his record,
he will write, “This one was born there.” Selah
7Those who sing and those who dance will say,
“All my springs rise in you.”
fields.summary: God loves Zion, and people of many nations will be counted as born there.

fields.title: Psalm 88
fields.body_html:
A prayer from the darkness

A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the music director. On mahalath leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.

1LORD, God who saves me,
I have cried for help by day, and at night I am before you.
2Let my prayer make its way into your presence;
bend down and hear me as I cry.
3For I have had my fill of troubles,
and my life has come to the edge of Sheol.
4I am reckoned with those who descend into the pit;
I have become like someone with no strength left.
5I am turned loose among the dead,
like those killed in battle who lie buried, whom you no longer keep in mind,
who are beyond the reach of your hand.
6You have laid me at the bottom of the pit,
in places of darkness, in the deep waters.
7Your fury presses down on me;
you have crushed me under all your waves. Selah
8You have driven my friends away from me
and made me loathsome to them;
I am shut in, with no way out.
9My eyes are worn out with misery.
Day after day I call on you, LORD,
holding out my hands to you.
10Are your wonders done for the dead?
Do the spirits of the dead stand up to give you thanks? Selah
11Does anyone tell of your loyal love in the grave,
or of your faithfulness in Abaddon?
12Will anyone in the darkness know your wonders,
or your saving justice in the land where all is forgotten?
13As for me, LORD, I keep calling to you for help;
at dawn my prayer is there to meet you.
14LORD, why do you cast me off?
Why do you turn your face away from me?
15From my youth I have been afflicted and close to dying;
I bear your terrors and am at a loss.
16Your blazing anger has rolled over me;
your terrors have put an end to me.
17Like water they swirl around me the whole day;
from every side at once they close in.
18You have taken far from me those I love and my friends;
my one companion is the dark.
fields.summary: Heman cries out from the edge of death, abandoned by friends, with darkness as his only companion.

fields.title: Psalm 89
fields.body_html:
Your promise to David, and the fallen crown

A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.

1Forever I will sing of the loyal love the LORD has shown;
to one generation after another
my mouth will tell how faithful you are.
2For I declare that loyal love is built to last forever;
you have set your faithfulness firm in the heavens.
3“With the one I chose I have made a covenant;
to David, my servant, I have given my oath:
4‘I will make your line secure forever
and make your throne stand for every generation.’” Selah
5The heavens give thanks for your wonders, LORD,
and for your faithfulness in the gathering of the holy ones.
6For who in the clouds above is the LORD’s equal?
Which of the heavenly powers is like the LORD?
7God is held in great awe in the court of the holy ones,
and feared above all who stand around him.
8LORD God of Armies,
who is as strong as you, LORD?
Your faithfulness surrounds you on every side.
9You are master of the proud sea;
when its waves rear up, you hush them.
10You crushed Rahab like one cut down in battle;
your powerful arm sent your enemies running.
11The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours as well;
you laid the foundations of the world and of everything in it.
12North and south are your creation;
Tabor and Hermon ring with joy at your name.
13Yours is an arm full of might;
your hand has strength, and your right hand is lifted high.
14Your throne rests on what is right and just;
loyal love and faithfulness walk ahead of you.
15How blessed are the people who have learned to shout for joy in worship;
LORD, they live in the light of your presence.
16They find joy in your name the whole day,
and your righteousness raises them up.
17For you are the splendor of their strength,
and by your goodwill our strength is raised high.
18For the shield that protects us is the LORD’s,
and the king who rules us belongs to the Holy One of Israel.
19Long ago you spoke in a vision to your loyal ones
and said, “I have laid help on a mighty man;
I have lifted high a man I chose from the people.
20I found David, my servant;
I have poured my holy oil on him to make him king,
21and my hand will stay with him,
and my arm will make him strong.
22No enemy will outwit him,
and no one who does wrong will bring him low.
23I will shatter his foes before his eyes
and cut down the people who hate him.
24My faithfulness and my loyal love will stay beside him,
and through my name his strength will rise.
25I will put the sea under his hand
and the rivers under his right hand.
26He will call to me, ‘It is you who are my Father,
my God, my rock where I am safe.’
27And I will give him the rank of firstborn,
set high above every king on earth.
28I will keep my loyal love for him forever,
and my covenant with him will hold fast.
29I will make his line last for all time,
and his throne as long as the sky endures.
30If his descendants abandon my instruction
and do not live by my rulings,
31if they treat my decrees as nothing
and do not keep my commands,
32then I will call their rebellion to account with the rod
and their guilt with beatings.
33But my loyal love I will never cut off from him,
and my faithfulness will not prove false.
34I will never desecrate my covenant;
what my lips have spoken I will not change.
35I have sworn by my holiness, once and for all,
that I will never lie to David:
36his line will last forever,
and his throne will stand before me like the sun,
37it will be made firm forever like the moon,
that faithful witness in the clouds.” Selah
38But now you have thrown him off and rejected him;
you are enraged with your anointed king.
39You have disowned the covenant with your servant;
you have thrown his crown in the dirt and defiled it.
40You have torn gaps in all his walls
and left his fortresses in rubble.
41Everyone who comes along the road has robbed him;
his neighbors treat him with scorn.
42You have made his foes’ right hand strong
and filled all his enemies with joy.
43Yes, you have blunted his sword’s edge
and left him unable to stand in the fight.
44You have made his glory fade
and thrown his throne down into the dust.
45You have made his young days short
and covered him with disgrace like a cloak. Selah
46How long, LORD? Will you keep yourself hidden forever?
Will your anger go on burning like fire?
47Remember how brief my life is!
Is it for nothing that you have created every human being?
48Who can go on living and never see death?
Who can save their own life from the grip of Sheol? Selah
49Lord, where are the acts of loyal love you showed in the past,
the ones you swore to David by your faithfulness?
50Lord, keep in mind the scorn heaped on your servants;
I hold within me the insults of all the many peoples,
51the insults your enemies have hurled, LORD,
the taunts that have dogged every step of your anointed king.
52May the LORD be blessed forever!
Amen and amen.
fields.summary: Ethan sings of God’s loyal love and the covenant with David, then laments that God seems to have rejected the anointed king, and asks how long.

fields.title: Psalm 90
fields.body_html:
Teach us to count our days

A prayer of Moses, the man of God.

1Lord, you have been our home through every generation.
2Before the mountains came to birth,
before you labored to bring to birth the earth and all the world,
from the endless past to the endless future you are God.
3You make mortals go back to dust;
you say, “Return, children of Adam.”
4For in your eyes a thousand years are like yesterday, once it has gone by,
or like one watch of the night.
5You wash them away like a flood. They are a passing sleep.
When morning comes they are like grass that springs up again.
6In the morning it blooms and grows fresh;
by evening it droops and dries out.
7For we are worn away by your anger
and struck with terror by your rage.
8You have laid our wrongs out before you;
what we hid is lit up by the light of your face.
9All our days slip away under your wrath;
our years end like a sigh.
10Our lifetime lasts seventy years, or eighty for the strong;
yet even its best is toil and sorrow,
for it hurries past, and we take flight.
11Who knows the force of your anger?
Your fury matches the reverence you deserve.
12Teach us, then, to reckon our days rightly,
so that our hearts may grow wise.
13Turn back to us, LORD! How long must we wait?
Show pity to your servants.
14Fill us with your loyal love at daybreak,
and we will shout for joy and rejoice as long as we live.
15Match the days you brought us low with days of gladness,
and the years of hardship we have known with years of joy.
16Let your servants see your deeds,
and let their children see your splendor.
17May the Lord our God show us his kindness.
Give lasting worth to the work of our hands;
yes, give the work of our hands lasting worth.
fields.summary: Moses prays to God, who has been the people’s home in every generation, and asks God to teach them to reckon their days rightly and establish the work of their hands.

fields.title: Psalm 91
fields.body_html:
In the shelter of the Most High

1Whoever makes a home under the cover of the Most High
will spend the night in the shade of the Almighty.
2This is what I say about the LORD: “He is my shelter and my stronghold,
my God, the one I rely on.”
3It is he who will rescue you from the bird-catcher’s trap
and from the plague that destroys.
4He will spread his feathers over you, and beneath his wings you will find shelter.
His faithfulness surrounds you like a shield and a wall.
5You need not be afraid of the terrors that come at night
or the arrow that speeds by in daylight,
6or the disease that prowls in the dark,
or the destruction that ravages at noon.
7A thousand may drop beside you,
ten thousand close by your right hand,
yet it will not reach you.
8You will only watch with your own eyes
and see the wicked paid back.
9For you, LORD, are my refuge!
You have made the Most High your home.
10No evil will strike you;
no plague will get close to your home.
11For he will give his angels orders about you,
to protect you wherever you go.
12They will carry you in their hands,
and you will not hurt your foot on a stone.
13You will walk over lions and cobras;
you will crush young lions and serpents under your feet.
14“Those who cling to me with love I will rescue;
I will lift them high out of reach, because they know my name.
15They will cry out to me, and I will answer;
in their distress I will stand by them;
I will free them and bring them honor.
16I will give them their fill of long life
and show them my saving help.”
fields.summary: Whoever lives under the shelter of the Most High will be protected from every danger, for God promises to rescue the one who loves God.

fields.title: Psalm 92
fields.body_html:
It is good to give thanks

A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.

1It is a good thing to thank the LORD,
to sing and play in praise of your name, Most High,
2to tell of your loyal love at sunrise
and of your faithfulness through the nights,
3with the ten-stringed instrument and the harp,
to the sounding music of the lyre.
4For your deeds, LORD, have filled me with joy;
I sing out over all that your hands have made.
5LORD, how great the things you do!
How very deep your plans!
6Senseless people do not know it;
fools cannot grasp this:
7though the wicked shoot up like green plants
and all who do wrong are in bloom,
it is only so that they may be destroyed for all time.
8But you, LORD,
are enthroned on high for all time.
9Look at your enemies, LORD!
Look, your enemies are doomed;
everyone who does evil will be driven apart.
10But you have made me strong like a wild ox;
fresh oil has been poured over me.
11My eyes have looked in triumph on those who lay in wait for me;
my ears have heard what became of the evildoers who rose up against me.
12The righteous will thrive like the palm tree
and rise tall as a cedar on Lebanon.
13Rooted in the LORD’s house,
they will bloom in the courtyards of our God.
14Even when they are old they will still bear fruit;
they will stay rich with sap and green,
15bearing witness that the LORD is just:
my rock, in whom nothing is crooked.
fields.summary: It is good to give thanks to God, whose works are great; the righteous flourish like palm trees.

fields.title: Psalm 93
fields.body_html:
The LORD is King

1The LORD is King! He has put on majesty like a robe;
the LORD has dressed himself and tied on strength like a belt.
The world stands firm; nothing can shake it.
2Your throne has stood firm from ancient days;
you have always been.
3The rivers have risen, LORD;
the rivers have raised their roar;
the rivers lift high their crashing waves.
4Above the roar of the great waters,
above the crash of the ocean’s breakers,
the LORD is majestic on high.
5Your decrees can be fully trusted;
holiness suits your house,
LORD, for all time to come.
fields.summary: God is King, robed in majesty, mightier than the roaring waters, and God’s decrees stand firm.

fields.title: Psalm 94
fields.body_html:
God who judges the earth, rise up

1God of retribution, LORD,
God of retribution, shine out!
2Stand up, Judge of all the earth,
and give the arrogant what their deeds have earned.
3LORD, how much longer will the wicked,
how much longer will the wicked celebrate?
4Insolent words gush from them;
everyone who does evil talks big.
5They grind down your people, LORD;
they oppress the nation that belongs to you.
6Widows and foreigners they put to death;
orphans they murder.
7They say, “The LORD is not looking;
Jacob’s God pays no attention.”
8Get some understanding, you brutish people!
Fools, when will you start to think wisely?
9Will the one who set the ear in place not hear?
Will the one who shaped the eye not see?
10Will the one who disciplines nations not correct them,
the one who teaches humans all they know?
11The LORD knows what humans are thinking,
and that their thoughts are only a puff of air.
12How blessed is the one whom you correct, LORD,
and train through your instruction,
13giving them calm in the days of trouble,
while the pit is being dug for the wicked.
14The LORD will not reject his people;
he will never desert those who belong to him.
15For justice will once again be joined to what is right,
and all who are honest at heart will follow it.
16Who will take my side against the wicked?
Who will stand with me against those who do wrong?
17If the LORD had not helped me,
I would soon have been living where all is silent.
18The moment I said, “My foot is giving way,”
your loyal love, LORD, held me up.
19When my worries crowd in on me,
your comfort fills me with joy.
20Will a ruling power bent on ruin ever be your partner,
one that uses the law to create misery?
21They gather against the righteous to take their lives,
and they condemn innocent people to death.
22But the LORD has proved to be my high fortress;
my God has been a rock that shelters me.
23He will make their evil recoil on them
and put an end to them through their own wickedness;
the LORD our God will put an end to them.
fields.summary: The psalmist calls on God, the Judge of all the earth, to repay the arrogant, and finds comfort in God’s support when his foot slips.

fields.title: Psalm 95
fields.body_html:
Bow to the King; listen today

1Come, let us sing out with joy to the LORD
and raise a glad shout to the Rock who saves us.
2Let us go out to meet him with thanks,
and lift a glad shout to him in our songs.
3For the LORD is a mighty God,
a mighty King high over all gods,
4who holds the deep places of the earth in his hand;
the tops of the mountains are his as well,
5the sea belongs to him because he made it,
and his hands shaped the dry ground.
6Come, let us bow down to the ground and bend low;
let us kneel in front of the LORD, the one who made us.
7For it is he who is our God,
and we are a people he pastures, a flock he tends with his own hand.
Oh, that today you would listen to his voice!
8“Do not let your hearts grow hard, as happened at Meribah,
on the day of Massah out in the desert,
9when your ancestors put me to the test
and challenged me, even after they had watched my work.
10Forty years long I was weary and disgusted with that generation.
I said, ‘These are people whose hearts wander off;
they have never learned my ways.’
11So in my anger I took an oath:
‘They will never come into my place of rest.’”
fields.summary: The people are called to sing to God, the great King, and to worship, but warned not to harden their hearts as their ancestors did in the wilderness.

fields.title: Psalm 96
fields.body_html:
A new song for all the earth

1Sing a new song to the LORD!
All the earth, sing to the LORD!
2Raise your song to the LORD; bless his name.
Day after day announce the good news of how he saves.
3Tell the nations of his glory,
and all the peoples of the wonders he has done.
4For the LORD is great and worthy of the highest praise;
he must be revered above every god.
5For every god the peoples serve is a mere nothing, an idol,
but it was the LORD who made the heavens.
6Splendor and majesty stand in his presence;
strength and beauty fill his holy place.
7Give the LORD what is due, you families of the nations;
give the LORD glory and might.
8Give the LORD the glory his name deserves;
bring a gift and enter his courts.
9Bow low before the LORD in holy splendor;
tremble in his presence, all the earth.
10Tell the nations, “The LORD is King!
The world stands firm; nothing can make it totter.
He will judge the peoples fairly.”
11Let the heavens be full of joy and the earth be glad;
let the sea thunder with all that lives in it.
12Let the fields and everything in them celebrate;
then every tree in the woods will cry out with joy,
13in the presence of the LORD, for he is on the way, on the way to judge the earth.
He will bring justice to the world
and judge its peoples by his own faithfulness.
fields.summary: All the earth is called to sing a new song to God, who is to be feared above all gods and comes to judge the world in righteousness.

fields.title: Psalm 97
fields.body_html:
The LORD is King over all

1The LORD is King! Let the earth be glad,
and the many far-off coastlands celebrate.
2Clouds and deep darkness surround him;
his throne is built on what is right and just.
3Fire marches ahead of him
and burns up his enemies on every side.
4The world is lit by the flash of his lightning;
the earth sees it and quakes.
5In the presence of the LORD the mountains soften like wax,
in the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.
6The skies announce that he is righteous,
and every people sees his glory.
7Let everyone who serves carved idols be disgraced,
all who brag about worthless gods;
bow down before him, all you gods!
8Zion hears of it and is filled with joy;
the towns of Judah celebrate
your acts of justice, LORD.
9For it is you, LORD, who are Most High over the whole earth;
you are lifted far above every god.
10All who love the LORD, hate what is evil!
He watches over the lives of his faithful people
and rescues them from the power of the wicked.
11Light is scattered like seed for the righteous,
and joy for those whose hearts are true.
12Be glad in the LORD, you righteous people,
and thank him, calling his holy name to mind.
fields.summary: God is King; fire and lightning go before God, idols are put to shame, and the righteous rejoice.

fields.title: Psalm 98
fields.body_html:
Creation greets its coming Judge

A psalm.

1Sing the LORD a new song because of the wonders he has done!
By his own right hand and his holy arm he has won the victory.
2The LORD has let his saving power be known;
he has shown his justice openly for the nations to see.
3He has kept in mind his loyal love and faithfulness toward the people of Israel;
the farthest places on earth have seen
how our God saves.
4Raise a glad shout to the LORD, all the earth;
burst into joyful song and make music!
5Make music for the LORD on the lyre,
the lyre and the voice of song!
6With trumpets and the ram’s horn sounding,
lift a glad shout before the King, the LORD.
7Let the sea and everything in it thunder,
the world and everyone living there.
8May the rivers clap their hands,
and the mountains all sing for joy together,
9in the presence of the LORD, for he is on the way to judge the earth.
He will govern the world rightly
and the peoples with fairness.
fields.summary: All the earth is called to sing a new song to God for the wonders God has done and the victory God has won, for God comes to judge.

fields.title: Psalm 99
fields.body_html:
Holy is the King enthroned in Zion

1The LORD is King; let the peoples shudder!
He is seated on the cherubim as on a throne; let the earth shake!
2In Zion the LORD is great;
he towers over all the peoples.
3Let the peoples give thanks to your name, great and awe-inspiring.
He is holy!
4Mighty King who loves justice,
it is you who have set fairness firmly in place;
you have done what is just and right in Jacob.
5Lift high the LORD our God,
and bow low at his footstool.
He is holy!
6Among his priests were Moses and Aaron,
and among those who called on his name was Samuel;
they called out to the LORD, and he answered them.
7From the pillar of cloud he spoke with them;
they kept the decrees he laid down and the rule he gave them.
8LORD our God, it was you who answered them.
To them you were a God who forgives,
yet one who punished their wrongs.
9Lift high the LORD our God,
and bow low on his holy hill,
because the LORD our God is holy.
fields.summary: God is King, enthroned on the cherubim, holy and just, who answered Moses, Aaron and Samuel.

fields.title: Psalm 100
fields.body_html:
All the earth, come in with thanks

A psalm for giving thanks.

1Raise a glad shout to the LORD, all the earth!
2Serve the LORD and be glad doing it;
come before him with ringing cries of joy.
3Be sure of this: the LORD is God!
He is the one who made us, and we belong to him.
We are his people, the flock he pastures.
4Come through his gates giving thanks,
into his courtyards with praise;
thank him and bless his name.
5For the LORD is good; his loyal love has no end,
and his faithfulness stands from one generation to the next.
fields.summary: All the earth is called to shout for joy to God, who made us and whose loyal love lasts forever.

fields.title: Psalm 101
fields.body_html:
A king’s vow of integrity

Of David. A psalm.

1Loyal love and justice will be my song; LORD, I will make music for you.
2I will take care to keep to the blameless way. When will you come to me? Inside my own house I will live with an undivided heart.
3I will not fix my eyes on anything vile. I hate the deeds of those who turn away; they will get no hold on me.
4A crooked heart will stay far from me; I will not keep company with evil.
5Anyone who secretly slanders a neighbor I will destroy; anyone with lofty eyes and a swollen heart I will not put up with.
6I will watch for those in the land who are faithful and bring them to live with me; those who walk the blameless way will be my servants.
7Deceivers will find no home in my house; liars will not keep their place in my sight.
8Each morning I will make an end of the wicked in the land, and rid the city of the LORD of all who do wrong.
fields.summary: David resolves to live with integrity and to have nothing to do with the wicked.

fields.title: Psalm 102
fields.body_html:
A prayer from the ashes for Zion

A prayer of someone in deep trouble, who is worn out and pours out a complaint before the LORD.

1LORD, listen to my prayer; let my call for help reach you.
2Do not turn your face away from me on the day trouble presses me hard. Bend down and listen to me; on the day I call, be quick to answer.
3For my days are going up in smoke, and my bones are scorched like a hearth.
4My heart is beaten down and dried up like grass; I do not even remember to eat.
5All my groaning has worn me down until my bones stick to my skin.
6I am like an owl out in the wilderness, a little owl in a place of ruins.
7Sleep will not come; I am like a single bird sitting on the housetop.
8My enemies scorn me the whole day; those who jeer at me make my name a curse.
9For ashes are the bread I eat, and tears fall into what I drink,
10because of your fury and your anger; you picked me up and flung me away.
11My days are a shadow that stretches out as the sun goes down; I dry up like grass.
12But you, LORD, are King on your throne forever, and your name lives on from one generation to the next.
13You will stand up and take pity on Zion; the hour to be kind to her is here, the time you set has come.
14For your servants treasure her very stones and grieve over her dust.
15Then nations will stand in awe of the name of the LORD, and every king on earth will tremble at your glory.
16For the LORD will build Zion again; he will be seen in all his glory.
17He will listen when the destitute pray and will not wave their prayers aside.
18Put this in writing for the generation still to come, and a people that is still to be created will praise the LORD,
19that the LORD bent down from his holy heights and looked out from heaven over the earth,
20to listen to the moaning of captives and free those marked for death,
21so that people may make the LORD’s name known in Zion and sing his praise in Jerusalem,
22when nations and kingdoms all gather to serve the LORD.
23On the road of life he has worn down my strength and made my days few.
24So I say: My God, do not take me away when only half my days are done, you whose years run on from age to age.
25Long ago you set the earth on its foundations; the heavens are what your hands have made.
26They will come to an end, but you stand firm; all of them will grow old and thin like a cloak. Like worn clothing you will exchange them, and they will be gone.
27But you are the one who does not change, and your years will never be finished.
28The children of your servants will make their home in the land, and their descendants will be kept safe in your presence.
fields.summary: A person in deep trouble pours out a complaint to God, whose years never end, and trusts that God will rebuild Zion.

fields.title: Psalm 103
fields.body_html:
Bless the LORD, my soul

Of David.

1Bless the LORD, my soul; let all that is deep within me bless his holy name.
2Bless the LORD, my soul, and never forget all that he has done for you,
3who pardons all your wrongdoing, who cures every illness you have,
4who ransoms your life from the grave, who makes loyal love and compassion your crown,
5who fills your life with good things, so that you are made young again like the eagle.
6The LORD acts to set things right and gives justice to all who are crushed by others.
7He let Moses know his ways and let the people of Israel see what he could do.
8Tender and gracious is the LORD, slow to anger, rich in loyal love.
9He does not keep bringing charges, and he does not hold on to anger for all time.
10He has not treated us as our sins called for, nor paid us back in full for our wrongs.
11As far as the sky towers over the earth, so mighty is his loyal love over all who fear him.
12As distant as sunrise is from sunset, so distant has he set our rebellious acts from us.
13Just as a father feels for his children, the LORD feels tender love for all who fear him.
14For he knows what we are made of; he does not forget that we are only dust.
15Mortals have days like grass; they bloom like a flower in the open field,
16a wind blows across it and it has vanished; its own place will not know it again.
17But the loyal love of the LORD lasts from age to age on all who fear him, while his righteousness reaches their children’s children,
18for all who hold to his covenant and are careful to carry out what he commands.
19The LORD has fixed his throne in heaven; his royal power reigns over all there is.
20Bless the LORD, you angels of his, strong warriors who carry out what he says and listen for the sound of his word.
21Bless the LORD, all his armies, his attendants who carry out what he wants.
22Bless the LORD, all that he has made, everywhere under his rule. Bless the LORD, my soul.
fields.summary: The psalmist calls on himself to bless God, who forgives, heals and redeems, and whose loyal love is as high as the heavens.

fields.title: Psalm 104
fields.body_html:
The Creator’s world, full of creatures

1Bless the LORD, my soul. LORD my God, how great you are! Splendor and majesty are the robes you wear,
2you wrap yourself in light as in a cloak and spread out the sky like a tent cloth,
3who builds his upper rooms with beams set in the waters above, who turns the clouds into his chariot and travels on the wings of the wind,
4who makes the winds his messengers and flames of fire his servants.
5He fixed the earth on its bases, never to be toppled, for all time to come.
6The deep was the robe you put over it; the waters rose and stood above the mountains.
7When you rebuked them, the waters ran; at the roar of your thunder they rushed off,
8they went up over the mountains and down into the valleys, to the place you had fixed for them.
9You fixed a limit they may not pass; they will not come back to cover the land.
10You let springs loose into the stream beds; they find their way between the mountains.
11Every creature of the open country drinks from them; there the wild donkeys satisfy their thirst.
12Close by them the birds of the air settle and call out from the leafy branches.
13From his rooms on high he waters the mountains, and the earth has its fill of the fruit of your work.
14He makes grass spring up for the herds and plants for people to tend, so that food comes out of the ground,
15wine that brings joy to human hearts, oil that makes faces glow, and bread that keeps people strong.
16The LORD’s trees have all the water they need, the cedars he planted on Lebanon,
17where birds build their nests, and the stork lives high in the cypress trees.
18The wild goats have the high mountains, and the hyraxes take shelter in the crags.
19He made the moon for keeping the feasts and seasons; the sun knows the hour it should set.
20You send darkness, night comes, and every animal of the woods steals out.
21The young lions roar as they hunt, asking God for their meal.
22At sunrise they draw back together and settle down to rest in their lairs.
23Then human beings head out to their work and keep at their tasks till evening.
24LORD, how many and varied your works are! You made them all with skill and wisdom; the earth is crowded with what you have made.
25Look at the sea, so vast and reaching out on every side! It swarms with countless creatures, living things tiny and huge.
26Ships travel across it, and so does Leviathan, the creature you shaped to play in its waves.
27Every one of them waits for you to give them food when it is needed.
28You hand it out and they pick it up; you open your hand, and they eat their fill of good things.
29If you turn your face away, they panic; if you withdraw their breath, they breathe their last and go back to the dust they came from.
30When you send your spirit out, they come into being, and you make the face of the land new.
31Let the glory of the LORD stand forever; let the LORD be glad in the things he has made,
32who glances at the earth and it quakes, who touches the mountains and they send up smoke.
33All my life long I will sing to the LORD; while I am still here I will make music to my God.
34Let what I ponder bring him pleasure; as for me, my joy is in the LORD.
35Let sinners be wiped out from the earth, and let no wicked people be left. Bless the LORD, my soul. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The psalmist blesses God for creation, the heavens, the waters, the creatures and the seasons, all of which look to God for life.

fields.title: Psalm 105
fields.body_html:
The LORD keeps his promise

1Thank the LORD and call on his name; tell every people what he has done.
2Sing to him, play and sing his praise; talk of all the wonderful things he has done.
3Take pride in his holy name; let all who look to the LORD be glad at heart.
4Turn to the LORD and to his strength; come into his presence again and again.
5Call to mind the wonders he has worked, his signs, and the verdicts he spoke,
6you descendants of his servant Abraham, you children of Jacob, the ones he chose.
7He, the LORD, is our God; his rulings reach the whole earth.
8He keeps his covenant in mind forever, the promise he laid down for a thousand generations,
9the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac,
10and he set it in place for Jacob as a decree, for Israel as a covenant that lasts forever,
11saying, “The land of Canaan I give to you, a share marked out for you to inherit.”
12When they were only a handful of people, a few outsiders living in that land,
13wandering from one nation to the next, from one kingdom to another people,
14he let no one do them wrong, and he took kings to task over them:
15“Do not lay a hand on my anointed ones; do not hurt my prophets.”
16He summoned a famine over the land and broke off every supply of bread.
17But he had already sent a man on ahead of them: Joseph, who was sold to be a slave.
18Shackles bruised his feet, and his neck was locked in iron,
19until the day his own words came true; the word of the LORD refined him.
20The king sent orders to free him; the ruler of many peoples let him loose.
21He put him in charge of his palace and gave him rule over all his wealth,
22with power to put his officials in chains if he chose, and to make his counselors wise.
23So Israel came into Egypt, and Jacob settled as a guest in the land of Ham.
24There he made his people grow greatly in number, until they were too strong for their enemies.
25He turned the hearts of the Egyptians to hatred of his people and to scheming against his servants.
26He sent his servant Moses, and with him Aaron, his chosen one.
27Among the Egyptians they carried out the signs he had spoken of, and wonders throughout the land of Ham.
28He sent darkness and the land went dark; and they did not defy his word.
29He made their waters blood and left their fish dead.
30Frogs swarmed over their land, even into the inner rooms of their kings.
31At his command came swarms of flies, and gnats covered every part of their land.
32Instead of rain he gave them hail, with fire flashing across their land.
33He beat down their grapevines and their fig trees and splintered every tree in their land.
34At his word the locusts arrived, swarms of young locusts too many to count,
35and they devoured every green plant in their land and swallowed up the harvest of their fields.
36And he killed the firstborn of every family in their land, the first sons born of their strength.
37He brought his people out carrying silver and gold, and in all his tribes not one person stumbled.
38Egypt was happy to see them go, since fear of them had come over its people.
39He spread a cloud above them like a screen, and fire to light up the night.
40When they asked, he sent quail, and he gave them their fill of bread from heaven.
41He opened up a rock and water streamed out, running like a river through the parched land.
42For he remembered the holy word he had spoken to Abraham, his servant.
43So he led his people out rejoicing, his chosen ones singing aloud for joy.
44He gave them the lands of other nations, and they took over what those peoples had worked for,
45so that they would keep his decrees and hold fast to his instructions. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The people are called to give thanks for God’s covenant with Abraham and the wonders God did through Joseph, Moses and the exodus.

fields.title: Psalm 106
fields.body_html:
Israel’s unfaithfulness and God’s mercy

1Praise the LORD! Give the LORD thanks, for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever.
2Who can put into words the mighty deeds of the LORD or tell out all the praise he deserves?
3How blessed are those who hold to justice and do what is right at every moment!
4LORD, think of me when you favor your people; come to me with your saving help,
5so that I may see the good things you give your chosen ones, be glad with your nation in its gladness, and give glory together with the people who belong to you.
6Like our ancestors, we have sinned; we have gone astray and done what is evil.
7Our ancestors in Egypt did not take your wonders to heart; they did not remember how great your loyal love was, and at the sea, the Red Sea, they rebelled.
8Still he rescued them, for the honor of his name, to show how mighty he is.
9He spoke sharply to the Red Sea, and it went dry; he brought them over the deep places as if across open country.
10He rescued them from the power of the one who hated them and set them free from the enemy’s grip.
11The waters closed over their enemies; not a single one remained.
12Then they trusted his promises and sang songs of praise to him.
13How quickly they forgot his deeds! They would not wait to hear what he intended.
14Out in the wilderness their cravings ran wild, and in the wasteland they challenged God.
15He granted what they demanded, but with it he sent a disease that wasted them away.
16They turned jealous of Moses there in the camp, and of Aaron, the man set apart as holy to the LORD.
17The ground split open and swallowed Dathan; it closed over Abiram and his followers.
18Then fire flared up in their company, and flames devoured the wicked.
19They made a calf at Horeb and bowed low before an idol of molten metal.
20They traded God, their glory, for the figure of a grass-eating bull.
21They forgot God their Savior and the great deeds he had worked in Egypt,
22wonders in the land of Ham, fearsome acts at the Red Sea.
23So he said he would wipe them out; but Moses, his chosen one, stood in the gap before him to turn his anger away so that he would not destroy them.
24They looked down on the land of delight and put no faith in what he had promised,
25They muttered in their tents and would not heed the voice of the LORD.
26So he raised his hand in an oath that they would die in the wilderness,
27and that their children would be brought down among the nations and scattered through foreign lands.
28They bound themselves to the Baal of Peor and ate offerings made to the dead.
29They made him angry by what they did, and plague burst out among them.
30Then Phinehas rose and stepped in, and the plague was halted.
31And that deed was counted to him as righteousness for all generations, for all time.
32At the waters of Meribah they made him angry, and Moses paid dearly because of them,
33for they defied his Spirit, and Moses let hasty words pass his lips.
34They did not wipe out the peoples the LORD had told them to destroy,
35instead they mixed with the nations and took up their ways.
36They served those nations’ idols, which turned into a trap for them.
37They even offered up their own sons and daughters to demons.
38They spilled the blood of the innocent, their own sons and daughters, slaughtered as offerings to Canaan’s idols, and the land was made unclean by bloodshed.
39They made themselves unclean by what they did and were unfaithful like a prostitute in their ways.
40So the LORD burned with anger against his people and came to loathe his own possession.
41He handed them over to other nations, and people who hated them became their masters.
42Their enemies crushed them and forced them to bow under their power.
43Again and again he rescued them, but they kept to their own rebellious plans and sank down in their sin.
44Even so, he saw the trouble they were in when their cry reached him.
45For their sake he called to mind his covenant and turned from his anger, because his loyal love is so great.
46He moved all those who had carried them off to treat them with pity.
47Rescue us, LORD our God, and bring us back together from among the nations, so that we may thank your holy name and make our boast in praising you.
48May the LORD, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come! And let all the people answer, “Amen!” Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: Israel confesses its repeated sins from Egypt to the land, and God’s repeated mercy, and asks God to gather them from the nations.

fields.title: Psalm 107
fields.body_html:
Let the rescued give thanks

1Give the LORD thanks, for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever.
2Let those whom the LORD has bought back say it, those he freed from the grip of the enemy,
3and brought them in from other lands, from the east and the west, the north and the south.
4Some strayed through the wilderness, along a barren track, and found no town to live in.
5Starving and parched, they felt their life draining out of them.
6In their distress they called out to the LORD, and he rescued them from their troubles.
7He guided them on a level road until they came to a town to live in.
8Let them give the LORD thanks for his loyal love and for the wonders he works for humankind.
9For he gives drink to those who are parched and fills the starving with good food.
10Some lived in darkness, in the blackest gloom, held fast in misery and iron,
11because they had defied what God said and scorned the purpose of the Most High.
12So he broke their pride with hard labor; they fell, and no one came to help.
13In their distress they called out to the LORD, and he saved them from their troubles.
14He led them out of the darkness and the blackest gloom and snapped the chains that held them.
15Let them give the LORD thanks for his loyal love and for the wonders he works for humankind.
16For he smashes doors of bronze and hacks through bars of iron.
17Some were fools, and their rebellious ways and their wrongdoing brought suffering on them.
18They could not stand the sight of food, and came close to the gates of death.
19In their distress they called out to the LORD, and he saved them from their troubles.
20He sent his word and made them well; he pulled them out of the pit of death.
21Let them give the LORD thanks for his loyal love and for the wonders he works for humankind.
22Let them bring offerings of thanks and with glad shouts recount what he has done.
23Some sailed out to sea in ships, trading over the vast waters,
24they saw for themselves what the LORD does, his marvels out on the deep.
25At his word a gale sprang up and drove the waves of the sea high.
26Up they were tossed to the sky, and down into the depths; in such danger their nerve gave way.
27They lurched and swayed like someone drunk, and all their skill at sea came to nothing.
28In their distress they called out to the LORD, and he brought them out from their troubles.
29He turned the gale into a gentle breath, and the waves around them fell silent.
30How glad they were when all grew still! And he brought them to the harbor they longed for.
31Let them give the LORD thanks for his loyal love and for the wonders he works for humankind.
32Let them lift him high where the people gather and praise him where the elders sit in council.
33He can dry up rivers until they are desert and turn springs of water into parched land,
34and rich farmland into a salt flat, for the evil done by those who live there.
35He makes the desert a pool of water and dry country into bubbling springs.
36There he settles the hungry, and they build a town to live in.
37They seed the fields and plant vines, and gather a rich harvest.
38He blesses them, and their numbers grow and grow; he does not let their herds dwindle.
39Then they dwindle and are brought down by cruel rule, disaster and grief.
40He heaps scorn on the powerful and leaves them lost in a wasteland without a road.
41But he raises the needy from their misery and makes their families grow like flocks of sheep.
42Those who live upright lives look on with joy, and all wickedness has nothing more to say.
43Whoever is wise should mark these things and ponder the loyal love the LORD has shown again and again.
fields.summary: Those whom God has redeemed are called to give thanks: wanderers, prisoners, the sick and sailors in a storm all cried out, and God rescued them.

fields.title: Psalm 108
fields.body_html:
Morning praise and a prayer for victory

A song. A psalm of David.

1My heart is firm, God; I will sing and play songs of praise with all my soul.
2Come awake, harp and lyre! I will wake up the dawn.
3LORD, I will thank you before all peoples; I will sing your praise in every nation.
4For your loyal love towers above the heavens, and your faithfulness rises to the clouds.
5God, be lifted high above the heavens; let your glory spread over all the earth.
6So that those you love may be set free, bring rescue with your right hand and answer me!
7God has spoken from his holy place: “I will rejoice as I share out Shechem and mark off the Valley of Succoth.
8Gilead belongs to me, Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the helmet on my head, Judah the staff of my rule.
9Moab is my washing bowl; on Edom I toss my sandal; I raise the victor’s shout over Philistia!”
10Who will take me into the walled city? Who will guide me all the way to Edom?
11Is it not you, God, who rejected us and no longer march out with our armies?
12Help us against the enemy, for any rescue that people can bring is useless.
13With God on our side we will fight with courage; he is the one who will crush our foes underfoot.
fields.summary: David’s heart is firm, and he praises God among the nations and trusts God for victory.

fields.title: Psalm 109
fields.body_html:
God of my praise, do not be silent

For the music director. Of David. A psalm.

1God whom I praise, do not keep silent.
2For the wicked have opened deceitful mouths against me; they speak to me with lies on their tongues.
3They have hemmed me in with hateful words and attacked me for no reason.
4They repay my love by accusing me, yet I go on praying.
5They hand me evil for the good I did, and hatred in exchange for my love.
6Put someone wicked in charge of him; may an accuser take his stand at his right side.
7When he is tried, may the verdict be guilty, and may his very prayer count as sin.
8May his life be short, and may someone else take over his position.
9May his children lose their father and his wife be left a widow.
10May his children roam about as beggars, searching for food far from their ruined homes.
11May the moneylender snatch up all he owns, and strangers carry off what he worked for.
12May no one keep showing him loyal love, and no one take pity on his orphaned children.
13May his line come to an end, their name erased within a generation.
14May the LORD keep in mind the guilt of his ancestors, and may his mother’s sin never be erased.
15May their sins stay always before the LORD, and may he wipe out all memory of them from the earth.
16For he never thought to show loyal love; he hounded the poor and needy and the heartbroken to their death.
17He loved to curse, and the curse has come back on him; he had no wish to bless, and blessing has stayed far from him.
18He put on cursing as his clothing; it seeped like water into his inner being and soaked like oil deep into his bones.
19May it be the cloak he wraps around him, the belt he ties on every day.
20May this be how the LORD repays my accusers, those who speak evil against me.
21But you, Lord GOD, take my side for the honor of your name; rescue me, for your loyal love is good.
22For I am poor and helpless; my heart within me is pierced through.
23Like a shadow lengthening at dusk I pass away; I am brushed off like a locust.
24My knees buckle from going without food, and my body has grown thin, with no fat left on it.
25They treat me with contempt; when they catch sight of me, they shake their heads at me.
26LORD my God, come to my help! Save me, true to your loyal love.
27Make them see that this is your own hand at work, that you, LORD, are the one who did it.
28They may curse, but you will bless; when they rise against me they will be disgraced, while your servant rejoices.
29May my accusers be dressed in dishonor and wrapped in their own shame like a cloak.
30My lips will thank the LORD over and over; I will praise him in the middle of the crowd.
31For he takes his place at the right side of the needy, to save them from those who would sentence them to death.
fields.summary: Attacked by liars, David asks God to deal with his accuser and to save him because of God’s loyal love.

fields.title: Psalm 110
fields.body_html:
A king and priest forever

Of David. A psalm.

1The LORD declares to my lord: “Take your seat at my right hand, while I lay your enemies beneath your feet like a footstool.”
2From Zion the LORD will stretch out the scepter of your power: rule where your enemies surround you!
3Your people offer themselves gladly on the day you march out in strength, in splendor and holiness. Out of the dawn’s womb your youth comes to you fresh as the dew.
4The LORD has taken an oath and will not take it back: “You are a priest for all time, after the pattern of Melchizedek.”
5The Lord stands at your right side, and when the day of his anger comes, he shatters kings.
6He passes judgment on the nations, and the dead lie everywhere; he crushes the leaders over the wide earth.
7On the way he drinks from a stream, and so he stands with his head held high.
fields.summary: God declares to the king, “Take your seat at my right hand,” and makes him a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.

fields.title: Psalm 111
fields.body_html:
The great works of the LORD

1Praise the LORD! I will thank the LORD with all my heart where upright people gather, in the whole assembly.
2The deeds of the LORD are great; all who take pleasure in them search them out.
3Everything he does shines with splendor and majesty, and his righteousness stands for all time.
4He has set up a memorial of his wonderful deeds; the LORD is gracious and tender in mercy.
5He feeds those who fear him and keeps his covenant in mind for all time.
6He made the might of his deeds known to his people when he gave them the nations’ land to inherit.
7All that his hands do is faithful and just; every one of his precepts can be trusted.
8They stand secure for all time, framed with faithfulness and integrity.
9He sent his people redemption and set his covenant in place for all time. Holy and awe-inspiring is his name!
10The fear of the LORD is where wisdom begins; all who carry them out show good sense. His praise stands for all time.
fields.summary: The psalmist praises God’s great works, faithful covenant and redemption; the fear of God is where wisdom begins.

fields.title: Psalm 112
fields.body_html:
The life of one who fears the LORD

1Praise the LORD! How blessed are all who fear the LORD, whose great delight is in his commands!
2Their descendants will be powerful in the land, for the family of the upright is blessed.
3Their houses are full of wealth and riches, and their righteousness stands for all time.
4When darkness falls, a light shines out for the upright: they are gracious, full of compassion, and righteous.
5Things go well for people who are kind and lend to others, and who handle their dealings with justice.
6They will never be overthrown; the righteous will be remembered for all time.
7Bad news does not frighten them; their hearts stand firm because they trust in the LORD.
8Their hearts are held steady and they will not be afraid, until they see what becomes of their enemies.
9They have given generously, spreading their gifts among the needy; their righteousness stands for all time, and their strength will rise in honor.
10The wicked see it and are galled; they grind their teeth and melt away; what the wicked long for is lost.
fields.summary: Those who fear God and delight in God’s commands are blessed; they are generous and need not fear bad news.

fields.title: Psalm 113
fields.body_html:
The LORD lifts up the lowly

1Praise the LORD! You who serve the LORD, give praise; give praise to the name of the LORD!
2May the name of the LORD be blessed from now on and for all time.
3From where the sun comes up to where it goes down, the name of the LORD is worthy of praise.
4The LORD is lifted high over every nation; his glory rises above the heavens.
5Who can compare with the LORD our God, who has taken his seat on high,
6who bends low to see what is in the heavens and on the earth?
7He lifts the poor up out of the dust and raises those in need from the ash heap,
8to seat them with nobles, beside the leaders of his people.
9He gives the woman without children a household of her own, a glad mother of children. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The servants of God are called to praise the name of God, who is enthroned on high and lifts up the poor.

fields.title: Psalm 114
fields.body_html:
When Israel came out of Egypt

1When Israel left Egypt, when the house of Jacob left a people whose speech was strange to them,
2Judah became his holy place, Israel the realm he rules.
3The sea looked and ran away; the Jordan turned and flowed back.
4The mountains sprang about like rams, the hills like lambs from the flock.
5What is wrong, sea, that you run away? Jordan, why do you turn back?
6Mountains, why do you spring about like rams, and you hills, like lambs from the flock?
7Earth, shake with fear before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
8who changed the rock into a pool of water, and hard flint into a flowing spring.
fields.summary: When Israel left Egypt, the sea fled and the mountains skipped before God.

fields.title: Psalm 115
fields.body_html:
Not to us, but to your name

1Do not give us the glory, LORD, do not give it to us. Give it to your name, for the sake of your loyal love and your faithfulness.
2Why should the nations be allowed to say, “So where is their God?”
3Yet our God is in the heavens, and whatever he wills, he does.
4Their idols are made of silver and gold, shaped by human hands.
5They have a mouth, yet say nothing; they have eyes, yet see nothing.
6They have ears, yet hear nothing; they have a nose, yet smell nothing.
7They have hands, yet feel nothing; feet, yet never walk; no sound comes from their throats.
8The people who make them will end up like them, and so will everyone who relies on them.
9People of Israel, put your trust in the LORD! He is the one who helps them and shields them.
10House of Aaron, put your trust in the LORD! He is the one who helps them and shields them.
11You who fear the LORD, put your trust in the LORD! He is the one who helps them and shields them.
12The LORD has kept us in mind, and he will bless: he will bless the people of Israel, he will bless the family of Aaron.
13He will bless all who fear the LORD, the least of them and the greatest alike.
14May the LORD make you grow in number, you and your children too.
15You are blessed by the LORD, the one who made the heavens and the earth.
16The heavens are the LORD’s own heavens; the earth he has handed over to humankind.
17The dead do not praise the LORD, nor do any who sink down into the silence.
18As for us, we will bless the LORD now and for all time to come. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: Glory belongs to God’s name, not to us; idols are lifeless, but God blesses those who trust in God.

fields.title: Psalm 116
fields.body_html:
I love the LORD, who heard me

1I love the LORD, for he listens when I call to him and plead for mercy.
2Because he has turned his ear toward me, I will call to him all my days.
3The ropes of death were wound around me, and the anguish of Sheol had caught me; I met with distress and grief.
4So I cried out to the LORD by name: Please, LORD, save my life!
5The LORD shows grace and does what is right; our God is tender and merciful.
6The LORD keeps watch over people with no defense; when I sank down helpless, he rescued me.
7Come back to your rest, my soul, because the LORD has treated you with kindness.
8You have pulled me back from death, kept my eyes from weeping and my feet from tripping.
9I will go about my life in the presence of the LORD, here in the lands of the living.
10I kept my faith even when I said, I am suffering terribly.
11In my panic I said, Every human being is false.
12What return can I make to the LORD for all his kindness to me?
13I will lift high the cup of salvation and call out the name of the LORD.
14What I promised the LORD I will carry out, with all his people looking on.
15The death of his loyal ones weighs heavily in the sight of the LORD.
16Yes, LORD, I belong to you as your servant, a servant born to your servant woman; you have untied the ropes that bound me.
17I will bring you a thank offering and call on the LORD by name.
18What I promised the LORD I will carry out, with all his people looking on,
19in the courts of the LORD’s house, within you, Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The psalmist loves God, who heard his cry when death surrounded him, and he will keep his vows.

fields.title: Psalm 117
fields.body_html:
All nations, praise the LORD

1Praise the LORD, every nation! Sing his praises, all you peoples!
2For his loyal love toward us is overwhelming, and the LORD stays faithful forever. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: All nations are called to praise God, whose loyal love is great.

fields.title: Psalm 118
fields.body_html:
The stone the builders cast aside

1Give the LORD thanks, for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever.
2Let Israel say it now: “His loyal love lasts forever.”
3Let the house of Aaron say it now: “His loyal love lasts forever.”
4Let those who fear the LORD say it now: “His loyal love lasts forever.”
5When I was hemmed in I called to the LORD; the LORD answered me by bringing me out into open space.
6With the LORD for me, I have no fear. What can any human being do to me?
7The LORD is with me as my helper, and I will see the downfall of those who hate me.
8It is better to make the LORD your refuge than to rely on human beings.
9It is better to make the LORD your refuge than to rely on princes.
10All the nations closed in around me; in the name of the LORD I drove them back.
11They closed in around me, yes, they closed in on every side; in the name of the LORD I drove them back.
12They came at me like a swarm of bees, but they burned out like a fire in thornbushes; in the name of the LORD I drove them back.
13You shoved me hard to make me fall, but the LORD came to my help.
14The LORD is my strength and the theme of my song; he has come to my rescue.
15The tents of the righteous ring with glad shouts of rescue: “The right hand of the LORD acts with power!
16The right hand of the LORD is raised in triumph; the right hand of the LORD acts with power!”
17I am not going to die; I will live and tell what the LORD has done.
18The LORD disciplined me hard, yet he did not let death take me.
19Open the gates of righteousness for me, so I may go in and thank the LORD.
20This is the LORD’s gate; those who are righteous may pass through it.
21I thank you that you answered me and became my salvation.
22The stone the builders cast aside is now the stone at the head of the corner.
23This has come from the LORD; we look on it with wonder.
24This is the day on which the LORD has acted; let us celebrate and be glad because of it.
25LORD, we beg you, save us! LORD, we beg you, give us success!
26Blessings on the one who comes in the LORD’s name! Out of the LORD’s house we speak a blessing over you.
27The LORD is God; he has given us light. Tie the festival offering with ropes and bring it right to the altar’s horns.
28You are my God, so I will thank you; I will exalt you, my God.
29Give the LORD thanks, for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever.
fields.summary: The people give thanks to God, whose loyal love lasts forever; the stone the builders cast aside is now the stone at the head of the corner.

fields.title: Psalm 119
fields.body_html:
Your word, my delight and my life

1How blessed are those whose way of life is without fault, who walk by the instruction of the LORD!
2How blessed are those who hold fast to his decrees and seek him with their whole heart.
3They do nothing crooked; they keep to the ways he has shown.
4You have laid down your precepts to be kept with all care.
5If only my life were set firmly on keeping your statutes!
6Then I will not be put to shame, as I keep my eyes on all your commands.
7With an honest heart I will give you thanks, as I come to learn your righteous rulings.
8I will hold to your statutes; do not leave me wholly alone.
9How can the young keep their way of life clean? By taking care to live as your word directs.
10I have searched for you with all my heart; do not let me drift away from your commands.
11Deep in my heart I have kept your word safe, so that I will not sin against you.
12All praise to you, LORD! Teach me your statutes.
13Aloud I tell over every ruling you have spoken.
14Following your decrees gives me as much joy as all the riches in the world.
15I will think deeply about your precepts and keep my eyes on your ways.
16Your statutes are my joy; I will not let your word slip from my mind.
17Treat your servant with kindness, and I will live and hold to your word.
