18Take the veil from my eyes, so that I may see the wonders in your instruction.
19I am only a foreigner living on the earth; do not keep your commands hidden from me.
20I am worn thin by longing for your rulings, every hour.
21You rebuke the proud, the people under a curse who wander away from your commands.
22Lift insult and contempt off me, for I have held to your decrees.
23Even when men in power sit and talk against me, your servant keeps thinking about your statutes.
24Yes, I delight in your decrees; they are the advisers I listen to.
25I lie pressed down in the dust; give me life, as your word has said.
26I laid my life out before you, and you gave me an answer; teach me your statutes.
27Help me grasp the path your precepts mark out, and I will ponder your wonderful deeds.
28I am melting away in sorrow; lift me up as your word has said.
29Keep me far from every false path, and be gracious to me by giving me your instruction.
30The path of faithfulness is the one I have chosen; I have set your rulings in front of me.
31I have held tight to your decrees, LORD; let me not be disgraced.
32I will run along the path of your commands, for you open my heart wide.
33Show me, LORD, the path of your statutes, and I will hold to it to the very end.
34Make me understand, and I will guard your instruction and keep it wholeheartedly.
35Guide me along the track of your commands, for that is where my delight is.
36Bend my heart toward your decrees, not toward greedy profit.
37Turn my eyes from gazing at empty things; keep me alive as I walk in your ways.
38Make good your promise to your servant, so that you will be feared.
39Turn aside the scorn I fear so much, for your rulings are good.
40See how I long for your precepts! Keep me alive in your righteousness.
41Let your loyal love reach me, LORD, and your rescue, as your promise assured me.
42Then I will have a reply for the one who mocks me, because I rely on your word.
43Do not take the word of truth wholly from my mouth, for I have waited in hope for your rulings.
44I will keep your instruction always, for all time to come.
45I will walk where there is room and freedom, because I have searched for your precepts.
46I will talk about your decrees in front of kings and not be put to shame.
47I will find my joy in your commands, because I love them.
48I will raise my hands toward your commands, which I love, and I will ponder your statutes.
49Keep in mind the word you gave your servant; you have made me hope in it.
50Here is my comfort when I am brought low: your promise has kept me alive.
51The proud have heaped scorn on me without limit, yet I have not swerved from your instruction.
52I call to mind your rulings from long ago, LORD, and I find comfort.
53Because of the wicked, who have abandoned your instruction, a hot anger takes hold of me.
54Your statutes have become my songs in every place where I live as a foreigner.
55Through the night I think of your name, LORD, and I hold to your instruction.
56This has been my part in life: I have held to your precepts.
57The LORD is my share in life; I have said that I will hold to your words.
58With my whole heart I have pleaded for your favor; show me kindness, just as your promise said.
59I have thought hard about how I live, and turned my steps back to your decrees.
60Quickly, without waiting, I set myself to keep your commands.
61The wicked have tangled me in their ropes, but I have not forgotten your instruction.
62In the middle of the night I get up to thank you for your righteous rulings.
63I stand with all who fear you, with everyone who holds to your precepts.
64LORD, your loyal love fills all the earth; teach me your statutes.
65LORD, you have treated your servant well, just as your word said.
66Train me in good sense and knowledge, for I rely on your commands.
67Until I was brought low, I kept wandering off; but now I hold to your word.
68You are good, and you bring about good; teach me your statutes.
69The proud have plastered lies all over me, but with my whole heart I hold to your precepts.
70Their hearts are thick and dull as fat, but I delight in your instruction.
71It did me good to be brought low, so that I would learn your statutes.
72The instruction you have spoken is worth more to me than gold and silver by the thousand.
73Your hands made me and shaped me; give me insight, so that I can learn your commands.
74Those who fear you will be glad when they see me, for I have set my hope on your word.
75I know, LORD, that your rulings are just, and that you brought me low because you are faithful.
76Let your loyal love comfort me, I pray, as your promise to your servant said.
77Send your tender mercy to me so that I may live; your instruction is what I delight in.
78Let the proud be disgraced, for they have twisted the truth to harm me; but I will ponder your precepts.
79Let those who fear you come back to me, those who know your decrees.
80Let my heart be whole in keeping your statutes, so that I will not be disgraced.
81I am worn out with longing for your rescue; I have set my hope on your word.
82My eyes grow dim as I watch for your promise; I keep asking when you will comfort me.
83I am like a skin bottle dried and cracked in the smoke, yet your statutes have not slipped my mind.
84How many days does your servant have left? When will you judge those who hunt me down?
85The proud have dug pits to catch me, people who do not live by your instruction.
86All your commands can be trusted; people hunt me down with lies. Help me!
87They came close to finishing me off in the land, yet I have not let go of your precepts.
88Keep me alive in your loyal love, and I will hold to the decree you have spoken.
89LORD, your word lasts forever; it is fixed in place in the heavens.
90Your faithfulness lasts from one generation to the next; you set the earth in its place, and it remains.
91They stand today by your rulings, since all things are your servants.
92Had I not taken delight in your instruction, I would have died in my trouble.
93Never will I forget your precepts, for you have used them to give me life.
94I belong to you; save me, for I have searched out your precepts.
95The wicked lie in wait to destroy me, but I keep my mind on your decrees.
96I have seen that every perfect thing has its limit, but your command reaches wide beyond measure.
97How I love your instruction! I turn it over in my mind all day long.
98Through your commands I grow wiser than my enemies, since they are mine forever.
99I see more deeply than all my teachers, because your decrees fill my thoughts.
100I understand more than the old, because I have kept your precepts.
101I have held my feet back from every wicked road, so that I may keep your word.
102I have not strayed from your rulings, for you yourself have been my teacher.
103How sweet your words taste to me, sweeter than honey on my tongue!
104Through your precepts I gain understanding, so I hate every road built on lies.
105Your word is a lamp to guide my feet and a light for the road I travel.
106I have sworn an oath and I stand by it: I will keep your righteous rulings.
107I am bowed down with trouble; LORD, give me life as your word has said.
108LORD, please accept the praise I freely offer, and teach me your rulings.
109Every day my life hangs in the balance, yet I do not forget your instruction.
110The wicked spread a trap to catch me, yet I have not wandered from your precepts.
111I have received your decrees as my portion for all time; they make my heart glad.
112I have turned my heart to carry out your statutes for all time, to the very end.
113I hate people whose loyalty is divided, but I love your instruction.
114In you I find my hiding place and my shield; my hope is fixed on your word.
115Get away from me, you evildoers! I mean to keep the commands my God has given.
116Hold me up as you have promised, so that I may live; do not let my hope end in shame.
117Hold me fast, and I will be safe; I will keep my eyes on your statutes always.
118You throw aside all who wander from your statutes, for their cunning is an empty lie.
119All the wicked of the earth you throw away like dross; that is why I love your decrees.
120My skin crawls with dread of you, and your rulings fill me with fear.
121I have done what is fair and just; do not give me up to those who oppress me.
122Pledge yourself for your servant’s good; do not let the proud crush me.
123My eyes grow weary as I watch for your salvation and for the righteous promise you made.
124Treat your servant as your loyal love moves you, and teach me your statutes.
125I am your servant; make me understand, so that I come to know your decrees.
126The time has come for the LORD to act, for people have broken your instruction.
127So I love your commands above gold, above the finest gold.
128So I hold all your precepts to be right in everything; I hate every road built on lies.
129Your decrees are full of wonder; that is why I keep them with all my being.
130When your words are opened up, they shed light; they bring understanding to the naive.
131I gasp for breath with my mouth wide open, so deeply do I long for your commands.
132Turn toward me and be gracious, as is your way with those who love your name.
133Keep my steps steady by your word, and let no evil be master over me.
134Set me free when people oppress me, and I will keep your precepts.
135Turn the light of your face toward your servant, and train me in your statutes.
136My eyes pour out streams of water, because people do not keep your instruction.
137LORD, you are just in all you do, and your rulings are straight and true.
138You have laid down your decrees in righteousness and in complete faithfulness.
139My zeal burns me up, for my enemies have forgotten your words.
140Your word has been tried in the fire and found pure, and your servant loves it.
141I am of no account and scorned, yet I have not forgotten your precepts.
142Your righteousness stays right for all time, and your instruction is the truth.
143Trouble and hardship have overtaken me, yet your commands are my joy.
144Your decrees are right for all time; help me understand, so that I may live.
145With my whole heart I call to you; LORD, answer me! I will keep your statutes.
146I cry to you: save me, and I will hold to your decrees.
147Before the light of dawn I am up, crying out for help; my hope is in your word.
148My eyes are open before each watch of the night, so that I may ponder your promise.
149Hear my voice because of your loyal love; LORD, give me life in keeping with your justice.
150Those who chase after wicked schemes are closing in; your instruction is far from their minds.
151But you, LORD, are close at hand, and every one of your commands is truth.
152From your decrees I have known for a long time that you laid their foundations to last forever.
153Look at my suffering and pull me out of it, for I have not forgotten your instruction.
154Take up my cause and set me free; give me life as you have promised.
155The wicked are a long way from being saved, since they never look for your statutes.
156Great is your compassion, LORD; give me life as your rulings direct.
157Many people hunt me and stand against me, yet I have not swerved from your decrees.
158When I see traitors I feel sick, for they have not kept your word.
159Look how much I love your precepts! LORD, give me life because of your loyal love.
160Your word is truth from first to last; each of your righteous rulings stands forever.
161Rulers hunt me down for no reason, but it is your word that makes my heart tremble.
162Your promise makes me glad, as glad as one who carries off rich plunder.
163I hate lies, I detest them, but I love your instruction.
164I praise you seven times every day because your rulings are righteous.
165Those who love your instruction enjoy deep peace, and nothing trips them up.
166LORD, I look in hope for your salvation, and I carry out your commands.
167With all my being I keep your decrees, and I love them deeply.
168I keep your precepts and your decrees, for everything I do lies open before you.
169LORD, let my cry come close to you; give me understanding as your word has said.
170Let my prayer for mercy reach you; rescue me as you have promised.
171Let praise bubble up from my lips, for you teach me your statutes.
172Let my tongue answer with songs about your word, since every command you give is right.
173Reach out your hand to help me, since your precepts are what I have chosen.
174LORD, I yearn for you to save me, and your instruction is my joy.
175Keep me alive to praise you, and let your rulings come to my aid.
176Like a lost sheep I have wandered off; search for your servant, since your commands have not slipped from my mind.
fields.summary: In twenty-two sections, one for each letter of the alphabet, the psalmist delights in God’s instruction, prays to keep it, and finds it a lamp for his feet.

fields.title: Psalm 120
fields.body_html:
Living among people who hate peace

A song of ascents.

1When I was in trouble I cried out to the LORD, and he gave me an answer.
2LORD, rescue me from people whose lips tell lies, whose tongues deceive.
3You deceitful tongue, what will he give you, and what more will he heap on you?
4Sharpened arrows from a fighter’s bow, and hot coals of broom wood!
5How miserable I am, living as a foreigner in Meshech, making my home among the tents of Kedar!
6For far too long I have had to live beside people who hate peace.
7I stand for peace, but when I open my mouth, they choose war.
fields.summary: In trouble among liars and people who hate peace, the psalmist cries out to God.

fields.title: Psalm 121
fields.body_html:
The LORD guards your going and coming

A song of ascents.

1I look up to the mountains.
Where will my help come from?
2My help is from the LORD,
the one who made heaven and earth.
3May he never let your foot stumble;
may the one who guards you never doze.
4Indeed, the one who guards Israel
never dozes off and never sleeps.
5The LORD is the one who guards you;
The LORD is shade at your right side.
6By day the sun will not beat down on you,
and by night the moon will do you no harm.
7The LORD will guard you against every harm;
he will guard your very life.
8The LORD will guard you as you set out and as you return,
from now on and for all time.
fields.summary: The psalmist’s help comes from God, who made heaven and earth and who will guard his going out and coming in.

fields.title: Psalm 122
fields.body_html:
Pray for Jerusalem’s peace

A song of ascents. Of David.

1I was full of joy when they said to me, “Come, let us set out for the house of the LORD!”
2Now here we are, standing inside your gates, Jerusalem!
3Jerusalem, built as a city whose buildings are joined close together,
4where the tribes make their way up, the tribes that belong to the LORD, as was decreed for Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
5For there the seats of justice are placed, the royal thrones of David’s family.
6Pray that Jerusalem will have peace: “May all who love you live at ease.
7Let your walls be at peace and your strongholds be secure.”
8For the sake of my brothers and sisters and my friends I will say, “May peace be inside you!”
9Because the house of the LORD our God is here, I will work for what is good for you.
fields.summary: Pilgrims rejoice to stand in Jerusalem and pray for its peace.

fields.title: Psalm 123
fields.body_html:
Eyes on the LORD, like a servant’s on a master

A song of ascents.

1I raise my eyes to you, the one who reigns in heaven.
2Servants watch the hand of their master, and a servant woman watches the hand of the woman she serves. In the same way we keep our eyes on the LORD our God, waiting for him to show us favor.
3Show us favor, LORD, show us favor, for we have swallowed more contempt than we can bear.
4We have had our fill and more of the mockery of the comfortable and the contempt of the arrogant.
fields.summary: As servants watch their master’s hand, the people look to God for mercy.

fields.title: Psalm 124
fields.body_html:
If the LORD had not been on our side

A song of ascents. Of David.

1Let Israel say it now: if the LORD had not stood with us,
2if the LORD had not stood with us when people rose up against us,
3then they would have devoured us alive in the heat of their anger against us,
4then the floodwaters would have carried us off, a torrent would have rushed over us,
5then the raging waters would have closed over us.
6Blessed be the LORD! He did not give us up to be torn apart by their teeth.
7We have slipped free like a bird from the bird-catchers’ trap; the trap is broken, and we are free!
8We find our help in the name of the LORD, the one who made heaven and earth.
fields.summary: If God had not been on Israel’s side, they would have been swept away; their help is in God’s name.

fields.title: Psalm 125
fields.body_html:
Like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken

A song of ascents.

1Whoever trusts in the LORD is like Mount Zion: nothing can shake it; it stays in place forever.
2Mountains ring Jerusalem all around, and the LORD is all around his people, from now on and forever.
3Wicked rule will not stay in place over the land that belongs to the righteous, or even the righteous might reach out their hands to do wrong.
4LORD, be good to good people, to all whose hearts are upright.
5But as for people who wander off onto crooked paths, the LORD will drive them away with all who do evil. May Israel have peace!
fields.summary: Those who trust God are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken.

fields.title: Psalm 126
fields.body_html:
Bring us back like streams in the Negev

A song of ascents.

1When the LORD turned things around for Zion, we were like people in a dream.
2Then we laughed and laughed, and our tongues rang with joyful shouts. Then people among the nations said, “What great things the LORD has done for them!”
3Great things indeed the LORD has done for us, and how glad we were!
4LORD, restore us again, as the rains bring the dry streams of the Negev back to life.
5People who sow their seed in tears will bring in the harvest with songs of joy.
6People may go out in tears as they carry the seed for sowing, but they will surely come home shouting for joy, their arms full of sheaves.
fields.summary: When God restored Zion’s fortunes the people laughed for joy, and they pray that those who sow in tears will reap with songs of joy.

fields.title: Psalm 127
fields.body_html:
Unless the LORD builds the house

A song of ascents. Of Solomon.

1If the LORD does not build the house, the work of its builders comes to nothing. If the LORD does not guard the city, the watchman’s sleepless night is wasted.
2It does you no good to get up early and stay up late, eating food earned by anxious work; he gives sleep to the one he loves.
3Children are a gift handed down from the LORD; the fruit of the womb is a reward.
4Children born to the young are like arrows in a fighter’s hand.
5How blessed is the one who has a quiver filled with them! They will not be disgraced when they argue with enemies at the city gate.
fields.summary: Unless God builds the house, its builders work in vain; children are a gift from God.

fields.title: Psalm 128
fields.body_html:
The blessing on those who fear the LORD

A song of ascents.

1How blessed is everyone who fears the LORD and lives the way he directs!
2You will enjoy the food your own hands have worked for; how blessed you will be, and how good your life!
3In the heart of your home your wife will be like a vine loaded with grapes, and around your table your children will be like young olive plants.
4See how the one who fears the LORD will be blessed!
5May the LORD send you blessing from Zion, and may you look on Jerusalem’s good fortune as long as you live,
6and may you live long enough to see your grandchildren. May Israel have peace!
fields.summary: Those who fear God are blessed with fruitful work and family.

fields.title: Psalm 129
fields.body_html:
Attacked often, never defeated

A song of ascents.

1Again and again they have attacked me since I was young — let Israel say it now.
2Again and again they have attacked me since I was young, but they have never beaten me.
3They ran their plows over my back and cut long furrows in it.
4The LORD does what is right: he has cut through the ropes of the wicked.
5May everyone who hates Zion be disgraced and driven back.
6May they be like grass growing on a roof, which dries up before it can grow tall,
7too little to fill a reaper’s hand or to make an armful for the one who ties the sheaves,
8and no one passing by calls out, “The LORD’s blessing be on you! We bless you in the name of the LORD!”
fields.summary: Israel’s enemies have attacked since its youth but have not prevailed, and the psalmist prays that they will be put to shame.

fields.title: Psalm 130
fields.body_html:
Out of the depths, waiting for the Lord

A song of ascents.

1From the deep waters I call to you, LORD.
2Lord, listen to me as I call! Turn your ears toward my cry for mercy.
3LORD, if you kept count of every wrong, Lord, who could stand before you?
4But forgiveness is found with you, and so you are held in awe.
5I am waiting for the LORD; with all that I am I wait, and I hope in what he has promised.
6I long for the Lord more than night guards long for the morning, yes, more than night guards for the morning.
7Israel, wait in hope for the LORD! For loyal love is found with the LORD, and with him is redemption in full measure.
8It is he who will redeem Israel from all its wrongs.
fields.summary: From the depths the psalmist cries to God, who forgives, and he waits for God more than watchmen wait for morning.

fields.title: Psalm 131
fields.body_html:
Calm like a weaned child

A song of ascents. Of David.

1LORD, there is no pride in my heart, no arrogance in my eyes. I do not go after things too great for me, or too wonderful for me to grasp.
2Instead, I have made myself calm and quiet, like a child past nursing age resting on its mother; I am calm within, like that child.
3Israel, wait in hope for the LORD, from now on and forever.
fields.summary: The psalmist has calmed and quieted himself like a weaned child, and urges Israel to hope in God.

fields.title: Psalm 132
fields.body_html:
The LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion

A song of ascents.

1LORD, remember David and all the hardship he went through,
2how he made an oath to the LORD and a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob,
3“I will not set foot in my own house or climb into my bed,
4I will not let my eyes sleep or my eyelids close,
5until I have found the LORD a place to stay, a home for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
6Listen! We heard of it in Ephrathah, and came across it in the fields of Jaar.
7Come, we will enter his home and bow down before the footstool under his feet.
8Rise up, LORD! Come to the place where you will rest, you and the ark of your might.
9Let your priests be dressed in righteousness, and let those loyal to you cry out with joy.
10Because of David your servant, do not refuse the king you have anointed.
11The LORD has given David his word on oath, a true word he will never take back: “I will place a child of your own body on your throne.
12If your sons are faithful to my covenant and to the decrees I will teach them, their sons as well will sit on your throne for all time.”
13For the LORD chose Zion; he longed to make it his home.
14“Here is my resting place for all time; I will live here, for this is the place I longed for.
15I will richly bless the city’s food supply; I will give its poor all the bread they need.
16I will dress its priests in salvation, and its faithful people will shout and sing for joy.
17There I will make David’s horn sprout up; I have trimmed a lamp for my anointed king.
18I will dress his enemies in shame, but the crown on his head will gleam.”
fields.summary: The people ask God to remember David, and God swears to keep David’s line on the throne and to dwell in Zion.

fields.title: Psalm 133
fields.body_html:
How good it is to live as one

A song of ascents. Of David.

1See how good it is, how lovely, when brothers and sisters live together in harmony!
2It is like the fine anointing oil on the head that flows down the beard, down Aaron’s beard, and down over the collar of his robes,
3like the dew of Hermon coming down on the hills of Zion. For it is there that the LORD has decreed the blessing, life without end.
fields.summary: How good it is when God’s people live together in unity.

fields.title: Psalm 134
fields.body_html:
Bless the LORD by night

A song of ascents.

1Now bless the LORD, every servant of the LORD who stands night after night in the house of the LORD!
2Raise your hands toward the sanctuary, and bless the LORD!
3From Zion may the LORD, the one who made heaven and earth, bless you.
fields.summary: The servants of God in the house of God are called to bless God at night.

fields.title: Psalm 135
fields.body_html:
Praise the LORD, who chose Israel

1Praise the LORD! Praise the name of the LORD; give him praise, you servants of the LORD,
2who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courtyards of the house of our God.
3Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; make music to his name, for that is a delight.
4For the LORD chose Jacob to be his own, Israel to be his special treasure.
5I am sure of it: the LORD is great, and our Lord stands above all gods.
6Whatever the LORD chooses to do, he does it, in the heavens, on the earth, in the seas and in all the ocean depths.
7He raises the clouds from the far edges of the earth; he makes lightning flash with the rain and brings the wind out of his storehouses.
8He struck down the firstborn of Egypt, of people and of animals alike.
9Into your very heart, Egypt, he sent signs and wonders, against Pharaoh and all his officials.
10He struck down many nations and killed powerful kings,
11Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan,
12and he gave their land away as a heritage, a heritage for his people Israel.
13LORD, your name will last forever; LORD, people will remember you in every generation.
14For the LORD will take up the cause of his people and show pity to his servants.
15The idols of the nations are made of silver and gold, shaped by human hands.
16They have a mouth, yet say nothing; they have eyes, yet see nothing.
17They have ears, yet hear nothing; there is not even breath in their mouths.
18The people who make them will end up like them, and so will everyone who relies on them.
19People of Israel, bless the LORD! Family of Aaron, bless the LORD!
20Family of Levi, bless the LORD! All who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
21May the LORD be blessed from Zion, he who lives in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The people praise God, who chose Jacob, does whatever God pleases and brought Israel out of Egypt; idols are lifeless.

fields.title: Psalm 136
fields.body_html:
His loyal love lasts forever

1Give the LORD thanks, for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever.
2Give thanks to the God of gods, for his loyal love lasts forever.
3Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his loyal love lasts forever.
4To the one who alone does great wonders, for his loyal love lasts forever.
5To the one who made the heavens with skill and wisdom, for his loyal love lasts forever.
6To the one who spread out the land over the waters, for his loyal love lasts forever.
7To the one who made the great lights, for his loyal love lasts forever.
8the sun to rule by day, for his loyal love lasts forever.
9the moon and the stars to rule by night, for his loyal love lasts forever.
10To the one who struck Egypt through their firstborn, for his loyal love lasts forever.
11and he led Israel out from among them, for his loyal love lasts forever.
12with a strong hand and a stretched-out arm, for his loyal love lasts forever.
13To the one who split the Red Sea apart, for his loyal love lasts forever.
14and he brought Israel through the middle of it, for his loyal love lasts forever.
15and he shook Pharaoh and his army off into the Red Sea, for his loyal love lasts forever.
16To the one who guided his people through the wilderness, for his loyal love lasts forever.
17To the one who struck down great kings, for his loyal love lasts forever.
18and he killed powerful kings, for his loyal love lasts forever.
19Sihon king of the Amorites, for his loyal love lasts forever.
20and Og king of Bashan, for his loyal love lasts forever.
21and he gave their land away as a heritage, for his loyal love lasts forever.
22a heritage for Israel his servant, for his loyal love lasts forever.
23who remembered us when we were brought low, for his loyal love lasts forever.
24and he tore us free from our enemies, for his loyal love lasts forever.
25who gives food to every living creature, for his loyal love lasts forever.
26Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his loyal love lasts forever.
fields.summary: Each line of thanks to God for creation and for rescuing Israel answers that God’s loyal love lasts forever.

fields.title: Psalm 137
fields.body_html:
By the rivers of Babylon

1Beside the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down; we wept as we thought of Zion.
2On the poplar trees there we hung up our lyres.
3For there the people who had taken us captive demanded songs from us; those who tormented us wanted us to be cheerful: “Sing for us a song from Zion!”
4How could we sing the LORD’s song in a land of strangers?
5Jerusalem, if I ever forget you, may my right hand forget how to play.
6May my tongue stay stuck to the roof of my mouth should I fail to remember you, should I fail to prize Jerusalem above my chief delight.
7LORD, hold the day of Jerusalem’s fall against the Edomites, who shouted, “Strip it, strip it bare, right down to its foundations!”
8Daughter Babylon, soon to be laid waste, how blessed is the one who pays you back in full for all you did to us!
9How blessed is the one who grabs your little children and smashes them on the rock!
fields.summary: By the rivers of Babylon the exiles weep as they remember Zion and cannot sing God’s song in a foreign land.

fields.title: Psalm 138
fields.body_html:
Thanks for an answered prayer

Of David.

1With all my heart I will give you thanks; in the presence of the gods I will make music for you.
2I will bow down facing your holy temple and praise your name for your loyal love and your faithfulness; for you have made your promise great, beyond all that your name had made known.
3The day I called, you answered me; you filled me with courage and strength within.
4LORD, every king on earth will give you thanks, because they have heard the words you spoke.
5They will sing of the LORD’s ways, because the glory of the LORD is so great.
6The LORD is high, yet he looks upon those who are low; the proud he knows from a distance.
7Even when I walk through the middle of trouble, you keep me alive. You reach out your hand against my enemies’ fury, and your right hand rescues me.
8The LORD will carry out his plan for me. LORD, your loyal love lasts forever; do not let go of what your hands have made.
fields.summary: David gives thanks for God’s loyal love and faithfulness, for God looks on the lowly and will fulfill God’s purpose for him.

fields.title: Psalm 139
fields.body_html:
The LORD knows me through and through

For the music director. Of David. A psalm.

1LORD, you have looked deep into me, and you know me.
2Whether I sit down or get up, you know it;
even from far away you grasp what I am thinking.
3When I travel and when I lie down, you sift through it all;
every path I take is well known to you.
4No word is yet on my tongue,
and already, LORD, you know the whole of it.
5You close me in from behind and from in front;
you have placed your hand on me.
6Knowledge like this is beyond me, too wonderful;
it towers so high that I cannot reach it.
7Where could I go to get away from your Spirit?
Where could I run to escape your presence?
8Should I climb up to the heavens, you are there;
should I lie down in Sheol, there you are as well.
9If I take flight on the wings of the dawn
and go to live beyond the farthest sea,
10there too your hand would be leading me,
and your right hand would take hold of me.
11If I tell myself that the darkness will surely overwhelm me
and the light around me will turn to night,
12even the darkness hides nothing from you;
night shines as bright as day,
and dark and light are the same to you.
13It was you who made the deepest parts of me;
you wove my body together while I was still in my mother’s womb.
14I give you thanks, for the way I was made is awe-inspiring and marvelous.
What you make is wonderful,
and deep within I know it well.
15Not one of my bones was hidden from you
as I was being formed out of sight,
worked like fine embroidery deep within the earth.
16Your eyes saw me while I was still unshaped; in your book they were all written down,
the days that were shaped for me,
each one of them set in place.
17God, how I treasure your thoughts!
How immense their number is!
18Should I try to count them, they would outnumber the sand.
I wake up, and I am with you still.
19God, if only you would put the wicked to death!
Murderers, get away from me,
20those who name you as they plot their wickedness;
your enemies speak your name in falsehood.
21LORD, how could I not hate those who hate you,
or feel disgust for those who rise up against you?
22My hatred for them is total;
they have become my own enemies.
23God, look deep into me and know my heart;
put me to the test and know my restless thoughts.
24Look and see whether I am on a path that brings harm,
and guide me along the road that never ends.
fields.summary: God knows the psalmist completely, is present everywhere and formed him in the womb; he asks God to search him and lead him.

fields.title: Psalm 140
fields.body_html:
Rescue me from violent people

For the music director. A psalm of David.

1LORD, rescue me from evil people; keep me safe from those who do violence,
2who scheme harm in their hearts and keep starting battles day after day.
3They whet their tongues like a serpent; viper’s venom lies hidden behind their lips. Selah
4LORD, guard me from the clutches of the wicked; shield me from violent people who are scheming to make me fall.
5Arrogant people have hidden a trap for me; they have stretched out ropes as a net beside the path and laid snares to catch me. Selah
6I have told the LORD, “You are my God.” Turn your ear, LORD, to the sound of my pleading.
7Lord GOD, mighty one who saves me, you have covered my head on the day the weapons clash.
8LORD, do not give the wicked what they crave; do not let their scheme succeed, or they will grow proud. Selah
9As for those who close in around me, may the harm their own lips speak come down over their heads.
10Let burning coals rain down on them; may they be hurled into fire, into deep pits, never to get up again.
11Let no slanderer find a firm place in the land; let disaster hunt down the violent and strike them again and again.
12I know that the LORD will take up the case of the oppressed and see that the needy get justice.
13The righteous will surely give thanks to your name, and people of integrity will make their home before you.
fields.summary: David asks God to rescue him from violent and slanderous people.

fields.title: Psalm 141
fields.body_html:
A guard over my mouth

A psalm of David.

1LORD, I am calling to you; come to me quickly. Hear my voice as I cry out to you.
2Let my prayer stand before you like incense, my lifted hands like the offering at evening.
3LORD, station a guard at my mouth; keep a sentry at the doorway of my lips.
4Keep my heart from leaning toward anything evil, from joining with wrongdoers in their wicked acts; let me not share their rich food.
5Let a righteous person strike me: that is loyal love. Let them reprove me: that is oil for my head, and may my head never refuse it. But all the while I pray against the evil they do.
6When their rulers are flung down the face of the cliff, people will hear my words and know that they were kind.
7Like clods when the ground is plowed and broken open, our bones lie scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
8But my eyes look to you, Lord GOD; I make you my refuge. Do not let my life be poured out.
9Guard me from the grip of the trap they have set for me, from the snares of those who do wrong.
10May the wicked be caught together in their own nets, while I make my way past.
fields.summary: David asks God to keep watch over his mouth and to keep him from the snares of the wicked.

fields.title: Psalm 142
fields.body_html:
A prayer from the cave

A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.

1I call out loud to the LORD; I raise my voice to the LORD, pleading for mercy.
2I spill out my complaint in front of him; I tell him all about my distress.
3When my spirit is fading within me, you are the one who knows my path. Along the road I travel they have hidden a trap for me.
4Look to my right and see: there is no one who knows me. Every way of escape is gone; nobody looks out for me.
5I cry out to you, LORD. I say, “You are my shelter, all I have in the land of the living.”
6Pay heed to my cry, because I am in the depths. Rescue me from those who hunt me, since they are stronger than I am.
7Lead me out of this prison, so that I may thank your name. Then the righteous will crowd around me, because you will treat me with goodness.
fields.summary: In the cave David cries out to God, for no one cares for him, and God is his refuge.

fields.title: Psalm 143
fields.body_html:
Do not bring your servant to trial

A psalm of David.

1LORD, hear my prayer; listen as I plead for mercy. Answer me in your faithfulness and in your righteousness.
2Do not bring your servant to trial, for no living person can be found in the right before you.
3The enemy has hunted me down and ground my life into the dust; he has left me to live in dark places, like people dead for ages.
4My spirit sinks within me, and my heart is stunned inside me.
5I recall the days long past; I think over all that you have done and reflect on what your hands have made.
6I hold out my hands to you; my whole being waits for you like ground worn out by drought. Selah
7LORD, hurry and answer me; my spirit is failing. Do not keep your face hidden from me, or I will become one of those who sink into the pit.
8Each morning let me hear of your loyal love, since you are the one I rely on. Teach me which road to walk, for my whole being reaches up to you.
9Snatch me from my enemies, LORD; I have taken cover with you.
10Teach me to do what pleases you, since you are my God. May your Spirit, who is good, guide me across even ground.
11LORD, for the honor of your name, keep me alive; in your righteousness lead me out of my distress.
12In your loyal love you will put an end to my enemies and wipe out all who attack my life, for I am your servant.
fields.summary: David pleads for mercy, for no one living is righteous before God, and asks God to teach him to do God’s will.

fields.title: Psalm 144
fields.body_html:
A prayer for the king’s victory

Of David.

1Blessed be the LORD, my rock, the one who teaches my hands to fight and my fingers to make war.
2He is my loyal love and my stronghold, my tower on the heights and the one who sets me free, my shield, the one I shelter in, who brings my people under my rule.
3LORD, what are human beings, that you take notice of them, mere mortals, that you give them a thought?
4Human beings are like a breath; their days are a shadow sliding by.
5LORD, bow your heavens low and come down; touch the mountains and make them pour out smoke.
6Make the lightning flash and scatter the enemy; let your arrows fly and throw them into confusion.
7Reach out your hands from on high; free me and pull me out of deep waters, out of the grip of foreigners,
8who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.
9God, I will sing you a new song; I will play music for you on the ten-stringed harp,
10the one who gives victory to kings, who snatches his servant David away from the cruel sword.
11Free me and pull me out of the grip of foreigners, who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.
12Then may our sons be like saplings grown tall while they are still young, and our daughters like corner columns carved for a royal house,
13our storehouses full, supplying every kind of food, our flocks multiplying into the thousands, tens of thousands across our pastures,
14our cattle heavy with young. May there be no breach in our walls, no going out into exile, no cry of distress in our streets.
15How blessed the people who live like this! How blessed the people who have the LORD as their God!
fields.summary: David blesses God, his rock, who trains him for battle, and prays for a blessed and prosperous people.

fields.title: Psalm 145
fields.body_html:
My God the King, forever praised

A song of praise. Of David.

1My God, the King, I will lift you high in praise and bless your name for ever and ever.
2Day after day I will bless you and give praise to your name for ever and ever.
3The LORD is great, worthy of the highest praise, and there is no searching out the depth of his greatness.
4Each generation will praise your works to the one after it and announce your mighty acts.
5I will reflect on your majesty, its glory and splendor, and on the story of your wonders.
6People will speak of the power of your fearsome deeds, and I will tell of your greatness.
7They will spill over with the memory of your great goodness and sing out for joy at your righteousness.
8The LORD is full of grace and compassion, slow to anger and great in loyal love.
9The LORD is good to everyone; his compassion covers all that he has made.
10LORD, all your works will thank you, and your faithful people will bless you.
11They will speak of your glorious reign and tell of your power,
12to make his mighty acts known to all people, and the glorious splendor of his reign.
13Your kingdom is a kingdom for all the ages, and your rule lasts through every generation.
14The LORD holds up everyone who stumbles and raises all who are bent low.
15All eyes are turned to you in hope, and you provide their food when it is needed.
16You open your hand and give every living creature what it longs for.
17In all his ways the LORD is righteous; in all his deeds he is faithful.
18The LORD is close to everyone who calls to him, to all who call to him sincerely.
19He grants what those who fear him desire; he hears their cry for help and rescues them.
20The LORD guards everyone who loves him, but he will wipe out all the wicked.
21With my own mouth I will speak praise to the LORD; may all creatures bless his holy name for all time to come.
fields.summary: David praises God, the King, who is gracious and merciful, near to all who call, and whose kingdom lasts forever.

fields.title: Psalm 146
fields.body_html:
Trust the God of Jacob, not rulers

1Praise the LORD! My soul, praise the LORD!
2All my life I will praise the LORD; as long as I exist I will make music for my God.
3Do not rely on rulers, on mere mortals, who have no power to rescue.
4Their breath leaves them and they go back to the soil they came from; that same day all they had planned is gone.
5How blessed are those who have the God of Jacob to help them, whose hope rests on the LORD their God!
6who made heaven and earth and the sea with all they contain, who remains true forever,
7who brings justice to the oppressed and provides bread for the hungry. The LORD releases the prisoners;
8The LORD makes the blind see; the LORD raises up those bent low; the LORD loves people who are righteous;
9The LORD protects the foreigners living in the land; he upholds the orphan and the widow, but he overturns the way of the wicked.
10The LORD will rule as King forever; Zion, your God will reign from one generation to the next. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The psalmist will praise God all his life, for God, not princes, made heaven and earth and gives justice to the oppressed.

fields.title: Psalm 147
fields.body_html:
The LORD who counts stars and heals

1Praise the LORD! It is good to make music for our God; it is a delight, and praise is fitting.
2The LORD is rebuilding Jerusalem; he is bringing together Israel’s scattered exiles.
3He heals those whose hearts are crushed and bandages their injuries.
4He decides how many stars there are and gives each one its name.
5Our Lord is great and mighty in power; there is no measuring his understanding.
6The LORD lifts up the lowly and throws the wicked down to the earth.
7Sing out to the LORD with thanks; make music for our God on the lyre,
8who wraps the sky in clouds, who gets rain ready for the land, who makes grass sprout on the mountains,
9who gives the beasts their food and feeds the raven’s chicks when they call.
10It is not the power of the horse that delights him, nor a soldier’s strong legs that please him.
11What pleases the LORD is people who revere him and look with hope to his loyal love.
12Jerusalem, glorify the LORD! Zion, praise your God!
13For he has made the bars of your gates strong and has blessed your children inside your walls.
14He keeps your frontiers at peace and satisfies you with the richest wheat.
15He issues his orders to the earth, and his word goes out at a run.
16He sends snow that lies like wool and strews frost like ash.
17He flings down his ice in pieces like crumbs; who can hold out against his cold?
18He sends his word, and the ice thaws; he sets his wind blowing, and the waters run.
19He makes his words known to Jacob, his statutes and his rulings to Israel.
20No other nation has he treated this way; his rulings are unknown to them. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: God rebuilds Jerusalem, heals the brokenhearted, counts the stars and sends the snow, and delights in those who fear God.

fields.title: Psalm 148
fields.body_html:
All creation, praise the LORD

1Praise the LORD! Let the heavens praise the LORD; let the heights above give him praise!
2Praise him, all his angels! All the armies of heaven, praise him!
3Sun and moon, praise him! All shining stars, praise him!
4Praise him, heaven of heavens, along with the waters up above the sky!
5May they praise the name of the LORD; at his command they came into being.
6He fixed them in their places for ever and always; he made a law for them that will not pass away.
7From the earth below, praise the LORD, sea monsters and all the watery deeps,
8fire and hail, snow and fog, gales of wind that do what he says,
9the mountains and all the hills, trees that bear fruit and all the cedars,
10wild beasts and all cattle, creatures that crawl and birds that fly,
11earthly kings and all peoples, nobles and all the earth’s rulers,
12young men and young women alike, the old together with the young!
13Let them all bring praise to the name of the LORD, since his name alone is lifted high; his splendor towers over earth and sky.
14For his own people he has raised up a horn, a source of praise for all his faithful, the Israelites, a people near to him. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The heavens, the earth and all creatures are called to praise God.

fields.title: Psalm 149
fields.body_html:
A new song for the faithful

1Praise the LORD! Sing a new song to the LORD; sing his praise where the faithful gather!
2Let Israel be glad in the one who made it; let Zion’s people rejoice in their King.
3Let them praise his name in dance and make music for him on tambourine and lyre.
4For the LORD is pleased with his people; he dresses the humble in the beauty of salvation.
5Let the faithful be jubilant in their glory; let them cry out with joy as they lie on their beds.
6with songs that lift God high in their throats and a two-edged sword held in their hands,
7to bring retribution on the nations and to punish the peoples,
8to put their kings in chains and their nobles in iron shackles,
9to carry out on them the judgment already written. This honor belongs to all his faithful. Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: The faithful are called to sing a new song and to praise God with dancing, for God delights in the people.

fields.title: Psalm 150
fields.body_html:
Everything that breathes, praise him

1Praise the LORD! Praise God in his holy place; praise him in the great expanse of his power!
2Praise him for the mighty things he has done; praise him as fits his boundless greatness!
3Praise him with the ram’s horn blast; praise him with harp and lyre!
4Praise him with hand drum and dance; praise him on strings and pipes!
5Praise him with clear-sounding cymbals; praise him with cymbals that ring out like a shout!
6Let every creature that breathes praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!
fields.summary: Everything that has breath is called to praise God with trumpet, harp, strings and cymbals.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
Praise the LORD! Praise God in his holy place; praise him in the great expanse of his power!

— Psalm 150:1

The Psalms begin with a single person on a path, delighting in God’s instruction. They end with everything that breathes, praising. In between lies the whole of human life: enemies and exile, sin and forgiveness, sickness and long nights, festivals and harvests, kings who rose and kings who fell. The book has never once looked away from trouble. And yet it ends here.

Psalm 150 is the shortest possible summary of everything the Psalter has learned. It gives no new reason for praise; the hundred and forty-nine psalms before it have given them all. It says only where God is to be praised (in his holy place, and in the great expanse of his power), why (“for the mighty things he has done”), how (with the ram’s horn, harp and lyre, hand drum and dance, strings and pipes, and cymbals that ring out like a shout) and who. The answer to that last question is the book’s last line, and it leaves no one out.

Where the Psalms point

The ending is not a mood. The psalmists who wrote “How long, LORD?” did not stop meaning it when they wrote “Praise the LORD!” The book ends in praise because it believes that is where history ends: with the LORD as King over all the earth, the nations gathered to him, and his loyal love proved true. Again and again the Psalms look forward to that day, and their hope was larger than anything Israel had yet seen.

Christians read that hope as fulfilled in Jesus. He is the blessed one of Psalm 1 who delighted in God’s law, and the son of Psalm 2 whom the nations raged against. He prayed Psalm 22 on the cross, and its second half, the praise in the great assembly and the ends of the earth turning to the LORD, began to come true when he rose. He is the lord of Psalm 110, seated at God’s right hand; the shepherd of Psalm 23, who said, “I am the good shepherd”; the stone the builders cast aside. And the church has never stopped singing the Psalms, from the first Christians who were urged to speak to one another in “psalms, hymns and Spirit-given songs” to every congregation and every lonely reader who has prayed them since.

So the call of Psalm 150 is not only to the choirs of the temple. It reaches the reader of this book, wherever the Psalms have found you: in a lament, in a confession, on a pilgrimage, or already singing.

Where to go from here

Preachers and writers have lived in the Psalms for as long as there has been a church, and many of the best of them are in this library. A few places to begin:

  • On the shepherd psalm (Psalm 23). Alexander Maclaren’s The Shepherd King of Israel reads it as the old king David looking back on his shepherd years; Hudson Taylor’s Blessed Adversity takes up its last verse.
  • On the two paths (Psalm 1). Hudson Taylor’s Blessed Prosperity.
  • On longing and lament. Maclaren’s Thirsting for God (Psalm 42), Spurgeon’s Waiting Only Upon God (Psalm 62) and Elisabeth Elliot’s I Keep a Quiet Heart (Psalm 131).
  • On God our refuge (Psalms 46 and 91). A. W. Tozer’s God Is Our Refuge and Strength, and Maclaren’s The City and River of God and The Sheltering Wing.
  • On pilgrimage (Psalms 84 and 121). Elisabeth Elliot’s Hearts Set on Pilgrimage, A. B. Simpson’s From Strength to Strength and Maclaren’s Looking to the Hills.
  • On the cross (Psalms 22 and 31). Maclaren’s Into Thy Hands and Robert Murray M’Cheyne’s The Spirit Committed to God, both on the prayer Jesus prayed as he died; Justin Martyr’s Dialogue with Trypho, for how the earliest Christians read Psalm 22 and Psalm 110.
  • On praise. Maclaren’s The Satisfier of All Desires (Psalm 145), and on Psalm 147, Spurgeon’s Healing for the Wounded and Tozer’s The Infinite God.
  • On praying and singing the Psalms. William Law’s A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life, with its chapter on chanting psalms in private devotion; Andrew Murray’s The Inner Chamber, on Psalm 119; Hannah Whitall Smith’s The Christian’s Secret of a Happy Life, on Psalm 139; and The Prayers Jesus Learned, an Ochorus Original on the prayers of the Old Testament, David’s psalms among them.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to the Psalms in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, psalm by psalm, what the great writers of the church have said about each one.

But the best next step may simply be to keep reading the Psalms, one a day or five, and to pray them as you go. They were never meant to be finished. Readers who have prayed them all their lives say they understand them better each time, because each time they bring more of their own life to them. The book is waiting for you to add your voice to its last line:

Let every creature that breathes praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!

— Psalm 150:6
